序言

序言这里是一九三〇年与三一年两年间的杂文的结集。
Here is a collection of essays from 1930 and 31.当三〇年的时候，期刊已渐渐的少见，有些是不能按期出版了，大约是受了逐日加紧的压迫。《语丝》和《奔流》，则常遭邮局的扣留，地方的禁止，到底也还是敷延不下去。那时我能投稿的，就只剩了一个《萌芽》，而出到五期，也被禁止了，接着是出了一本《新地》。所以在这一年内，我只做了收在集内的不到十篇的短评。
In the past 30 years, journals have gradually become rare, and some of them cannot be published on schedule, probably due to increasing oppression day by day. "Yusi" and "Torrent" are often detained by the post office, and the local prohibition still cannot be extended in the end. At that time, there was only one "Sprout" left to submit, and it was also banned in the fifth issue, followed by a book "New Land". So during this year, I only made less than ten short reviews included in the collection.此外还曾经在学校里演讲过两三回，那时无人记录，讲了些什么，此刻连自己也记不清楚了。只记得在有一个大学里演讲的题目，是《象牙塔和蜗牛庐》。大意是说，象牙塔里的文艺，将来决不会出现于中国，因为环境并不相同，这里是连摆这“象牙之塔”的处所也已经没有了；不久可以出现的，恐怕至多只有几个“蜗牛庐”。蜗牛庐者，是三国时所谓“隐逸”的焦先曾经居住的那样的草窠，大约和现在江北穷人手搭的草棚相仿，不过还要小，光光的伏在那里面，少出，少动，无衣，无食，无言。因为那时是军阀混战，任意杀掠的时候，心里不以为然的人，只有这样才可以苟延他的残喘。但蜗牛界里那里会有文艺呢，所以这样下去，中国的没有文艺，是一定的。这样的话，真可谓已经大有蜗牛气味的了，不料不久就有一位勇敢的青年在政府机关的上海《民国日报》上给我批评，说我的那些话使他非常看不起，因为我没有敢讲共产党的话的勇气。谨案在“清党”以后的党国里，讲共产主义是算犯大罪的，捕杀的网罗，张遍了全中国，而不讲，却又为党国的忠勇青年所鄙视。这实在只好变了真的蜗牛，才有“庶几得免于罪戾”的幸福了。
In addition, I once gave two or three speeches in school, but no one recorded what I said, and I can't even remember what I said at the moment. I only remember the title of a speech in a university, which was "Ivory Tower and Snail House". The gist is that the literature and art in the ivory tower will never appear in China in the future, because the environment is different, and there is no place to place this "ivory tower" here; I am afraid that there will be only a few "snail huts" that can appear soon. The snail hut is the grass nest where the so-called "reclusive" Jiao Xian once lived during the Three Kingdoms, which is about the same as the grass hut built by the poor in Jiangbei now, but it is smaller, and the light lies on it, less out, less movement, no clothes, no food, and no words. Because it was a time when the warlords were fighting and killing and plundering at will, the people who didn't think it was the only way to survive his breathing. But there will be literature and art in the snail world, so if this continues, there will be no literature and art in China, which is certain. Unexpectedly, a brave young man criticized me in the Shanghai "Republic of China Daily" of the government agency, saying that his words made him look down on me very much, because I did not have the courage to speak the words of the Communist Party. In the party and state after the "purge of the party", talking about communism is considered a great crime, and the snare of hunting and killing has spread throughout China, but it is despised by the loyal and brave youth of the party and the state. This really has to become a real snail in order to have the happiness of "almost being exempted from sin".而这时左翼作家拿着苏联的卢布之说，在所谓“大报”和小报上，一面又纷纷的宣传起来，新月社的批评家也从旁很卖了些力气。有些报纸，还拾了先前的创造社派的几个人的投稿于小报上的话，讥笑我为“投降”，有一种报则载起《文坛贰臣传》来，第一个就是我，——但后来好像并不再做下去了。
At this time, left-wing writers took the Soviet ruble theory and promoted it in the so-called "broadsheets" and tabloids, and the critics of the Crescent Society also sold some strength from the side. Some newspapers also picked up the words of several people who had previously created the Society in the tabloids, ridiculing me for "surrendering", and one newspaper carried the "Biography of the Second Minister of the Literary World", the first one was me,—— but then it seemed that it was no longer done.卢布之谣，我是听惯了的。大约六七年前，《语丝》在北京说了几句涉及陈源教授和别的“正人君子”们的话的时候，上海的《晶报》上就发表过“现代评论社主角”唐有壬先生的信札，说是我们的言动，都由于墨斯科的命令。这又正是祖传的老谱，宋末有所谓“通虏”，清初又有所谓“通海”，向来就用了这类的口实，害过许多人们的。所以含血喷人，已成了中国士君子的常经，实在不单是他们的识见，只能够见到世上一切都靠金钱的势力。至于“贰臣”之说，却是很有些意思的，我试一反省，觉得对于时事，即使未尝动笔，有时也不免于腹诽，“臣罪当诛兮天皇圣明”，腹诽就决不是忠臣的行径。但御用文学家的给了我这个徽号，也可见他们的“文坛”上是有皇帝的了。
I am used to hearing the ballad of the ruble. About six or seven years ago, when "Yusi" said a few words involving Professor Chen Yuan and other "upright gentlemen" in Beijing, Shanghai's "Jingbao" published a letter from Mr. Tang Youren, the "protagonist of the Modern Review Society", saying that our words and actions were all due to Musco's orders. This is the ancestral genealogy, there was the so-called "Tonglu" at the end of the Song Dynasty, and the so-called "Tonghai" in the early Qing Dynasty, which has always used this kind of excuse and harmed many people. Therefore, spraying people with blood has become a common scripture for Chinese gentlemen, not only their knowledge, but also the power of money that everything in the world can see. As for the saying of "second minister", it is very interesting, I try to reflect on it, and I feel that for current affairs, even if I have not written about it, sometimes it is inevitable to slander, "the sin of the minister should be punished by the emperor's wisdom", and slander is by no means the act of a loyal minister. But the imperial writers gave me this badge, which also shows that there are emperors in their "literary world".去年偶然看见了几篇梅林格（Franz Mehring）的论文，大意说，在坏了下去的旧社会里，倘有人怀一点不同的意见，有一点携贰的心思，是一定要大吃其苦的。而攻击陷害得最凶的，则是这人的同阶级的人物。他们以为这是最可恶的叛逆，比异阶级的奴隶造反还可恶，所以一定要除掉他。我才知道中外古今，无不如此，真是读书可以养气，竟没有先前那样“不满于现状”了，并且仿《三闲集》之例而变其意，拾来做了这一本书的名目。然而这并非在证明我是无产者。一阶级里，临末也常常会自己互相闹起来的，就是《诗经》里说过的那“兄弟阋于墙”，——但后来却未必“外御其侮”。例如同是军阀，就总在整年的大家相打，难道有一面是无产阶级么？而且我时时说些自己的事情，怎样地在“碰壁”，怎样地在做蜗牛，好像全世界的苦恼，萃于一身，在替大众受罪似的：也正是中产的智识阶级分子的坏脾气。只是原先是憎恶这熟识的本阶级，毫不可惜它的溃灭，后来又由于事实的教训，以为惟新兴的无产者才有将来，却是的确的。
Last year, I happened to see a few papers by Franz Mehring, to the effect that in the old society that was broken, if someone had a little different opinion or a little distraction, they would have to suffer a lot. And the one who attacked and framed the most was the person of the same class as this person. They thought this was the most hateful rebellion, even more hateful than the rebellion of slaves of different classes, so they must get rid of him. I just knew that ancient and modern times at home and abroad, all of them are like this, it is really reading can nourish qi, and I am not as "dissatisfied with the status quo" as before, and I changed my mind by imitating the example of "Sanxian Collection", and picked up the name of this book. However, this does not prove that I am a proletarian. In the first class, at the end of the day, they often quarrel with each other, which is the "brothers quarrel against the wall" mentioned in the "Book of Songs",—— but later they may not be "insulted by the outside". For example, if you are a warlord, you always fight each other all year round, is there a side of the proletariat? And I always talk about my own things, how I am "hitting a wall" and how I am being a snail, as if the suffering of the whole world is converging and suffering for the masses: it is also the bad temper of the intellectual class members of the middle class. It is only that at first it was a hatred of this familiar class, and it was not a pity for its collapse, and later, because of the lessons of facts, it was thought that only the emerging proletariat had a future, but it was true.自从一九三一年二月起，我写了较上年更多的文章，但因为揭载的刊物有些不同，文字必得和它们相称，就很少做《热风》那样简短的东西了；而且看看对于我的批评文字，得了一种经验，好像评论做得太简括，是极容易招得无意的误解，或有意的曲解似的。又，此后也不想再编《坟》那样的论文集，和《壁下译丛》那样的译文集，这回就连较长的东西也收在这里面，译文则选了一篇《现代电影与有产阶级》附在末尾，因为电影之在中国，虽然早已风行，但这样扼要的论文却还少见，留心世事的人们，实在很有一读的必要的。还有通信，如果只有一面，读者也往往很不容易了然，所以将紧要一点的几封来信，也擅自一并编进去了。
Since February 1931, I have written more articles than the previous year, but because the publications published are somewhat different, the text must be commensurate with them, and I rarely do something as short as "Hot Wind"; And looking at my criticism, I have gained an experience that it seems that comments are too concise, and it is very easy to attract unintentional misunderstandings or intentional misinterpretations. In addition, I did not want to compile a collection of essays like "Grave" or a collection of translations like "Under the Wall", this time even the longer ones were included in it, and the translation text was selected as "Modern Cinema and the Proletariat" at the end, because although films have long been popular in China, such concise papers are still rare, and people who pay attention to world affairs are really necessary to read. There is also correspondence, if there is only one side, it is often not easy for readers to understand, so several more important letters are also compiled together without authorization.一九三二年四月三十日之夜，编讫并记。
On the night of April 30, 1932, it was compiled and recorded.

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

"Hard Translation" and "Class Nature of Literature"一
One听说《新月》月刊团体里的人们在说，现在销路好起来了。这大概是真的，以我似的交际极少的人，也在两个年青朋友的手里见过第二卷第六七号的合本。顺便一翻，是争“言论自由”的文字和小说居多。近尾巴处，则有梁实秋先生的一篇《论鲁迅先生的“硬译”》，以为“近于死译”。而“死译之风也断不可长”，就引了我的三段译文，以及在《文艺与批评》的后记里所说：“但因为译者的能力不够，和中国文本来的缺点，译完一看，晦涩，甚而至于难解之处也真多；倘将仂句拆下来呢，又失了原来的语气。在我，是除了还是这样的硬译之外，只有束手这一条路了，所余的惟一的希望，只在读者还肯硬着头皮看下去而已”这些话，细心地在字旁加上圆圈，还在“硬译”两字旁边加上套圈，于是“严正”地下了“批评”道：“我们‘硬着头皮看下去’了，但是无所得。‘硬译’和‘死译’有什么分别呢？”
I heard people in the "Crescent" monthly group saying that sales are getting better now. This is probably true, people like me who have very little communication have also seen the combined copy of Volume 2, No. 6 and No. 7 in the hands of two young friends. By the way, most of the texts and novels are about "freedom of speech". Near the tail, there is a piece by Mr. Liang Shiqiu "On Mr. Lu Xun's "Hard Translation"", which is considered "close to dead translation". And "the wind of dead translation must not last", quoted my three translations, and said in the afterword of "Literature and Art and Criticism": "But because of the translator's insufficient ability and the shortcomings of the Chinese text, there are many obscure and even difficult to understand after the translation; If the sentence is removed, it will lose its original tone. For me, in addition to such a hard translation, there is only one way to tie up, and the only hope left is that the reader is willing to bite the bullet and read it", carefully adding a circle next to the word, and adding a ferrule next to the word "hard translation", so "solemnly" underwent "criticism": "We 'bite the bullet and look at it', but we got nothing." What is the difference between 'hard translation' and 'dead translation'? ”新月社的声明中，虽说并无什么组织，在论文里，也似乎痛恶无产阶级式的“组织”，“集团”这些话，但其实是有组织的，至少，关于政治的论文，这一本里都互相“照应”；关于文艺，则这一篇是登在上面的同一批评家所作的《文学是有阶级性的吗？》的余波。在那一篇里有一段说：“……但是不幸得很，没有一本这类的书能被我看懂。……最使我感得困难的是文字，……简直读起来比天书还难。……现在还没有一个中国人，用中国人所能看得懂的文字，写一篇文章告诉我们无产文学的理论究竟是怎么一回事。”字旁也有圆圈，怕排印麻烦，恕不照画了。总之，梁先生自认是一切中国人的代表，这些书既为自己所不懂，也就是为一切中国人所不懂，应该在中国断绝其生命，于是出示曰“此风断不可长”云。
In the statement of the Crescent Society, although there is no organization, in the paper, it seems to hate the words "organization" and "group" of the proletariat, but in fact it is organized, at least, the papers on politics are "caring" each other; Regarding literature and art, this article is the same critic who posted above, "Is Literature Class-Oriented?" The aftermath of ". In that passage there is a passage that says: "...... But unfortunately, there is no book of this kind that I can understand. …… What makes me most difficult is the words,...... It's even harder to read than a heavenly book. …… There is not a Chinese person who writes an article in a text that the Chinese can understand to tell us what the theory of proletarian literature is all about. There is also a circle next to the word, for fear of trouble in typesetting, I will not follow the picture. In short, Mr. Liang considers himself to be the representative of all Chinese, and these books are not understood by himself, that is, they are not understood by all Chinese, and their lives should be cut off in China, so he showed them and said, "This wind must not last".别的“天书”译著者的意见我不能代表，从我个人来看，则事情是不会这样简单的。第一，梁先生自以为“硬着头皮看下去”了，但究竟硬了没有，是否能够，还是一个问题。以硬自居了，而实则其软如棉，正是新月社的一种特色。第二，梁先生虽自来代表一切中国人了，但究竟是否全国中的最优秀者，也是一个问题。这问题从《文学是有阶级性的吗？》这篇文章里，便可以解释。Proletary这字不必译音，大可译义，是有理可说的。但这位批评家却道：“其实翻翻字典，这个字的涵义并不见得体面，据《韦白斯特大字典》，Proletary的意思就是：A citizen of the lowest class who served the state not with property，but only by having children。……普罗列塔利亚是国家里只会生孩子的阶级！（至少在罗马时代是如此）”其实正无须来争这“体面”，大约略有常识者，总不至于以现在为罗马时代，将现在的无产者都看作罗马人的。这正如将Chemie译作“舍密学”，读者必不和埃及的“炼金术”混同，对于“梁”先生所作的文章，也决不会去考查语源，误解为“独木小桥”竟会动笔一样。连“翻翻字典”（《韦白斯特大字典》！）也还是“无所得”，一切中国人未必全是如此的罢。
I cannot represent the opinions of other translators of the "Book of Heaven", but from my personal point of view, things will not be so simple. First, Mr. Liang thinks he has "bitten the bullet and watched it", but whether it is hard and whether it can be is still a question. It is a characteristic of the Crescent Society. Second, although Mr. Liang has always represented all Chinese, whether he is the best in the country is also a question. This question begins with "Is literature class-oriented?" In this article, it can be explained. The word Proletary does not need to be translated, it can be translated, and it is reasonable. But the critic said: "In fact, if you look at the dictionary, the meaning of this word is not necessarily decent, according to the Webster Dictionary, Proletary means: A citizen of the lowest class who served the state not with property, but only by having children." …… Proletaria is the class in the country that only gives birth to children! (at least in Roman times) "In fact, there is no need to fight for this "decency", and those with a little common sense will not regard the present as the Roman era and regard the present proletariat as Romans. This is just like translating Chemie as "esotericism", readers will not confuse it with Egyptian "alchemy", and will never examine the etymology of the article written by Mr. "Liang", misunderstanding that "single-log bridge" will actually start writing. Even "flipping through the dictionary" ("Webster's Great Dictionary"!) It is still "nothing", and all Chinese people may not be like this.

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

二

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

Two但于我最觉得有兴味的，是上节所引的梁先生的文字里，有两处都用着一个“我们”，颇有些“多数”和“集团”气味了。自然，作者虽然单独执笔，气类则决不只一人，用“我们”来说话，是不错的，也令人看起来较有力量，又不至于一人双肩负责。然而，当“思想不能统一”时，“言论应该自由”时，正如梁先生的批评资本制度一般，也有一种“弊病”。就是，既有“我们”便有我们以外的“他们”，于是新月社的“我们”虽以为我的“死译之风断不可长”了，却另有读了并不“无所得”的读者存在，而我的“硬译”，就还在“他们”之间生存，和“死译”还有一些区别。
But what I find most interesting is that in Mr. Liang's text quoted in the previous section, there is a "we" used in two places, which is quite a bit of "majority" and "group" smell. Naturally, although the author writes alone, there is no one person, and it is good to use "we" to speak, and it also makes people look more powerful, and it is not so much that one person is responsible for both shoulders. However, when "ideas cannot be unified" and "speech should be free", just as Mr. Liang criticizes the capital system, there is also a "shortcoming". That is, there are "us" and "them" other than us, so although the "we" of the Crescent Society think that my "wind of dead translation will never last", there are other readers who read it and do not "gain nothing", and my "hard translation" still survives among "them", and there are still some differences from "dead translation".我也就是新月社的“他们”之一，因为我的译作和梁先生所需的条件，是全都不一样的。
I am also one of the "them" of the Crescent Society, because my translation is completely different from Mr. Liang's requirements.那一篇《论硬译》的开头论误译胜于死译说：“一部书断断不会完全曲译……部分的曲译即使是错误，究竟也还给你一个错误，这个错误也许真是害人无穷的，而你读的时候究竟还落个爽快。”末两句大可以加上夹圈，但我却从来不干这样的勾当。我的译作，本不在博读者的“爽快”，却往往给以不舒服，甚而至于使人气闷，憎恶，愤恨。读了会“落个爽快”的东西，自有新月社的人们的译著在：徐志摩先生的诗，沈从文凌叔华先生的小说，陈西滢（即陈源）先生的闲话，梁实秋先生的批评，潘光旦先生的优生学，还有白璧德先生的人文主义。
The beginning of the "On Hard Translation" argues that mistranslation is better than dead translation: "A book will not be completely mistranslated...... Even if some of the translations are wrong, they will give you a mistake, and this mistake may be really harmful, and you will still be happy when you read it. The last two sentences can be added to the circle, but I never do such a thing. My translations are not intended to be "refreshing" for readers, but they often give people discomfort, and even make people feel depressed, hateful, and resentful. After reading something that will "make you feel refreshed", the translations of the people of the Crescent Society are: Mr. Xu Zhimo's poems, Mr. Shen Congwen's novels by Ling Shuhua, the gossip of Mr. Chen Xiying (i.e. Chen Yuan), the criticism of Mr. Liang Shiqiu, the eugenics of Mr. Pan Guangdan, and the humanism of Mr. Bai Bide.所以，梁先生后文说：“这样的书，就如同看地图一般，要伸着手指来寻找句法的线索位置”这些话，在我也就觉得是废话，虽说犹如不说了。是的，由我说来，要看“这样的书”就如同看地图一样，要伸着手指来找寻“句法的线索位置”的。看地图虽然没有看《杨妃出浴图》或《岁寒三友图》那么“爽快”，甚而至于还须伸着手指（其实这恐怕梁先生自己如此罢了，看惯地图的人，是只用眼睛就可以的），但地图并不是死图；所以“硬译”即使有同一之劳，照例子也就和“死译”有了些“什么区别”。识得ABCD者自以为新学家，仍旧和化学方程式无关，会打算盘的自以为数学家，看起笔算的演草来还是无所得。现在的世间，原不是一为学者，便与一切事都会有缘的。
Therefore, Mr. Liang later said: "Such a book is like looking at a map, you have to stretch out your fingers to find the location of syntactic clues", these words are nonsense to me, although it is as if I don't say it. Yes, from my point of view, reading "such a book" is like looking at a map, you have to stretch out your fingers to find the "location of syntactic clues". Although looking at the map is not as "refreshing" as reading "Yang Fei Out of the Bathing Map" or "The Three Friends of the Cold Year", and even you have to stretch out your fingers (in fact, this is probably Mr. Liang himself, people who are used to reading maps can only use their eyes), but the map is not a dead map; Therefore, even if "hard translation" has the same effect, it is "somewhat different" from "dead translation" according to the example. Those who know ABCD think they are new scientists, but they still have nothing to do with chemical equations, and they think they are mathematicians, and they still have nothing to gain from the evolution of pen calculations. In "Is Literature Class-Oriented?" "I've never seen a chick with ears."“它怎样听见我叫它呢？”她想到前天四婆告诉她的耳朵是管听东西，眼是管看东西的。

It's enough, I understand "words", and I don't need to stretch out my fingers to find clues, but I don't "wait", thinking that looking at this paragraph is neither "refreshing" nor "refreshing", and there is little difference between not creating.临末，梁先生还有一个诘问：“中国文和外国文是不同的，……翻译之难即在这个地方。假如两种文中的文法句法词法完全一样，那么翻译还成为一件工作吗？……我们不妨把句法变换一下，以使读者能懂为第一要义，因为‘硬着头皮’不是一件愉快的事，并且‘硬译’也不见得能保存‘原来的精悍的语气’。假如‘硬译’而还能保存‘原来的精悍的语气’，那真是一件奇迹，还能说中国文是有‘缺点’吗？”我倒不见得如此之愚，要寻求和中国文相同的外国文，或者希望“两种文中的文法句法词法完全一样”。我但以为文法繁复的国语，较易于翻译外国文，语系相近的，也较易于翻译，而且也是一种工作。荷兰翻德国，俄国翻波兰，能说这和并不工作没有什么区别么？日本语和欧美很“不同”，但他们逐渐添加了新句法，比起古文来，更宜于翻译而不失原来的精悍的语气，开初自然是须“找寻句法的线索位置”，很给了一些人不“愉快”的，但经找寻和习惯，现在已经同化，成为己有了。中国的文法，比日本的古文还要不完备，然而也曾有些变迁，例如《史》《汉》不同于《书经》，现在的白话文又不同于《史》《汉》；有添造，例如唐译佛经，元译上谕，当时很有些“文法句法词法”是生造的，一经习用，便不必伸出手指，就懂得了。现在又来了“外国文”，许多句子，即也须新造，——说得坏点，就是硬造。据我的经验，这样译来，较之化为几句，更能保存原来的精悍的语气，但因为有待于新造，所以原先的中国文是有缺点的。有什么“奇迹”，干什么“吗”呢？但有待于“伸出手指”，“硬着头皮”，于有些人自然“不是一件愉快的事”。不过我是本不想将“爽快”或“愉快”来献给那些诸公的，只要还有若干的读者能够有所得，梁实秋先生“们”的苦乐以及无所得，实在“于我如浮云”。
At the end of the day, Mr. Liang also asked: "Chinese and foreign languages are different,...... The difficulty of translation is in this place. If the 'hard translation' can still preserve the 'original sharp tone', it is really a miracle, can it be said that Chinese has 'shortcomings'? I am not necessarily so foolish to seek the same foreign language as Chinese, or hope that "the grammar, syntax, and grammar of the two texts are exactly the same". I just think that Chinese with complex grammar is easier to translate into foreign languages, and similar language families are also easier to translate, and it is also a kind of work. The Netherlands turned to Germany, Russia turned to Poland, can it be said that this is no different from not working? Japanese is very "different" from Europe and the United States, but they gradually add new syntax, which is more suitable for translation than ancient Chinese without losing the original sharp tone. Chinese grammar is more complete than the ancient Japanese text, but there have been some changes, such as "Shi" and "Han" are different from "Book of Documents", and the current vernacular is different from "Shi" and "Han"; There are additions, such as the Tang translation of Buddhist scriptures, the Yuan translation of the upper edict, at that time, there were many "grammar syntactic and lexical grams" that were created, and once practiced, they did not have to stretch out their fingers to understand. Now there is "foreign language", and many sentences must be newly created,—— to put it badly, that is, hard fabrication. According to my experience, this translation can better preserve the original sharp tone than a few sentences, but because it needs to be recreated, the original Chinese has shortcomings. What is the "miracle", and what is "it"? But waiting to "stick out the finger" and "bite the bullet", for some people, it is naturally "not a pleasant thing". However, I didn't want to dedicate "refreshing" or "happy" to those gentlemen, as long as there are still a few readers who can gain something, the bitterness and joy and nothingness of Mr. Liang Shiqiu's "people" are really "like floating clouds for me".但梁先生又有本不必求助于无产文学理论，而仍然很不了了的地方，例如他说，“鲁迅先生前些年翻译的文学，例如厨川白村的《苦闷的象征》，还不是令人看不懂的东西，但是最近翻译的书似乎改变风格了。”只要有些常识的人就知道：“中国文和外国文是不同的”，但同是一种外国文，因为作者各人的做法，而“风格”和“句法的线索位置”也可以很不同。句子可繁可简，名词可常可专，决不会一种外国文，易解的程度就都一式。我的译《苦闷的象征》，也和现在一样，是按板规逐句，甚而至于逐字译的，然而梁实秋先生居然以为不能看懂者，乃是原文原是易解的缘故，也因为梁实秋先生是中国新的批评家了的缘故，也因为其中硬造的句法，是比较地看惯了的缘故。若在三家村里，专读《古文观止》的学者们，看起来又何尝不比“天书”还难呢。
For example, he said, "The literature translated by Mr. Lu Xun in previous years, such as Chuchuchuan Shiramun's "Symbol of Distress", is not incomprehensible, but the recent translations of books seem to have changed their style. As long as there is some common sense, people will know: "Chinese and foreign languages are different", but they are the same foreign language, because of the author's approach, and the "style" and "syntactic clue position" can also be very different. “硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

三

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

Three但是，这回的“比天书还难”的无产文学理论的译本们，却给了梁先生不小的影响。看不懂了，会有影响，虽然好像滑稽，然而是真的，这位批评家在《文学是有阶级性的吗？》里说：“我现在批评所谓无产文学理论，也只能根据我所能了解的一点材料而已。”这就是说：因此而对于这理论的知识，极不完全了。
However, this time, the translations of the proletarian literary theory that are "more difficult than the Book of Heaven" have had a great influence on Mr. Liang. If you don't understand it, it will have an impact, although it seems funny, but it is true, this critic in "Is Literature Class? "I now criticize the so-called proletarian literary theory, and I can only rely on the little material I can understand. This means that the knowledge of this theory is therefore extremely incomplete.但对于这罪过，我们（包含一切“天书”译者在内，故曰“们”）也只能负一部分的责任，一部分是要作者自己的胡涂或懒惰来负的。“什么卢那卡尔斯基，蒲力汗诺夫”的书我不知道，若夫“婆格达诺夫之类”的三篇论文和托罗兹基的半部《文学与革命》，则确有英文译本的了。英国没有“鲁迅先生”，译文定该非常易解。梁先生对于伟大的无产文学的产生，曾经显示其“等着，等着，等着”的耐心和勇气，这回对于理论，何不也等一下子，寻来看了再说呢。不知其有而不求曰胡涂，知其有而不求曰懒惰，如果单是默坐，这样也许是“爽快”的，然而开起口来，却很容易咽进冷气去了。
But for this sin, we (including all the translators of the "Book of Heaven", hence the "we") can only bear part of the responsibility, and part of it is borne by the author's own foolishness or laziness. I don't know about the book "What Lunakarsky, Pulkhanov", but the three treatises of "Bogdanov and the like" and half of Trotsky's "Literature and Revolution" do have English translations. There is no "Mr. Lu Xun" in the UK, and the translation should be very easy to understand. Mr. Liang once showed his patience and courage to "wait, wait, wait" for the production of great proletarian literature. If you just sit silently, it may be "refreshing", but when you open your mouth, it is easy to swallow the cold air.例如就是那篇《文学是有阶级性的吗？》的高文，结论是并无阶级性。要抹杀阶级性，我以为最干净的是吴稚晖先生的“什么马克斯牛克斯”以及什么先生的“世界上并没有阶级这东西”的学说。那么，就万喙息响，天下太平。但梁先生却中了一些“什么马克斯”毒了，先承认了现在许多地方是资产制度，在这制度之下则有无产者。不过这“无产者本来并没有阶级的自觉。是几个过于富同情心而又态度褊激的领袖把这个阶级观念传授了给他们”，要促起他们的联合，激发他们争斗的欲念。不错，但我以为传授者应该并非由于同情，却因了改造世界的思想。况且“本无其物”的东西，是无从自觉，无从激发的，会自觉，能激发，足见那是原有的东西。原有的东西，就遮掩不久，即如格里莱阿说地体运动，达尔文说生物进化，当初何尝不或者几被宗教家烧死，或者大受保守者攻击呢，然而现在人们对于两说，并不为奇者，就因为地体终于在运动，生物确也在进化的缘故。承认其有而要掩饰为无，非有绝技是不行的。
For example, the article "Is literature class-oriented?" The conclusion is that there is no class. To erase class nature, I think the cleanest ones are Mr. Wu Zhihui's "What Max Niux" and Mr. He's "There is no such thing as class in the world". Then, there will be a thousand breaths, and the world will be peaceful. But Mr. Liang was poisoned by some "what Max" and first admitted that many places are now bourgeois, and under this system there are proletarians. However, this "proletarian originally did not have class consciousness." It was a few overly sympathetic and narrow-minded leaders who taught them this class concept", to promote their unity and stimulate their desire to fight. Yes, but I think the teaching should not be out of sympathy, but because of the idea of transforming the world. Moreover, things that "have no such thing" cannot be conscious, cannot be stimulated, will be conscious, can be stimulated, which shows that it is the original thing. The original things were soon hidden, that is, as Grillaea said about the movement of the earth, and Darwin said that the evolution of living things, why not be burned to death by religious people at the beginning, or attacked by conservatives, but now people are not surprised by these two theories, because the earth is finally moving, and the living things are indeed evolving. Admitting that it exists and trying to cover it up as nothing, it is impossible to have a stunt.但梁先生自有消除斗争的办法，以为如卢梭所说：“资产是文明的基础”，“所以攻击资产制度，即是反抗文明”，“一个无产者假如他是有出息的，只消辛辛苦苦诚诚实实的工作一生，多少必定可以得到相当的资产。这才是正当的生活斗争的手段。”我想，卢梭去今虽已百五十年，但当不至于以为过去未来的文明，都以资产为基础。（但倘说以经济关系为基础，那自然是对的。）希腊印度，都有文明，而繁盛时俱非在资产社会，他大概是知道的；倘不知道，那也是他的错误。至于无产者应该“辛辛苦苦”爬上有产阶级去的“正当”的方法，则是中国有钱的老太爷高兴时候，教导穷工人的古训，在实际上，现今正在“辛辛苦苦诚诚实实”想爬上一级去的“无产者”也还多。然而这是还没有人“把这个阶级观念传授了给他们”的时候。一经传授，他们可就不肯一个一个的来爬了，诚如梁先生所说，“他们是一个阶级了，他们要有组织了，他们是一个集团了，于是他们便不循常轨的一跃而夺取政权财权，一跃而为统治阶级。”但可还有想“辛辛苦苦诚诚实实工作一生，多少必定可以得到相当的资产”的“无产者”呢？自然还有的。然而他要算是“尚未发财的有产者”了。梁先生的忠告，将为无产者所呕吐了，将只好和老太爷去互相赞赏而已了。
However, Mr. Liang has his own way of eliminating the struggle, believing that, as Rousseau said: "Assets are the foundation of civilization", "Therefore, attacking the bourgeois system is resisting civilization", and "If a proletarian is promising, he will only have to work hard and honestly for a lifetime, and he will definitely get considerable assets." This is the means of legitimate life struggle. "I think that although Rousseau has been gone for 150 years, we should not think that the civilizations of the past and the future are based on assets. (But if it is based on economic relations, it is naturally correct.) Greece and India all have civilizations, but they are not in a bourgeois society when they are prosperous, he probably knows; If he doesn't know, it's his mistake. As for the "legitimate" way for the proletariat to "work hard" to climb to the upper class of the proletariat, it is the ancient motto of the rich old lady in China to teach the poor workers when they are happy, but in fact, there are many "proletarians" who are "working hard, honestly, and honestly" to climb to the next level. However, this is when no one has yet "taught them this class concept". As Mr. Liang said, "They are a class, they have to be organized, they are a group, so they jump out of the way and seize the political power and property, and become the ruling class." But what about the "proletarians" who think that "if you work hard and honestly all your life, you will definitely get considerable assets"? Naturally, there are others. However, he is considered a "wealthy man who has not yet made a fortune". Mr. Liang's advice will be vomited by the proletariat, and he will have to praise each other with the old lady.那么，此后如何呢？梁先生以为是不足虑的。因为“这种革命的现象不能是永久的，经过自然进化之后，优胜劣败的定律又要证明了，还是聪明才力过人的人占优越的地位，无产者仍是无产者”。但无产阶级大概也知道“反文明的势力早晚要被文明的势力所征服”，所以“要建立所谓‘无产阶级文化’，……这里面包括文艺学术”。
So, what happens after that? Mr. Liang thought it was not a cause for concern. Because "this revolutionary phenomenon cannot be permanent, after natural evolution, the law of the fittest must be proved again, or the intelligent and talented occupy a superior position, and the proletariat is still the proletarian." But the proletariat probably also knows that "the anti-civilization forces will be conquered by the forces of civilization sooner or later", so "we must establish the so-called 'proletarian culture',...... This includes literature and art scholarship."自此以后，这才入了文艺批评的本题。
Since then, this has entered the topic of literary and artistic criticism.

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

四

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

Four梁先生首先以为无产者文学理论的错误，是“在把阶级的束缚加在文学上面”，因为一个资本家和一个劳动者，有不同的地方，但还有相同的地方，“他们的人性（这两字原本有套圈）并没有两样”，例如都有喜怒哀乐，都有恋爱（但所“说的是恋爱的本身，不是恋爱的方式”），“文学就是表现这最基本的人性的艺术”。这些话是矛盾而空虚的。既然文明以资产为基础，穷人以竭力爬上去为“有出息”，那么，爬上是人生的要谛，富翁乃人类的至尊，文学也只要表现资产阶级就够了，又何必如此“过于富同情心”，一并包括“劣败”的无产者？况且“人性”的“本身”，又怎样表现的呢？譬如原质或杂质的化学底性质，有化合力，物理学底性质有硬度，要显示这力和度数，是须用两种物质来表现的，倘说要不用物质而显示化合力和硬度的单单“本身”，无此妙法；但一用物质，这现象即又因物质而不同。文学不借人，也无以表示“性”，一用人，而且还在阶级社会里，即断不能免掉所属的阶级性，无需加以“束缚”，实乃出于必然。自然，“喜怒哀乐，人之情也”，然而穷人决无开交易所折本的懊恼，煤油大王那会知道北京检煤渣老婆子身受的酸辛，饥区的灾民，大约总不去种兰花，像阔人的老太爷一样，贾府上的焦大，也不爱林妹妹的。“汽笛呀！”“列宁呀！”固然并不就是无产文学，然而“一切东西呀！”“一切人呀！”“可喜的事来了，人喜了呀！”也不是表现“人性”的“本身”的文学。倘以表现最普通的人性的文学为至高，则表现最普遍的动物性——营养，呼吸，运动，生殖——的文学，或者除去“运动”，表现生物性的文学，必当更在其上。倘说，因为我们是人，所以以表现人性为限，那么，无产者就因为是无产阶级，所以要做无产文学。
Mr. Liang first thought that the mistake of the proletarian literary theory was to "impose class shackles on literature", because a capitalist and a laborer have different places, but there are also the same places, "their human nature (these two words originally have ferrules) are not different", for example, there are joys, sorrows, and sorrows, and love (but "what is said is love itself, not the way of love"), "literature is the art of expressing this most basic human nature". These words are contradictory and empty. Since civilization is based on assets and the poor strive to climb up as "promising", then climbing up is the essence of life, the rich are the supreme of mankind, and literature only needs to express the bourgeoisie. Moreover, how is the "itself" of "human nature" expressed? For example, the chemical base properties of the original material or impurities have the combined force, and the physical base properties have hardness, and to show this force and degree, it is necessary to use two substances to express it. But once a substance is used, this phenomenon is different depending on the substance. Literature does not borrow people, nor can it express "sex", once a person is employed, and it is still in the class society, that is, it is absolutely impossible to avoid the class nature to which it belongs, and there is no need to "restrict", which is actually out of necessity. Naturally, "joy, anger, sorrow, and happiness, human feelings", but the poor will never have the chagrin of opening a trading exchange, and the kerosene king will know the bitterness and bitterness suffered by the old woman of the Beijing cinder inspection, and the victims in the starving area probably never go to plant orchids, like the old lady of the broad man, Jiao Da on the Jia Mansion does not love Sister Lin. "Whistle!" "Lenin!" Although it is not proletarian literature, "everything!" "Everyone!" "The gratifying thing is coming, and people are happy!" nor is it literature that expresses the "itself" of "human nature". If literature that expresses the most ordinary human nature is the supreme, then literature that expresses the most common animal nature—nutrition, respiration, movement, reproduction—or literature that excludes "movement" and expresses biological nature, must be even higher. If we say that because we are human beings, we are limited to expressing human nature, then the proletariat is because we are the proletariat, so we must do proletarian literature.其次，梁先生说作者的阶级，和作品无关。托尔斯泰出身贵族，而同情于贫民，然而并不主张阶级斗争；马克斯并非无产阶级中的人物；终身穷苦的约翰孙博士，志行吐属，过于贵族。所以估量文学，当看作品本身，不能连累到作者的阶级和身分。这些例子，也全不足以证明文学的无阶级性的。托尔斯泰正因为出身贵族，旧性荡涤不尽，所以只同情于贫民而不主张阶级斗争。马克斯原先诚非无产阶级中的人物，但也并无文学作品，我们不能悬拟他如果动笔，所表现的一定是不用方式的恋爱本身。至于约翰孙博士终身穷苦，而志行吐属，过于王侯者，我却实在不明白那缘故，因为我不知道英国文学和他的传记。也许，他原想“辛辛苦苦诚诚实实的工作一生，多少必定可以得到相当的资产”，然后再爬上贵族阶级去，不料终于“劣败”，连相当的资产也积不起来，所以只落得摆空架子，“爽快”了罢。
Secondly, Mr. Liang said that the author's class has nothing to do with the work. Tolstoy was born into an aristocratic family and sympathized with the poor, but did not advocate class struggle; Max is not a figure in the proletariat; Dr. Johnson, who has been poor all his life, is more ambitious and vocal than aristocratic. Therefore, when evaluating literature, when looking at the work itself, it cannot be related to the author's class and identity. These examples are not enough to prove the classlessness of literature. Tolstoy was born into an aristocratic family and his old nature could not be cleansed, so he only sympathized with the poor and did not advocate class struggle. Max was not originally a proletarian figure, but he also had no literary works, and we cannot suspense that if he started writing, what he would show must be love itself without any way. As for Dr. Johnson, who was poor all his life, and whose ambitions were more than princes, I really did not understand the reason, because I did not know English literature and his biography. Perhaps, he originally thought that "hard and honest work for a lifetime, he would definitely get considerable assets", and then climbed up to the aristocratic class, but unexpectedly he was finally "inferior" and could not even accumulate considerable assets, so he only ended up emptying the shelf and "refreshing".其次，梁先生说，“好的作品永远是少数人的专利品，大多数永远是蠢的，永远是和文学无缘”，但鉴赏力之有无却和阶级无干，因为“鉴赏文学也是天生的一种福气”，就是，虽在无产阶级里，也会有这“天生的一种福气”的人。由我推论起来，则只要有这一种“福气”的人，虽穷得不能受教育，至于一字不识，也可以赏鉴《新月》月刊，来作“人性”和文艺“本身”原无阶级性的证据。但梁先生也知道天生这一种福气的无产者一定不多，所以另定一种东西（文艺？）来给他们看，“例如什么通俗的戏剧，电影，侦探小说之类”，因为“一般劳工劳农需要娱乐，也许需要少量的艺术的娱乐”的缘故。这样看来，好像文学确因阶级而不同了，但这是因鉴赏力之高低而定的，这种力量的修养和经济无关，乃是上帝之所赐——“福气”。所以文学家要自由创造，既不该为皇室贵族所雇用，也不该受无产阶级所威胁，去做讴功颂德的文章。这是不错的，但在我们所见的无产文学理论中，也并未见过有谁说或一阶级的文学家，不该受皇室贵族的雇用，却该受无产阶级的威胁，去做讴功颂德的文章，不过说，文学有阶级性，在阶级社会中，文学家虽自以为“自由”，自以为超了阶级，而无意识底地，也终受本阶级的阶级意识所支配，那些创作，并非别阶级的文化罢了。例如梁先生的这篇文章，原意是在取消文学上的阶级性，张扬真理的。但以资产为文明的祖宗，指穷人为劣败的渣滓，只要一瞥，就知道是资产家的斗争的“武器”，——不，“文章”了。无产文学理论家以主张“全人类”“超阶级”的文学理论为帮助有产阶级的东西，这里就给了一个极分明的例证。至于成仿吾先生似的“他们一定胜利的，所以我们去指导安慰他们去”，说出“去了”之后，便来“打发”自己们以外的“他们”那样的无产文学家，那不消说，是也和梁先生一样地对于无产文学的理论，未免有“以意为之”的错误的。
Secondly, Mr. Liang said, "Good works are always the patent of a few, most of them are always stupid, and they will always have nothing to do with literature", but the existence of appreciation has nothing to do with class, because "appreciating literature is also a natural blessing", that is, even in the proletariat, there will also be people who are "born with a blessing". From my inference, as long as people with this kind of "blessing", although they are too poor to be educated, as for not being able to read a word, they can also appreciate the monthly magazine "New Moon" as evidence of the original lack of class nature of "human nature" and literature and art "itself". But Mr. Liang also knew that there must not be many proletarians who were born with this kind of blessing, so he decided on another thing (literature and art?). Come and show them, "for example, popular dramas, movies, detective novels, etc.", because "ordinary laborers and peasants need entertainment, and perhaps a small amount of artistic entertainment". In this way, it seems that literature is indeed different depending on class, but this is determined by the level of appreciation, and the cultivation of this power has nothing to do with economics, but is a gift from God - "blessing". Therefore, writers should create freely, neither employed by the royal family nor threatened by the proletariat to write articles praising merits. This is good, but in the theory of proletarian literature that we have seen, I have not seen anyone say that or a class of writers should not be employed by the royal family, but should be threatened by the proletariat to do articles praising merit, but in a class society, although writers think they are "free" and think that they are beyond the class, they are unconsciously dominated by the class consciousness of their own class, and those creations are not the culture of other classes. For example, Mr. Liang's article was originally intended to abolish the class nature in literature and publicize the truth. But the ancestors who regarded bourgeoisie as civilization and the dregs of the poor as inferior dregs only need to glance to know that they are the "weapons" of the struggle of the bourgeoisie,—— no, "articles". Proletarian literary theorists use literary theories that advocate "all mankind" and "superclass" to help the proletariat, and here is a very clear example. As for Mr. Cheng Fangwu, "They will definitely win, so we will guide and comfort them", and after saying "go", they will "send" "them" other than themselves.又其次，梁先生最痛恨的是无产文学理论家以文艺为斗争的武器，就是当作宣传品。他“不反对任何人利用文学来达到另外的目的”，但“不能承认宣传式的文字便是文学”。我以为这是自扰之谈。据我所看过的那些理论，都不过说凡文艺必有所宣传，并没有谁主张只要宣传式的文字便是文学。诚然，前年以来，中国确曾有许多诗歌小说，填进口号和标语去，自以为就是无产文学。但那是因为内容和形式，都没有无产气，不用口号和标语，便无从表示其“新兴”的缘故，实际上也并非无产文学。今年，有名的“无产文学底批评家”钱杏邨先生在《拓荒者》上还在引卢那卡尔斯基的话，以为他推重大众能解的文学，足见用口号标语之未可厚非，来给那些“革命文学”辩护。但我觉得那也和梁实秋先生一样，是有意的或无意的曲解。卢那卡尔斯基所谓大众能解的东西，当是指托尔斯泰做了分给农民的小本子那样的文体，工农一看便会了然的语法，歌调，诙谐。只要看台明·培特尼（Demian Bednii）曾因诗歌得到赤旗章，而他的诗中并不用标语和口号，便可明白了。
Secondly, what Mr. Liang hates most is that proletarian literary theorists use literature and art as a weapon of struggle, that is, as propaganda materials. He "does not object to anyone using literature for other purposes", but "cannot admit that propaganda writing is literature". I thought this was self-disturbing talk. According to the theories I have seen, they only say that all literature and art must be propaganda, and no one advocates that only propaganda words are literature. It is true that since the year before last, there have indeed been many poetry and novels in China, filled in with entrance numbers and slogans, thinking that they are proletarian literature. But that is because the content and form are not proletarian, and without slogans and slogans, it is impossible to express its "emerging", and it is not actually proletarian literature. This year, Mr. Qian Xingcun, a famous "critic of proletarian literature", was still quoting Lunakarski's words in "Pioneer", thinking that he was promoting literature that could be understood by the masses, which shows that it is understandable to use slogans to defend those "revolutionary literature". But I think that's the same as Mr. Liang Shiqiu, intentional or unintentional misinterpretation. What Lunakarsky said the public could understand was that Tolstoy made a small book for the peasants, and the workers and peasants would understand the grammar, song, and humor at a glance. Just look at the fact that Demian Bednii once received a red flag for his poetry, and his poems did not use slogans and slogans.最后，梁先生要看货色。这不错的，是最切实的办法；但抄两首译诗算是在示众，是不对的。《新月》上就曾有《论翻译之难》，何况所译的文是诗。就我所见的而论，卢那卡尔斯基的《被解放的堂·吉诃德》，法兑耶夫的《溃灭》，格拉特珂夫的《水门汀》，在中国这十一年中，就并无可以和这些相比的作品。这是指“新月社”一流的蒙资产文明的余荫，而且衷心在拥护它的作家而言。于号称无产作家的作品中，我也举不出相当的成绩。但钱杏邨先生也曾辩护，说新兴阶级，于文学的本领当然幼稚而单纯，向他们立刻要求好作品，是“布尔乔亚”的恶意。这话为农工而说，是极不错的。这样的无理要求，恰如使他们冻饿了好久，倒怪他们为什么没有富翁那么肥胖一样。但中国的作者，现在却实在并无刚刚放下锄斧柄子的人，大多数都是进过学校的智识者，有些还是早已有名的文人，莫非克服了自己的小资产阶级意识之后，就连先前的文学本领也随着消失了么？不会的。俄国的老作家亚历舍·托尔斯泰和威垒赛耶夫，普理希文，至今都还有好作品。中国的有口号而无随同的实证者，我想，那病根并不在“以文艺为阶级斗争的武器”，而在“借阶级斗争为文艺的武器”，在“无产者文学”这旗帜之下，聚集了不少的忽翻筋斗的人，试看去年的新书广告，几乎没有一本不是革命文学，批评家又但将辩护当作“清算”，就是，请文学坐在“阶级斗争”的掩护之下，于是文学自己倒不必着力，因而于文学和斗争两方面都少关系了。
Finally, Mr. Liang wants to look at the goods. This is good and the most practical way; But copying two translated poems is considered to be for the public, which is not right. There was "On the Difficulty of Translation" in "New Moon", not to mention that the translated text was a poem. As far as I can see, Lunakarsky's "Don Quixote the Liberated", Faduev's "Colapse", and Gratkov's "Watergate" have no works that can be compared with them in the past eleven years in China. This refers to the remnants of the first-class Mongolian asset civilization of the "Crescent Society", and for the writers who wholeheartedly support it. In the works of so-called proletarian writers, I can't give comparable results. However, Mr. Qian Xingcun also defended that the emerging class, of course, was naïve and simple in terms of literary skills, and that it was the malice of "bourgeois" to immediately ask them for good works. This is very good for agricultural workers. Such unreasonable demands are just like making them cold and hungry for a long time, and blame them for not being as fat as the rich man. But Chinese authors, now there are really no people who have just put down the handle of the hoe and axe, most of them are intellectuals who have entered school, and some are literati who have long been famous. No, it won't. The old Russian writers Alexei Tolstoy and Willeseyev and Prishvin still have good works. I think that the root of the problem is not "using literature and art as a weapon of class struggle", but "using class struggle as a weapon of literature and art", under the banner of "proletarian literature", many people who have somersaulted have gathered, try to look at last year's new book advertisement, almost none of them are not revolutionary literature, and critics regard the defense as a "reckoning", that is, please let literature sit under the cover of "class struggle", so literature itself does not have to focus on it. Therefore, there is little relationship between literature and struggle.但中国目前的一时现象，当然毫不足作无产文学之新兴的反证的。梁先生也知道，所以他临末让步说，“假如无产阶级革命家一定要把他的宣传文学唤做无产文学，那总算是一种新兴文学，总算是文学国土里的新收获，用不着高呼打倒资产的文学来争夺文学的领域，因为文学的领域太大了，新的东西总有它的位置的。”但这好像“中日亲善，同存共荣”之说，从羽毛未丰的无产者看来，是一种欺骗。愿意这样的“无产文学者”，现在恐怕实在也有的罢，不过这是梁先生所谓“有出息”的要爬上资产阶级去的“无产者”一流，他的作品是穷秀才未中状元时候的牢骚，从开手到爬上以及以后，都决不是无产文学。无产者文学是为了以自己们之力，来解放本阶级并及一切阶级而斗争的一翼，所要的是全般，不是一角的地位。就拿文艺批评界来比方罢，假如在“人性”的“艺术之宫”（这须从成仿吾先生处租来暂用）里，向南面摆两把虎皮交椅，请梁实秋钱杏邨两位先生并排坐下，一个右执“新月”，一个左执“太阳”，那情形可真是“劳资”媲美了。
However, the current phenomenon in China is certainly not enough to counter the emerging proletarian literature. Mr. Liang also knew, so he made concessions at the end of the day, saying, "If the proletarian revolutionaries must call their propaganda literature proletarian literature, it is finally an emerging literature, and it is finally a new harvest in the literary land. But this seems to be the saying of "friendship between China and Japan, coexistence and common prosperity", which is a kind of deception from the perspective of the proletarians who are not yet feathered. I am afraid that there are really such "proletarian writers" who are willing to do so, but this is Mr. Liang's so-called "promising" "proletarian" who wants to climb up to the bourgeoisie. Proletarian literature is a wing of the struggle for the liberation of its own class and all classes with its own strength. Take the literary and art criticism circle as an analogy, if in the "palace of art" of "human nature" (which must be rented from Mr. Cheng Fangwu for temporary use), two tiger skin chairs are placed to the south, and the two gentlemen of Liang Shiqiu Qian Xing Village are invited to sit side by side, one holding the "new moon" on the right and the other holding the "sun" on the left, then the situation is really comparable to "labor and capital".

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

五

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

Five到这里，又可以谈到我的“硬译”去了。
At this point, we can talk about my "hard translation" again.推想起来，这是很应该跟着发生的问题：无产文学既然重在宣传，宣传必须多数能懂，那么，你这些“硬译”而难懂的理论“天书”，究竟为什么而译的呢？不是等于不译么？
In retrospect, this is a question that should follow: since proletarian literature focuses on propaganda, propaganda must be understood by most people, so why did you translate these "hard translations" and difficult theoretical "heavenly books"? Isn't it the same as not translating?我的回答，是：为了我自己，和几个以无产文学批评家自居的人，和一部分不图“爽快”，不怕艰难，多少要明白一些这理论的读者。
My answer is: for myself, for myself, and for a few people who call themselves proletarian literary critics, and some readers who do not want to be "refreshed", who are not afraid of difficulties, and who understand this theory to some extent.从前年以来，对于我个人的攻击是多极了，每一种刊物上，大抵总要看见“鲁迅”的名字，而作者的口吻，则粗粗一看，大抵好像革命文学家。但我看了几篇，竟逐渐觉得废话太多了。解剖刀既不中腠理，子弹所击之处，也不是致命伤。例如我所属的阶级罢，就至今还未判定，忽说小资产阶级，忽说“布尔乔亚”，有时还升为“封建余孽”，而且又等于猩猩（见《创造月刊》上的“东京通信”）；有一回则骂到牙齿的颜色。在这样的社会里，有封建余孽出风头，是十分可能的，但封建余孽就是猩猩，却在任何“唯物史观”上都没有说明，也找不出牙齿色黄，即有害于无产阶级革命的论据。我于是想，可供参考的这样的理论，是太少了，所以大家有些胡涂。对于敌人，解剖，咬嚼，现在是在所不免的，不过有一本解剖学，有一本烹饪法，依法办理，则构造味道，总还可以较为清楚，有味。人往往以神话中的Prometheus比革命者，以为窃火给人，虽遭天帝之虐待不悔，其博大坚忍正相同。但我从别国里窃得火来，本意却在煮自己的肉的，以为倘能味道较好，庶几在咬嚼者那一面也得到较多的好处，我也不枉费了身躯：出发点全是个人主义，并且还夹杂着小市民性的奢华，以及慢慢地摸出解剖刀来，反而刺进解剖者的心脏里去的“报复”。梁先生说“他们要报复！”其实岂只“他们”，这样的人在“封建余孽”中也很有的。然而，我也愿意于社会上有些用处，看客所见的结果仍是火和光。这样，首先开手的就是《文艺政策》，因为其中含有各派的议论。
Since the year before last, there have been many attacks on me personally, and in every kind of publication, the name of "Lu Xun" is almost always seen, and the author's tone is roughly like a revolutionary writer. But after reading a few articles, I gradually felt that there was too much nonsense. The scalpel did not hit the pores, and the place where the bullet hit was not fatal. For example, the class to which I belong has not yet been determined, suddenly talking about the petty bourgeoisie, sometimes saying "bourgeois", sometimes being elevated to "feudal remnants", and equal to orangutans (see "Tokyo News" in "Creation Monthly"); Once he scolded the color of his teeth. In such a society, it is very possible for feudal remnants to be in the limelight, but the feudal remnants are orangutans, but they are not explained in any "historical materialism", and there is no argument that the yellow teeth are harmful to the proletarian revolution. I thought that there were too few such theories for reference, so everyone was a little foolish. For the enemy, dissection, biting, it is now inevitable, but there is a book of anatomy, there is a book of cooking methods, and if it is handled according to the law, the structure of the taste can always be clearer and more flavorful. People often compare the mythical Prometheus to the revolutionaries, thinking that they stole fire to give to others, and although they were abused by the emperor, they did not regret it, but their breadth and perseverance were exactly the same. But I stole fire from another country, but my intention was to cook my own meat, thinking that if it tasted better, I might get more benefits on the side of the biter, and I didn't waste my body: the starting point was all individualism, and it was mixed with the luxury of a small citizen, and the "revenge" of slowly taking out the scalpel and stabbing it into the heart of the anatomist. Mr. Liang said, "They want to take revenge!" In fact, it is not only "them", such people are also very common among the "feudal remnants". However, I am also willing to be of some use in society, and the result of what the spectators see is still fire and light. In this way, the first thing to start is the "Literary and Art Policy", because it contains the discussions of various factions.郑伯奇先生现在是开书铺，印Hauptmann和Gregory夫人的剧本了，那时他还是革命文学家，便在所编的《文艺生活》上，笑我的翻译这书，是不甘没落，而可惜被别人着了先鞭。翻一本书便会浮起，做革命文学家真太容易了，我并不这样想。有一种小报，则说我的译《艺术论》是“投降”。是的，投降的事，为世上所常有。但其时成仿吾元帅早已爬出日本的温泉，住进巴黎的旅馆了，在这里又向谁去输诚呢。今年，说法又两样了，在《拓荒者》和《现代小说》上，都说是“方向转换”。我看见日本的有些杂志中，曾将这四字加在先前的新感觉派片冈铁兵上，算是一个好名词。其实，这些纷纭之谈，也还是只看名目，连想也不肯想的老病。译一本关于无产文学的书，是不足以证明方向的，倘有曲译，倒反足以为害。我的译书，就也要献给这些速断的无产文学批评家，因为他们是有不贪“爽快”，耐苦来研究这些理论的义务的。
Mr. Zheng Boqi is now opening a bookstore and printing the scripts of Hauptmann and Mrs. Gregory, when he was still a revolutionary writer, and in his "Literary Life", he laughed at my translation of this book, which was unwilling to decline, but unfortunately he was whipped by others. It is so easy to be a revolutionary writer, I don't think so. There is a tabloid that says that my translation of "Art Theory" is "surrender". Yes, surrender is common in the world. But at that time, Marshal Cheng Fangwu had already climbed out of the hot springs in Japan and stayed in a hotel in Paris. This year, there are two different statements, in "Pioneer" and "Modern Novel", it is said to be a "change of direction". I saw that some Japanese magazines had added these four words to the previous new sense faction Kataoka Teppei, which was a good term. In fact, these controversial talks are still old diseases that only look at the name and refuse to even think about it. Translating a book on proletarian literature is not enough to prove the direction, and if there is a distorted translation, it is enough to cause harm. My translation is also dedicated to these quick-witted proletarian literary critics, because they have the obligation not to be greedy for "refreshment" and to study these theories patiently.但我自信并无故意的曲译，打着我所不佩服的批评家的伤处了的时候我就一笑，打着我的伤处了的时候我就忍疼，却决不肯有所增减，这也是始终“硬译”的一个原因。自然，世间总会有较好的翻译者，能够译成既不曲，也不“硬”或“死”的文章的，那时我的译本当然就被淘汰，我就只要来填这从“无有”到“较好”的空间罢了。
But I am confident that I have no intentional translation, I smile when I am hurt by critics I don't admire, and I endure the pain when I hit my wounds, but I will never add or subtract, which is also one of the reasons why I always "hard translate". Naturally, there will always be better translators in the world who can translate articles that are neither distorted, nor "hard" or "dead", and then of course my translation will be eliminated, and I just need to fill in the space from "nothing" to "better".然而世间纸张还多，每一文社的人数却少，志大力薄，写不完所有的纸张，于是一社中的职司克敌助友，扫荡异类的批评家，看见别人来涂写纸张了，便喟然兴叹，不胜其摇头顿足之苦。上海的《申报》上，至于称社会科学的翻译者为“阿狗阿猫”，其愤愤有如此。在“中国新兴文学的地位，早为读者所共知”的蒋光Z先生，曾往日本东京养病，看见藏原惟人，谈到日本有许多翻译太坏，简直比原文还难读……他就笑了起来，说：“……那中国的翻译界更要莫名其妙了，近来中国有许多书籍都是译自日文的，如果日本人将欧洲人那一国的作品带点错误和删改，从日文译到中国去，试问这作品岂不是要变了一半相貌么？……”（见《拓荒者》也就是深不满于翻译，尤其是重译的表示。不过梁先生还举出书名和坏处，蒋先生却只嫣然一笑，扫荡无余，真是普遍得远了。藏原惟人是从俄文直接译过许多文艺理论和小说的，于我个人就极有裨益。我希望中国也有一两个这样的诚实的俄文翻译者，陆续译出好书来，不仅自骂一声“混蛋”就算尽了革命文学家的责任。
However, there is still a lot of paper in the world, but the number of people in each literary society is small, and the ambition is weak, and it is impossible to write all the paper, so the officials in the society defeat enemies and help friends, sweep away heterogeneous critics, and when they see others coming to scribble paper, they sigh and can't bear the pain of shaking their heads and stomping their feet. In Shanghai's "Declaration", as for calling the translators of social sciences "dogs and cats", they are so indignant. Mr. Jiang Guangz, who "has long been known to readers as the status of China's emerging literature", once went to Tokyo, Japan to recuperate, saw Kurahara Weihito, and said that many translations in Japan are too bad and are even more difficult to read than the original text...... He laughed and said, "...... Recently, many books in China have been translated from Japanese, if the Japanese translate the works of Europeans from that country from Japanese to China, wouldn't this work change half of its appearance? ......" (See "Pioneers", which means that he is deeply dissatisfied with translation, especially the retranslation. However, Mr. Liang also listed the title and disadvantages of the book, but Mr. Jiang only smiled and swept away, which is really far from common. Zangyuan Yuito has directly translated many literary and artistic theories and novels from Russian, which is very beneficial to me personally. I hope that there will be one or two such honest Russian translators in China who will translate good books one after another, not only calling themselves "bastards" but also fulfilling their responsibilities as revolutionary writers.然而现在呢，这些东西，梁实秋先生是不译的，称人为“阿狗阿猫”的伟人也不译，学过俄文的蒋先生原是最为适宜的了，可惜养病之后，只出了一本《一周间》，而日本则早已有了两种的译本。中国曾经大谈达尔文，大谈尼采，到欧战时候，则大骂了他们一通，但达尔文的著作的译本，至今只有一种，尼采的则只有半部，学英德文的学者及文豪都不暇顾及，或不屑顾及，拉倒了。所以暂时之间，恐怕还只好任人笑骂，仍从日文来重译，或者取一本原文，比照了日译本来直译罢。我还想这样做，并且希望更多有这样做的人，来填一填彻底的高谈中的空虚，因为我们不能像蒋先生那样的“好笑起来”，也不该如梁先生的“等着，等着，等着”了。
However, now, Mr. Liang Shiqiu does not translate these things, and the great man who calls people "Dog and Cat" does not translate, and Mr. Jiang, who has learned Russian, was originally the most suitable, but unfortunately after recovering from illness, only one "Week" was published, while Japan already has two translations. China used to talk a lot about Darwin and Nietzsche, but when it came to the European War, it scolded them, but there is only one translation of Darwin's works so far, and only half of Nietzsche's. So for the time being, I am afraid that I have no choice but to be ridiculed and scolded, still retranslated from Japanese, or take the original text and translate it literally according to the Japanese translation. I also want to do this, and I hope that more people who do this will fill the void in the complete high talk, because we can't be like Mr. Jiang's "funny", nor should we be like Mr. Liang's "waiting, waiting, waiting".

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

六

“硬译”与“文学的阶级性”

Six我在开头曾有“以硬自居了，而实则其软如棉，正是新月社的一种特色”这些话，到这里还应该简短地补充几句，就作为本篇的收场。
At the beginning, I had the words "I think I am hard, but in fact it is as soft as cotton, which is a characteristic of the Crescent Society", and I should add a few sentences briefly here as the end of this article.《新月》一出世，就主张“严正态度”，但于骂人者则骂之，讥人者则讥之。这并不错，正是“即以其人之道，还治其人之身”，虽然也是一种“报复”，而非为了自己。到二卷六七号合本的广告上，还说“我们都保持‘容忍’的态度（除了‘不容忍’的态度是我们所不能容忍以外），我们都喜欢稳健的合乎理性的学说”。上两句也不错，“以眼还眼，以牙还牙”，和开初仍然一贯。然而从这条大路走下去，一定要遇到“以暴力抗暴力”，这和新月社诸君所喜欢的“稳健”也不能相容了。
As soon as "New Moon" came out, it advocated a "strict attitude", but it scolded those who scolded people and ridiculed those who ridiculed it. This is not bad, it is "to treat others in their own way", although it is also a kind of "revenge", not for oneself. In the advertisement of the second volume of No. 6 and No. 7, it is also said that "we all maintain an attitude of 'tolerance' (except that the attitude of 'intolerance' is intolerable to us), and we all like a stable rational doctrine." The first two sentences are also good, "an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth", which is still consistent with the beginning. However, if you go down this road, you must encounter "fighting violence with violence", which is incompatible with the "stability" that the members of the Crescent Society like.这一回，新月社的“自由言论”遭了压迫，照老办法，是必须对于压迫者，也加以压迫的，但《新月》上所显现的反应，却是一篇《告压迫言论自由者》，先引对方的党义，次引外国的法律，终引东西史例，以见凡压迫自由者，往往臻于灭亡：是一番替对方设想的警告。
This time, the "free speech" of the Crescent Society was oppressed, and according to the old method, it was necessary to oppress the oppressors, but the reaction shown in the "New Moon" was an article "Accusing the Oppressors of Freedom of Speech", first quoting the other party's righteousness, then quoting foreign laws, and finally quoting the historical examples of the East and the West, so as to see that those who oppress freedom often lead to destruction: it is a warning conceived for the other party.所以，新月社的“严正态度”，“以眼还眼”法，归根结蒂，是专施之力量相类，或力量较小的人的，倘给有力者打肿了眼，就要破例，只举手掩住自己的脸，叫一声“小心你自己的眼睛！”
Therefore, the "solemn attitude" of the Crescent Society, the "eye for eye" method, in the final analysis, is a person with similar or less powerful power, if the eyes of the powerful are swollen, they must make an exception, only raise their hands to cover their faces, and shout "Be careful of your own eyes!" ”

习惯与改革

习惯与改革

习惯与改革

Habits and reforms体质和精神都已硬化了的人民，对于极小的一点改革，也无不加以阻挠，表面上好像恐怕于自己不便，其实是恐怕于自己不利，但所设的口实，却往往见得极其公正而且堂皇。
On the surface, it seems that they are afraid of their own inconvenience, but in fact they are afraid of being detrimental to themselves, but the excuses they set up are often extremely fair and dignified.今年的禁用阴历，原也是琐碎的，无关大体的事，但商家当然叫苦连天了。不特此也，连上海的无业游民，公司雇员，竟也常常慨然长叹，或者说这很不便于农家的耕种，或者说这很不便于海船的候潮。他们居然因此念起久不相干的乡下的农夫，海上的舟子来。这真像煞有些博爱。
This year's ban on the lunar calendar was originally trivial and irrelevant, but of course the merchants complained. Not only that, but even the unemployed vagrants and company employees in Shanghai often sighed, or that this was very inconvenient for farmers' farming, or that it was very inconvenient for sea ships to wait for the tide. They actually thought of the farmer in the countryside who had been irrelevant for a long time, and the boat on the sea. This is really a bit of fraternity.一到阴历的十二月二十三，爆竹就到处毕毕剥剥。我问一家的店伙：“今年仍可以过旧历年，明年一准过新历年么？”那回答是：“明年又是明年，要明年再看了。”他并不信明年非过阳历年不可。但日历上，却诚然删掉了阴历，只存节气。然而一面在报章上，则出现了《一百二十年阴阳合历》的广告。好，他们连曾孙玄孙时代的阴历，也已经给准备妥当了，一百二十年！
As soon as the 23rd day of the twelfth month of the lunar calendar arrives, firecrackers are peeled everywhere. I asked a shopkeeper: "Can we still celebrate the old calendar year this year, and will we celebrate the new calendar year next year?" The answer was: "Next year is next year, and I will watch it again next year." He didn't believe that next year had to be a solar year. But on the calendar, it is true that the lunar calendar is deleted, and only the solar terms are kept. However, on the other hand, in the newspaper, there was an advertisement for "One Hundred and Twenty Years of Lunar and Yang Calendar". Okay, they have even prepared the lunar calendar of the great-grandson era, one hundred and twenty years!梁实秋先生们虽然很讨厌多数，但多数的力量是伟大，要紧的，有志于改革者倘不深知民众的心，设法利导，改进，则无论怎样的高文宏议，浪漫古典，都和他们无干，仅止于几个人在书房中互相叹赏，得些自己满足。假如竟有“好人政府”，出令改革乎，不多久，就早被他们拉回旧道上去了。
Although Mr. Liang Shiqiu hates the majority, the power of the majority is great and important, and if those who are interested in reforming do not know the hearts of the people and try to guide and improve, then no matter what kind of high-literary grand discussions, romantic and classical discussions have nothing to do with them, only a few people admire each other in the study and get some satisfaction for themselves. If there was a "good people's government" and ordered reform, it would not be long before they would have been pulled back to the old road.真实的革命者，自有独到的见解，例如乌略诺夫先生，他是将“风俗”和“习惯”，都包括在“文化”之内的，并且以为改革这些，很为困难。我想，但倘不将这些改革，则这革命即等于无成，如沙上建塔，顷刻倒坏。中国最初的排满革命，所以易得响应者，因为口号是“光复旧物”，就是“复古”，易于取得保守的人民同意的缘故。但到后来，竟没有历史上定例的开国之初的盛世，只枉然失了一条辫子，就很为大家所不满了。
Real revolutionaries have their own unique opinions, such as Mr. Ulonov, who includes "customs" and "habits" in "culture" and thinks that it is very difficult to reform them. I think that if these reforms are not carried out, this revolution will be equivalent to nothing, like building a tower on the sand and collapsing in an instant. China's initial platoon revolution made it easy to get responders, because the slogan was "restore the old", that is, "retro", and it was easy to obtain the consent of the conservative people. But later, there was no historical rule at the beginning of the founding of the country, and only a braid was lost in vain, which was very dissatisfied with everyone.以后较新的改革，就著著失败，改革一两，反动十斤，例如上述的一年日历上不准注阴历，却来了阴阳合历一百二十年。
For example, the above-mentioned one-year calendar is not allowed to note the lunar calendar, but the lunar calendar has been combined, but the lunar calendar has been combined.这种合历，欢迎的人们一定是很多的，因为这是风俗和习惯所拥护，所以也有风俗和习惯的后援。别的事也如此，倘不深入民众的大层中，于他们的风俗习惯，加以研究，解剖，分别好坏，立存废的标准，而于存于废，都慎选施行的方法，则无论怎样的改革，都将为习惯的岩石所压碎，或者只在表面上浮游一些时。
There must be many people who welcome this kind of calendar, because this is supported by customs and habits, so there is also the support of customs and habits. The same is true for other things, if we do not go deep into the great layer of the people, study and dissect their customs and habits, distinguish between good and bad, establish standards for survival and waste, and carefully choose the method of implementation in existence and waste, then no matter what kind of reform it may be, it will be crushed by the rocks of habit, or only float on the surface.现在已不是在书斋中，捧书本高谈宗教，法律，文艺，美术……等等的时候了，即使要谈论这些，也必须先知道习惯和风俗，而且有正视这些的黑暗面的勇猛和毅力。因为倘不看清，就无从改革。仅大叫未来的光明，其实是欺骗怠慢的自己和怠慢的听众的。
Now it is no longer in the study, holding books and talking about religion, law, literature and art...... It's time to wait, even if you want to talk about this, you must first know the habits and customs, and have the courage and perseverance to face the dark side of them. Because if you don't see it clearly, you can't reform. Only shouting about the brightness of the future is actually deceiving the negligent self and the negligent listeners.

非革命的急进革命论者

非革命的急进革命论者

非革命的急进革命论者

Non-revolutionary radical revolutionaries倘说，凡大队的革命军，必须一切战士的意识，都十分正确，分明，这才是真的革命军，否则不值一哂。这言论，初看固然是很正当，彻底似的，然而这是不可能的难题，是空洞的高谈，是毒害革命的甜药。
If it is said that the revolutionary army of any brigade must have the consciousness of all soldiers very correct and clear, this is the real revolutionary army, otherwise it is not worth it. At first glance, this remark seems to be very legitimate and thorough, but it is an impossible problem, an empty rhetoric, and a sweet medicine to poison the revolution.譬如在帝国主义的主宰之下，必不容训练大众个个有了“人类之爱”，然后笑嘻嘻地拱手变为“大同世界”一样，在革命者们所反抗的势力之下，也决不容用言论或行动，使大多数人统得到正确的意识。所以每一革命部队的突起，战士大抵不过是反抗现状这一种意思，大略相同，终极目的是极为歧异的。或者为社会，或者为小集团，或者为一个爱人，或者为自己，或者简直为了自杀。然而革命军仍然能够前行。因为在进军的途中，对于敌人，个人主义者所发的子弹，和集团主义者所发的子弹是一样地能够制其死命；任何战士死伤之际，便要减少些军中的战斗力，也两者相等的。但自然，因为终极目的的不同，在行进时，也时时有人退伍，有人落荒，有人颓唐，有人叛变，然而只要无碍于进行，则愈到后来，这队伍也就愈成为纯粹，精锐的队伍了。
For example, under the dominance of imperialism, it is not allowed to train the masses to have "human love" and then smile and bow their hands to become a "world of great harmony", and under the forces resisted by revolutionaries, words or actions must not be used to make the majority of people gain correct consciousness. Therefore, the soldiers of each revolutionary unit are probably just resisting the status quo, which is roughly the same, and the ultimate purpose is extremely different. Or for society, or for a small group, or for a lover, or for oneself, or simply for suicide. However, the revolutionary army was still able to move forward. For on the march, against the enemy, the bullets fired by the individualists are the same as the bullets fired by the corporatists; When any soldier is killed or wounded, the combat effectiveness of the army must be reduced, and the two are equal. But naturally, because of the difference in ultimate purpose, when marching, there are always people who are discharged from the army, some people are abandoned, some people are decadent, and some people are rebellious, but as long as it does not hinder the progress, the more later, this team will become a pure and elite team.我先前为叶永蓁君的《小小十年》作序，以为已经为社会尽了些力量，便是这意思。书中的主角，究竟上过前线，当过哨兵（虽然连放枪的方法也未曾被教），比起单是抱膝哀歌，握笔愤叹的文豪们来，实在也切实得远了。倘若要现在的战士都是意识正确，而且坚于钢铁之战士，不但是乌托邦的空想，也是出于情理之外的苛求。
I previously wrote a preface to Ye Yongzhen's "Little Ten Years", thinking that I had done some strength for society, and that is what I meant. The protagonist in the book, who has been on the front line and worked as a sentinel (although he has not even been taught how to shoot a gun), is really far more practical than the literary heroes who just hugged their knees and lamented and held their pens and lamented. If the current warriors are all correct in consciousness and strong in steel, it is not only a utopian fantasy, but also out of unreasonable demands.但后来在《申报》上，却看见了更严厉，更彻底的批评，因为书中的主角的从军，动机是为了自己，所以深加不满。《申报》是最求和平，最不鼓动革命的报纸，初看仿佛是很不相称似的，我在这里要指出貌似彻底的革命者，而其实是极不革命或有害革命的个人主义的论客来，使那批评的灵魂和报纸的躯壳正相适合。
But later, in the "Declaration", I saw harsher and more thorough criticism, because the protagonist in the book joined the army, and his motivation was for himself, so he was deeply dissatisfied. The "Declaration" is the most peace-seeking and least revolutionary newspaper, and at first glance it seems very disproportionate, and I would like to point out here that it seems to be a complete revolutionary, but in fact it is an individualistic commentator who is extremely non-revolutionary or harmful to the revolution, so that the soul of criticism and the body of the newspaper are just right.其一是颓废者，因为自己没有一定的理想和无力，便流落而求刹那的享乐；一定的享乐，又使他发生厌倦，则时时寻求新刺戟，而这刺戟又须利害，这才感到畅快。革命便也是那颓废者的新刺戟之一，正如饕餮者餍足了肥甘，味厌了，胃弱了，便要吃胡椒和辣椒之类，使额上出一点小汗，才能送下半碗饭去一般。他于革命文艺，就要彻底的，完全的革命文艺，一有时代的缺陷的反映，就使他皱眉，以为不值一哂。和事实离开是不妨的，只要一个爽快。法国的波特莱尔，谁都知道是颓废的诗人，然而他欢迎革命，待到革命要妨害他的颓废生活的时候，他才憎恶革命了。所以革命前夜的纸张上的革命家，而且是极彻底，极激烈的革命家，临革命时，便能够撕掉他先前的假面，——不自觉的假面。这种史例，是也应该献给一碰小钉子，一有小地位（或小款子），便东窜东京，西走巴黎的成仿吾那样“革命文学家”的。
One is the decadent, because they do not have certain ideals and powerlessness, they fall into exile and seek momentary pleasure; A certain amount of pleasure makes him tired of it, so he always seeks new spears, and this spear must be interested, so he feels happy. The revolution is also one of the new thorns of the decadent, just as the gluttonous eater has enough fat and sweetness, is tired of taste, and has a weak stomach, so he has to eat pepper and chili peppers, so that he sweats a little on his forehead before he can send half a bowl of rice. He must be thorough and completely revolutionary in revolutionary literature and art, and as soon as there is a reflection of the flaws of the times, he frowns and thinks that it is not worth it. It's okay to leave with the facts, as long as it's refreshing. Baudelaire of France was known to everyone as a decadent poet, but he welcomed the revolution and hated it when it was about to hinder his decadent life. Therefore, the revolutionary on the paper on the eve of the revolution, and the extremely thorough and fierce revolutionary, was able to tear off his previous mask ,—— unconscious mask when the revolution was about to occur. This kind of historical example should also be dedicated to "revolutionary writers" like Cheng Fangwu, who touched a small nail and fled east to Tokyo and west to Paris as soon as he had a small status (or a small sum).其一，我还定不出他的名目。要之，是毫无定见，因而觉得世上没有一件对，自己没有一件不对，归根结蒂，还是现状最好的人们。他现为批评家而说话的时候，就随便捞到一种东西以驳诘相反的东西。要驳互助说时用争存说，驳争存说时用互助说；反对和平论时用阶级争斗说，反对斗争时就主张人类之爱。论敌是唯心论者呢，他的立场是唯物论，待到和唯物论者相辩难，他却又化为唯心论者了。要之，是用英尺来量俄里，又用法尺来量密达，而发见无一相合的人。因为别的一切，无一相合，于是永远觉得自己是“允执厥中”，永远得到自己满足。从这些人们的批评的指示，则只要不完全，有缺陷，就不行。但现在的人，的事，那里会有十分完全，并无缺陷的呢，为万全计，就只好毫不动弹。然而这毫不动弹，却也就是一个大错。总之，做人之道，是非常之烦难了，至于做革命家，那当然更不必说。
First, I can't name him yet. In short, they have no fixed opinion, so they feel that there is nothing right in the world, and there is nothing wrong with themselves, in the final analysis, they are still the best people in the current situation. When he speaks for critics now, he finds something to refute the opposite. It is necessary to use the theory of dispute when refuting the theory of mutual assistance, and use the theory of mutual assistance when refuting the theory of existence; When opposing peace, he used class struggle to argue, and when opposing struggle, he advocated human love. When it comes to arguing with materialists, he becomes an idealist again. In short, it is to measure the number of versts in feet and the ruler to measure the denseness, but it is found that there is no one who agrees. Because everything else is in harmony, I will always feel that I am "in the middle" and will always be satisfied by myself. From the instructions of these people's criticism, as long as they are incomplete and defective, they will not work. But nowadays, people's affairs will be very complete and flawless, so for the sake of perfection, they have no choice but to remain motionless. However, this is a big mistake. In short, the way of being a person is very troublesome, and as for being a revolutionary, of course, it is not to mention.《申报》的批评家对于《小小十年》虽然要求彻底的革命的主角，但于社会科学的翻译，是加以刻毒的冷嘲的，所以那灵魂是后一流，而略带一些颓废者的对于人生的无聊，想吃些辣椒来开开胃的气味。
Although the critics of "Declaration" demand the protagonist of a complete revolution in "Little Ten Years", the translation of the social sciences is a bitter and cynical, so the soul is second-class, and there is a slight sense of decadent people's boredom in life and want to eat some chili peppers to appetize them.

张资平氏的“小说学”

张资平氏的“小说学”

张资平氏的“小说学”

Zhang Ziping's "Novelology"张资平氏据说是“最进步”的“无产阶级作家”，你们还在“萌芽”，还在“拓荒”，他却已在收获了。这就是进步，拔步飞跑，望尘莫及。然而你如果追踪而往呢，就看见他跑进“乐群书店”中。
Zhang Ziping is said to be the "most progressive" "proletarian writer", you are still "sprouting" and "pioneering", but he is already reaping. This is progress, and it is out of reach. However, if you follow it, you will see him running into the "Lequn Bookstore".张资平氏先前是三角恋爱小说作家，并且看见女的性欲，比男人还要熬不住，她来找男人，贱人呀贱人，该吃苦。这自然不是无产阶级小说。但作者一转方向，则一人得道，鸡犬飞升，何况神仙的遗蜕呢，《张资平全集》还应该看的。这是收获呀，你明白了没有？
Zhang Ziping was previously a writer of love triangle novels, and saw that the sexual desire of women was even more unbearable than men, she came to find men, bitches, bitches, deserve hardships. This is naturally not a proletarian novel. But as soon as the author turns around, one person will gain the way, and the chickens and dogs will soar, not to mention the shedding of the gods, "The Complete Works of Zhang Ziping" should also be read. This is a gain, do you understand?"还有收获哩。《申报》报告，今年的大夏学生，敬请“为青年所崇拜的张资平先生”去教“小说学”了。中国老例，英文先生是一定会教外国史的，国文先生是一定会教伦理学的，何况小说先生，当然满肚子小说学。要不然，他做得出来吗？我们能保得定荷马没有“史诗作法”，沙士比亚没有“戏剧学概论”吗？
There is also a catch. According to the "Declaration" report, this year's Daxia students are invited to teach "novel studies" by "Mr. Zhang Ziping, who is admired by young people". In the old Chinese example, Mr. English will definitely teach foreign history, and Mr. Chinese will definitely teach ethics, not to mention Mr. Novel, of course, he is full of novels. Otherwise, could he do it? Can we be sure that Homer did not have an "epic approach" and Shakespeare did not have an "introduction to dramatism"?呜呼，听讲的门徒是有福了，从此会知道如何三角，如何恋爱，你想女人吗，不料女人的性欲冲动比你还要强，自己跑来了。朋友，等着罢。但最可怜的是不在上海，只好遥遥“崇拜”，难以身列门墙的青年，竟不能恭听这伟大的“小说学”。现在我将《张资平全集》和“小说学”的精华，提炼在下面，遥献这些崇拜家，算是“望梅止渴”云。
Alas, blessed are the disciples who listened to the lecture, from now on they will know how to triangle, how to fall in love, do you miss women, but unexpectedly, women's sexual impulses are stronger than yours, and they came by themselves. Friends, just wait. But the most pitiful thing is that he is not in Shanghai, so he has to "worship" from afar, and the young people who are difficult to stand on the wall cannot listen to this great "novel study". Now I have refined the essence of "The Complete Works of Zhang Ziping" and "Novelology" below, and dedicated these admirers from afar, which can be regarded as "looking at plums to quench thirst".那就是——△
