This is naturally the task of other works, and the author cannot be tasked with bearing all of them, but the reader must not ignore this, otherwise, as the Indian "Parables" says, it is said that it is because he wants to build a tall building and oppose the erection of pillars on the ground.我不加戒备的将这读完了，即因为上文所说的原因。而我相信这书所说的苏联的好处的，也还有一个原因，那就是十来年前，说过苏联怎么不行怎么无望的所谓文明国人，去年已在苏联的煤油和麦子面前发抖。而且我看见确凿的事实：他们是在吸中国的膏血，夺中国的土地，杀中国的人民。他们是大骗子，他们说苏联坏，要进攻苏联，就可见苏联是好的了。这一部书，正也转过来是我的意见的实证。
I read it unguarded, for the reasons mentioned above. And I believe that there is another reason why I believe in the benefits of the Soviet Union mentioned in this book, that is, the so-called civilized people who said that the Soviet Union could not do and was hopeless more than ten years ago were trembling in front of the kerosene and wheat of the Soviet Union last year. And I see the conclusive fact: they are sucking China's blood, seizing China's land, and killing China's people. They are big liars, they say that the Soviet Union is bad, and if they want to attack the Soviet Union, it can be seen that the Soviet Union is good. This book, Zhengya, is the empirical evidence of my opinion.一九三二年四月二十日，鲁迅于上海闸北寓楼记。
On April 20, 1932, Lu Xun recorded his residence in Zhabei, Shanghai.

我们不再受骗了

我们不再受骗了

我们不再受骗了

We are no longer deceived帝国主义是一定要进攻苏联的。苏联愈弄得好，它们愈急于要进攻，因为它们愈要趋于灭亡。
Imperialism must attack the Soviet Union. The better the Soviet Union did it, the more eager they were to attack, because the more they were destined to perish.我们被帝国主义及其侍从们真是骗得长久了。十月革命之后，它们总是说苏联怎么穷下去，怎么凶恶，怎么破坏文化。但现在的事实怎样？小麦和煤油的输出，不是使世界吃惊了么？正面之敌的实业党的首领，不是也只判了十年的监禁么？列宁格勒，墨斯科的图书馆和博物馆，不是都没有被炸掉么？文学家如绥拉菲摩维支，法捷耶夫，革拉特珂夫，绥甫林娜，唆罗诃夫等，不是西欧东亚，无不赞美他们的作品么？关于艺术的事我不大知道，但据乌曼斯基（K. Umansky）说，一九一九年中，在墨斯科的展览会就有二十次，列宁格勒两次（《Neue Kunst in Russland》），则现在的旺盛，更是可想而知了。然而谣言家是极无耻而且巧妙的，一到事实证明了他的话是撒谎时，他就躲下，另外又来一批。
We have been deceived by imperialism and its entourage for a long time. After the October Revolution, they always said how the Soviet Union was poor, how vicious it was, and how it destroyed culture. But what are the facts now? Didn't the export of wheat and kerosene surprise the world? Didn't the leader of the Industrial Party, who was a frontal enemy, only sentenced to ten years in prison? Leningrad, Mexico's libraries and museums, weren't they all blown up? Writers such as Suerafimovich, Fadeev, Gratkov, Suevlina, Sorokhov, etc., are not Western Europe and East Asia, all praise their works? I don't know much about art, but according to K. Umansky. Umansky said that in mid-1919, there were 20 exhibitions in Moscow and two in Leningrad ("Neue Kunst in Russland"), and the current vigor can be imagined. However, the rumor is extremely shameless and ingenious, and when it turns out that his words are lying, he hides and another batch comes.新近我看见一本小册子，是说美国的财政有复兴的希望的，序上说，苏联的购领物品，必须排成长串，现在也无异于从前，仿佛他很为排成长串的人们抱不平，发慈悲一样。
Recently, I saw a pamphlet saying that there is hope for the revival of the United States' finances, and in the preface, the Soviet Union's purchases must be lined up in a long string, and now it is no different from before, as if he was very grieving and showing mercy to the people in the long row.这一事，我是相信的，因为苏联内是正在建设的途中，外是受着帝国主义的压迫，许多物品，当然不能充足。但我们也听到别国的失业者，排着长串向饥寒进行；中国的人民，在内战，在外侮，在水灾，在榨取的大罗网之下，排着长串而进向死亡去。
I believe this, because the Soviet Union is in the process of construction, and the outside is oppressed by imperialism, and many items are of course not sufficient. But we also hear about the unemployed from other countries, marching in long lines to hunger and cold; The Chinese people, in civil wars, foreign insults, floods, and under the net of extraction, marched in long rows to death.然而帝国主义及其奴才们，还来对我们说苏联怎么不好，好像它倒愿意苏联一下子就变成天堂，人们个个享福。现在竟这样子，它失望了，不舒服了。——这真是恶鬼的眼泪。
However, imperialism and its minions still come to tell us how bad the Soviet Union is, as if it wants the Soviet Union to become a paradise at once and people will enjoy themselves. Now that it's like this, it's disappointed and uncomfortable. - These are really evil spirit tears.一睁开眼，就露出恶鬼的本相来的，——它要去惩办了。
As soon as he opened his eyes, he revealed the true nature of an evil ghost,—— he was going to punish him.它一面去惩办，一面来诳骗。正义，人道，公理之类的话，又要满天飞舞了。但我们记得，欧洲大战时候，飞舞过一回的，骗得我们的许多苦工，到前线去替它们死，接着是在北京的中央公园里竖了一块无耻的，愚不可及的“公理战胜”的牌坊（但后来又改掉了）。现在怎样？“公理”在那里？这事还不过十六年，我们记得的。
It punishes and deceives on the other hand. Words like justice, humanity, and axioms are going to fly all over the sky again. But we remember that during the European War, it flew once, deceived many of our hard laborers, went to the front line to die for them, and then erected a shameless, foolish "axiom victory" archway in Beijing's Central Park (but later changed it). How now? Where is the "axiom"? It's only been sixteen years, we remember.帝国主义和我们，除了它的奴才之外，那一样利害不和我们正相反？我们的痈疽，是它们的宝贝，那么，它们的敌人，当然是我们的朋友了。它们自身正在崩溃下去，无法支持，为挽救自己的末运，便憎恶苏联的向上。谣诼，诅咒，怨恨，无所不至，没有效，终于只得准备动手去打了，一定要灭掉它才睡得着。但我们干什么呢？我们还会再被骗么？
Imperialism and us, except for its minions, are not the same interests as ours? Our carbuncles are their treasures, so their enemies are, of course, our friends. They themselves are collapsing, unable to support it, and in order to save their own fate, they hate the Soviet Union's upward movement. Rumors, curses, resentment, everything, no effect, finally I had to prepare to fight, I had to destroy it to sleep. But what do we do? Will we still be deceived again?“苏联是无产阶级专政的，智识阶级就要饿死。”——一位有名的记者曾经这样警告我。是的，这倒恐怕要使我也有些睡不着了。但无产阶级专政，不是为了将来的无阶级社会么？只要你不去谋害它，自然成功就早，阶级的消灭也就早，那时就谁也不会“饿死”了。不消说，排长串是一时难免的，但到底会快起来。
"The Soviet Union was a dictatorship of the proletariat, and the intellectual class was going to starve to death." - A famous journalist once warned me like this. Yes, this is probably going to make me a little sleepless. But isn't the dictatorship of the proletariat for the future classless society? As long as you don't murder it, you will naturally succeed sooner, and the class will be eliminated sooner, and no one will "starve to death" at that time. Needless to say, the long queue is inevitable for a while, but it will be fast in the end.帝国主义的奴才们要去打，自己（！）跟着它的主人去打去就是。我们人民和它们是利害完全相反的。我们反对进攻苏联。我们倒要打倒进攻苏联的恶鬼，无论它说着怎样甜腻的话头，装着怎样公正的面孔。
The imperialist minions are going to fight, and they (!) Just follow its owner to fight. We the people have completely opposite interests with them. We opposed attacking the USSR. We must defeat the evil spirit that attacked the Soviet Union, no matter how sweet its words and its fair face may be.这才也是我们自己的生路！
This is also our own way of life!五月六日。
May 6th.

《竖琴》前记

《竖琴》前记

《竖琴》前记

"Harp" preface俄国的文学，从尼古拉斯二世时候以来，就是“为人生”的，无论它的主意是在探究，或在解决，或者堕入神秘，沦于颓唐，而其主流还是一个：为人生。
Russian literature, since the time of Nicholas II, has been "for life", whether its idea is to explore, or to solve, or to fall into mystery and decadence, and its mainstream is still one: for life.这一种思想，在大约二十年前即与中国一部分的文艺绍介者合流，陀思妥夫斯基，都介涅夫，契诃夫，托尔斯泰之名，渐渐出现于文字上，并且陆续翻译了他们的一些作品，那时组织的介绍“被压迫民族文学”的是上海的文学研究会，也将他们算作为被压迫者而呼号的作家的。
This kind of thinking merged with some literary and artistic introducers in China about twenty years ago, and the names of Dostovsky, Dujienev, Chekhov, and Tolstoy gradually appeared in writing, and some of their works were translated one after another.凡这些，离无产者文学本来还很远，所以凡所绍介的作品，自然大抵是叫唤，呻吟，困穷，酸辛，至多，也不过是一点挣扎。
All of this is still far from the original proletarian literature, so all the works introduced are naturally screaming, groaning, being poor, bitter, and at most, it is just a little struggle.但已经使又一部分人很不高兴了，就招来了两标军马的围剿。创造社竖起了“为艺术的艺术”的大旗，喊着“自我表现”的口号，要用波斯诗人的酒杯，“黄书”文士的手杖，将这些“庸俗”打平。还有一标是那些受过了英国的小说在供绅士淑女的欣赏，美国的小说家在迎合读者的心思这些“文艺理论”的洗礼而回来的，一听到下层社会的叫唤和呻吟，就使他们眉头百结，扬起了带着白手套的纤手，挥斥道：这些下流都从“艺术之宫”里滚出去！
But it has already made another part of the people very unhappy, so they have attracted the encirclement and suppression of two standard troops and horses. The Creation Society raised the banner of "art for art", shouted the slogan of "self-expression", and used the wine glasses of Persian poets and the canes of "yellow books" scribes to level these "vulgarities". Another mark is that those who have received British novels for the appreciation of gentlemen and ladies, and American novelists who have come back from the baptism of these "literary and artistic theories" to cater to the minds of readers, as soon as they hear the cries and groans of the lower classes, they frown, raise their slender hands with white gloves, and scold: These obscene people are all out of the "palace of art"!而且中国原来还有着一标布满全国的旧式的军马，这就是以小说为“闲书”的人们。小说，是供“看官”们茶余酒后的消遣之用的，所以要优雅，超逸，万不可使读者不欢，打断他消闲的雅兴。此说虽古，但却与英美时行的小说论合流，于是这三标新旧的大军，就不约而同的来痛剿了“为人生的文学”——俄国文学。
Moreover, China originally had an old-style military horse all over the country, which is the people who use novels as "idle books". Novels are for the "officials" to have fun after tea and drinking, so they should be elegant and transcendent, and must not make the reader unhappy and interrupt his leisure and elegance. Although this theory is ancient, it merges with the novel theory of the British and American times, so these three new and old armies have invariably suppressed "literature for life" - Russian literature.然而还是有着不少共鸣的人们，所以它在中国仍然是宛转曲折的生长着。
However, there are still many people who resonate with it, so it is still growing in China.但它在本土，却突然凋零下去了。在这以前，原有许多作者企望着转变的，而十月革命的到来，却给了他们一个意外的莫大的打击。于是有梅垒什珂夫斯基夫妇（D. S. Merezhikovski i Z. N. Hippius），库普林（A. I. Kuprin），蒲宁（I. A. Bunin），安特来夫（L. N. Andreev）之流的逃亡，阿尔志跋绥夫（M. P. Artzy-bashev），梭罗古勃（Fiodor Sologub）之流的沉默，旧作家的还在活动者，只剩了勃留梭夫（Valeri Briusov），惠垒赛耶夫（V. Veresaiev），戈理基（Maxim Gorki），玛亚珂夫斯基（V. V. Mayakovski）这几个人，到后来，还回来了一个亚历舍·托尔斯泰（Aleksei N. Tolstoi）。此外也没有什么显著的新起的人物，在国内战争和列强封锁中的文苑，是只见萎谢和荒凉了。
But in the mainland, it suddenly withered. Before this, many original authors hoped for change, but the arrival of the October Revolution gave them an unexpected and great blow. So there were Mr. and Mrs. Mereshkovsky (D. S. Merezhikovski i Z. N. Hippius), Kuplin (A. I. Kuprin), I. Kuprin (I. Kuprin). A. Bunin), L. Anderson (L. Bunin) N. Andreev) and others, M. P. Artzy-bashev), Fiodor Sologub and others, and the old writers who are still active, only Valeri Briusov, V. Veresaiev), Maxim Gorki, Mayakovsky (V. V. Mayakovski), and later, returned an Aleksei N. Tolstoi. In addition, there are no significant new figures, and the literary garden in the civil war and the blockade of the great powers is only wilted and desolate.至一九二〇年顷，新经济政策实行了，造纸，印刷，出版等项事业的勃兴，也帮助了文艺的复活，这时的最重要的枢纽，是一个文学团体“绥拉比翁的兄弟们”（Serapionsbrüder）。
By 1920, the New Economic Policy had been implemented, and the rise of papermaking, printing, publishing and other undertakings also helped to revive literature and art, and the most important hub at this time was the literary group "Serapionsbrüder" (Brothers of Serapionsbrüder).这一派的出现，表面上是始于二一年二月一日，在列宁格拉“艺术府”里的第一回集会的，加盟者大抵是年青的文人，那立场是在一切立场的否定。淑雪兼珂说过：“从党人的观点看起来，我是没有宗旨的人物。这不很好么？自己说起自己来，则我既不是共产主义者，也不是社会革命党员，也不是帝制主义者。我只是一个俄国人，而且对于政治，是没有操持的。大概和我最相近的，是布尔塞维克，和他们一同布尔塞维克化，我是赞成的。……但我爱农民的俄国。”这就很明白的说出了他们的立场。
The emergence of this school ostensibly began on February 1, 21, at the first meeting in the Leningrad "Art House", and the members were probably young literati, and their position was the denial of all positions. Shuxue Jianke said: "From the point of view of the party members, I am a person without a purpose. Isn't that good? Speaking of myself, I am neither a communist, nor a member of the Socialist Revolutionary, nor an imperialist. I am just a Russian, and I have no control over politics. Probably the closest to me is the Bolsheviks, and I am in favor of the Bolsheviks with them. …… But I love peasant Russia. This clearly states their position.但在那时，这一个文学团体的出现，却确是一种惊异，不久就几乎席卷了全国的文坛。在苏联中，这样的非苏维埃的文学的勃兴，是很足以令人奇怪的。然而理由很简单：当时的革命者，正忙于实行，惟有这些青年文人发表了较为优秀的作品者其一；他们虽非革命者，而身历了铁和火的试练，所以凡所描写的恐怖和战栗，兴奋和感激，易得读者的共鸣者其二；其三，则当时指挥文学界的瓦浪斯基，是很给他们支持的。讬罗茨基也是支持者之一，称之为“同路人”。同路人者，谓因革命中所含有的英雄主义而接受革命，一同前行，但并无彻底为革命而斗争，虽死不惜的信念，仅是一时同道的伴侣罢了。这名称，由那时一直使用到现在。
But at that time, the emergence of this literary group was indeed a surprise, and soon it almost swept the literary world across the country. In the Soviet Union, the rise of such non-Soviet literature was strange. However, the reason is simple: the revolutionaries at that time were busy implementing it, and only these young literati published excellent works; Although they are not revolutionaries, they have experienced the trials of iron and fire, so the horror and trembling, excitement and gratitude described are easy to resonate with readers; Third, Walansky, who was in command of the literary world at that time, was very supportive of them. Rotsky was also one of the supporters, calling him a "fellow traveler". Fellow travelers are those who accept the revolution because of the heroism contained in the revolution and move forward together, but do not completely fight for the revolution. This name has been used since then until now.然而，单说是“爱文学”而没有明确的观念形态的徽帜的“绥拉比翁的兄弟们”，也终于逐渐失掉了作为团体的存在的意义，始于涣散，继以消亡，后来就和别的同路人们一样，各各由他个人的才力，受着文学上的评价了。
However, the "brothers of Surabión", who only "love literature" without a clear conceptual form, finally gradually lost the meaning of their existence as a group, began to disperse, then died, and later, like other fellow travelers, each was evaluated by literature according to his own personal talents.在四五年以前，中国又曾盛大的绍介了苏联文学，然而就是这同路人的作品居多。这也是无足异的。一者，此种文学的兴起较为在先，颇为西欧及日本所赏赞和介绍，给中国也得了不少转译的机缘；二者，恐怕也还是这种没有立场的立场，反而易得介绍者的赏识之故了，虽然他自以为是“革命文学者”。
Four or five years ago, China had introduced Soviet literature in a grand way, but most of the works were by this fellow traveler. This is also no surprise. First, the rise of this kind of literature was relatively early, and it was appreciated and introduced by Western Europe and Japan, and China also got a lot of opportunities for translation; Second, I am afraid that it is still this position without a position, but it is easy to gain the appreciation of the introducer, although he thinks he is a "revolutionary writer".我向来是想介绍东欧文学的一个人，也曾译过几篇同路人作品，现在就合了十个人的短篇为一集，其中的三篇，是别人的翻译，我相信为很可靠的。可惜的是限于篇幅，不能将有名的作家全都收罗在内，使这本书较为完善，但我相信曹靖华君的《烟袋》和《四十一》，是可以补这缺陷的。
I have always wanted to introduce Eastern European literature, and I have translated several works of fellow travelers, and now I have combined ten short stories into one episode, three of which are translations by others, which I believe are very reliable. Unfortunately, due to space limitations, it is not possible to include all famous writers to make this book more complete, but I believe that Cao Jinghuajun's "Tobacco Bag" and "Forty-One" can make up for this defect.至于各个作者的略传，和各篇作品的翻译或重译的来源，都写在卷末的《后记》里，读者倘有兴致，自去翻检就是了。
As for the brief biographies of each author and the sources of translations or retranslations of each work, they are all written in the "Postscript" at the end of the volume, and readers can check them if they are interested.一九三二年九月九日，鲁迅记于上海。
On September 9, 1932, Lu Xun recorded in Shanghai.

论“第三种人”

论“第三种人”

论“第三种人”

On the "third kind of person"这三年来，关于文艺上的论争是沉寂的，除了在指挥刀的保护之下，挂着“左翼”的招牌，在马克斯主义里发见了文艺自由论，列宁主义里找到了杀尽共匪说的论客的“理论”之外，几乎没有人能够开口，然而，倘是“为文艺而文艺”的文艺，却还是“自由”的，因为他决没有收了卢布的嫌疑。但在“第三种人”，就是“死抱住文学不放的人”，又不免有一种苦痛的豫感：左翼文坛要说他是“资产阶级的走狗”。
In the past three years, the debate on literature and art has been silent, except for the protection of the commanding knife, the "left-wing" signboard, the theory of literary and artistic freedom in Marxism, and the "theory" of the critics who kill all the communists in Leninism, almost no one can speak. But the "third type of person", that is, "the person who clings to literature", inevitably has a painful premonition: the left-wing literary world wants to say that he is a "lackey of the bourgeoisie".代表了这一种“第三种人”来鸣不平的，是《现代》杂志第三和第六期上的苏汶先生的文章（我在这里先应该声明：我为便利起见，暂且用了“代表”，“第三种人”这些字眼，虽然明知道苏汶先生的“作家之群”，是也如拒绝“或者”，“多少”，“影响”这一类不十分决定的字眼一样，不要固定的名称的，因为名称一固定，也就不自由了）。他以为左翼的批评家，动不动就说作家是“资产阶级的走狗”，甚至于将中立者认为非中立，而一非中立，便有认为“资产阶级的走狗”的可能，号称“左翼作家”者既然“左而不作”，“第三种人”又要作而不敢，于是文坛上便没有东西了。然而文艺据说至少有一部分是超出于阶级斗争之外的，为将来的，就是“第三种人”所抱住的真的，永久的文艺。——但可惜，被左翼理论家弄得不敢作了，因为作家在未作之前，就有了被骂的豫感。
Representing this "third type of person" is Mr. Su Wen's article in the third and sixth issues of "Modern" magazine (I should first state here: for the sake of convenience, I have temporarily used the words "representative" and "third type of person", although I know that Mr. Su Wen's "group of writers" is also like rejecting words such as "or", "how much", and "influence", and do not have a fixed name, because once the name is fixed, it is not free). He thought that left-wing critics would say that writers were "bourgeois lackeys" at every turn, and even regarded neutrals as non-neutral, and once they were non-neutral, there was a possibility that they would think they were "bourgeois lackeys". However, literature and art are said to be at least partly beyond the class struggle, and for the future, it is the real and permanent literature and art embraced by the "third kind of people". ——But unfortunately, I was made afraid by left-wing theorists, because the writer had a premonition of being scolded before he did it.我相信这种豫感是会有的，而以“第三种人”自命的作家，也愈加容易有。我也相信作者所说，现在很有懂得理论，而感情难变的作家。然而感情不变，则懂得理论的度数，就不免和感情已变或略变者有些不同，而看法也就因此两样。苏汶先生的看法，由我看来，是并不正确的。
I believe that this feeling will be there, and writers who call themselves "third people" are becoming more and more likely to have it. I also believe what the author said, there are now writers who understand theory and have difficult feelings to change. However, if the feelings remain unchanged, then understanding the degree of theory will inevitably be a little different from those whose feelings have changed or changed slightly, and the views are therefore different. Mr. Su Wen's view, in my opinion, is not correct.自然，自从有了左翼文坛以来，理论家曾经犯过错误，作家之中，也不但如苏汶先生所说，有“左而不作”的，并且还有由左而右，甚至于化为民族主义文学的小卒，书坊的老板，敌党的探子的，然而这些讨厌左翼文坛了的文学家所遗下的左翼文坛，却依然存在，不但存在，还在发展，克服自己的坏处，向文艺这神圣之地进军。苏汶先生问过：克服了三年，还没有克服好么？回答是：是的，还要克服下去，三十年也说不定。然而一面克服着，一面进军着，不会做待到克服完成，然后行进那样的傻事的。但是，苏汶先生说过“笑话”：左翼作家在从资本家取得稿费；现在我来说一句真话，是左翼作家还在受封建的资本主义的社会的法律的压迫，禁锢，杀戮。所以左翼刊物，全被摧残，现在非常寥寥，即偶有发表，批评作品的也绝少，而偶有批评作品的，也并未动不动便指作家为“资产阶级的走狗”，而且不要“同路人”。左翼作家并不是从天上掉下来的神兵，或国外杀进来的仇敌，他不但要那同走几步的“同路人”，还要招致那站在路旁看看的看客也一同前进。
Naturally, since the establishment of the left-wing literary world, theorists have made mistakes, and among the writers, not only are there those who "do not do on the left", as Mr. Su Wen said, but also from left to right, and even become pawns of nationalist literature, the owners of bookstores, and spies of the enemy party. Mr. Su Wen asked: After three years of overcoming, has it not been overcome? The answer is: Yes, it will take 30 years to overcome it. However, while overcoming, marching, they will not do such stupid things as waiting until the overcoming is completed. However, Mr. Su Wen said a "joke": left-wing writers are getting fees from capitalists; Now let me tell you the truth, left-wing writers are still oppressed, imprisoned, and killed by the laws of feudal capitalist society. Therefore, left-wing publications, all destroyed, are now very few, that is, they are occasionally published, and there are very few critics of works, and occasionally criticize works, and they do not refer to writers as "lackeys of the bourgeoisie" at every turn, and do not "fellow travelers". Left-wing writers are not divine soldiers who fall from the sky or enemies who come in from abroad, they not only want the "fellow travelers" who walk a few steps together, but also attract the spectators who stand on the side of the road to move forward together.但现在要问：左翼文坛现在因为受着压迫，不能发表很多的批评，倘一旦有了发表的可能，不至于动不动就指“第三种人”为“资产阶级的走狗”么？我想，倘若左翼批评家没有宣誓不说，又只从坏处着想，那是有这可能的，也可以想得比这还要坏。不过我以为这种豫测，实在和想到地球也许有破裂之一日，而先行自杀一样，大可以不必的。
But now I have to ask: the left-wing literary world is now oppressed and cannot publish a lot of criticism, if once there is a possibility of publication, will it not be called the "third kind of person" as a "bourgeois lackey" at every turn? I think that if left-wing critics do not swear and do not swear, and only think about the bad, it is possible, and it can be considered worse than this. However, I think this kind of prediction is really unnecessary, just like thinking that the earth may rupture one day and commit suicide first.然而苏汶先生的“第三种人”，却据说是为了这未来的恐怖而“搁笔”了。未曾身历，仅仅因为心造的幻影而搁笔，“死抱住文学不放”的作者的拥抱力，又何其弱呢？两个爱人，有因为豫防将来的社会上的斥责而不敢拥抱的么？
However, Mr. Su Wen's "third kind of person" is said to have "put down his pen" for the horror of this future. How weak is the embrace of the author who has never experienced it, just because of the phantom created by the heart, and "clings to literature"? Do the two lovers dare not hug because of the future social reprimand?其实，这“第三种人”的“搁笔”，原因并不在左翼批评的严酷。真实原因的所在，是在做不成这样的“第三种人”，做不成这样的人，也就没有了第三种笔，搁与不搁，还谈不到。
In fact, the reason for the "pen shelving" of this "third type of person" is not the harshness of left-wing criticism. The real reason is that if you can't be such a "third kind of person", if you can't be such a person, you won't have a third kind of pen, and you can't talk about it whether you put it aside or not.生在有阶级的社会里而要做超阶级的作家，生在战斗的时代而要离开战斗而独立，生在现在而要做给与将来的作品，这样的人，实在也是一个心造的幻影，在现实世界上是没有的。要做这样的人，恰如用自己的手拔着头发，要离开地球一样，他离不开，焦躁着，然而并非因为有人摇了摇头，使他不敢拔了的缘故。
Born in a class society and want to be a super-class writer, born in an era of fighting and want to leave the battle and become independent, born in the present and want to make works for the future, such a person is really a phantom made by the mind, which does not exist in the real world. To be such a person is like pulling out his hair with his own hands and leaving the earth, he cannot do without it, anxious, but not because someone shook his head and made him dare not pull it out.所以虽是“第三种人”，却还是一定超不出阶级的，苏汶先生就先在豫料阶级的批评了，作品里又岂能摆脱阶级的利害；也一定离不开战斗的，苏汶先生就先以“第三种人”之名提出抗争了，虽然“抗争”之名又为作者所不愿受；而且也跳不过现在的，他在创作超阶级的，为将来的作品之前，先就留心于左翼的批判了。
Therefore, although he is a "third kind of person", he still cannot transcend the class, and Mr. Su Wen first anticipates the criticism of the class, and how can he get rid of the interests of class in his works; It must be inseparable from the battle, so Mr. Su Wen first proposed to fight in the name of "the third kind of person", although the name of "resistance" was unwilling to be accepted by the author; And he can't skip the present, he pays attention to left-wing criticism before creating super-class, future works.这确是一种苦境。但这苦境，是因为幻影不能成为实有而来的。即使没有左翼文坛作梗，也不会有这“第三种人”，何况作品。但苏汶先生却又心造了一个横暴的左翼文坛的幻影，将“第三种人”的幻影不能出现，以至将来的文艺不能发生的罪孽，都推给它了。
This is indeed a difficult situation. But this predicament comes because the phantom cannot become real. Even if there is no left-wing literary obstruction, there will be no such "third kind of people", let alone works. But Mr. Su Wen has created a phantom of the tyrannical left-wing literary world, and pushed the phantom of the "third kind of person" to it, and even the sins that cannot occur in literature and art in the future.左翼作家诚然是不高超的，连环图画，唱本，然而也不到苏汶先生所断定那样的没出息。左翼也要托尔斯泰，弗罗培尔。但不要“努力去创造一些属于将来（因为他们现在是不要的）的东西”的托尔斯泰和弗罗培尔。他们两个，都是为现在而写的，将来是现在的将来，于现在有意义，才于将来会有意义。尤其是托尔斯泰，他写些小故事给农民看，也不自命为“第三种人”，当时资产阶级的多少攻击，终于不能使他“搁笔”。左翼虽然诚如苏汶先生所说，不至于蠢到不知道“连环图画是产生不出托尔斯泰，产生不出弗罗培尔来”，但却以为可以产出密开朗该罗，达文希那样伟大的画手。而且我相信，从唱本说书里是可以产生托尔斯泰，弗罗培尔的。现在提起密开朗该罗们的画来，谁也没有非议了，但实际上，那不是宗教的宣传画，《旧约》的连环图画么？而且是为了那时的“现在”的。
Left-wing writers are certainly not superb, comic strips, and songbooks, but they are not as unpromising as Mr. Su Wen concluded. The left also wants Tolstoy and Froppel. But don't "strive to create something that belongs to the future (because they don't want it now)" Tolstoy and Froppel. Both of them are written for the present, and the future is the future of the present, and it is meaningful in the present, and it will be meaningful in the future. Especially Tolstoy, he wrote some short stories to show the peasants, and did not call himself a "third kind of person", and the number of attacks by the bourgeoisie at that time finally could not make him "put down his pen". Although the left, as Mr. Su Wen said, is not so stupid that they do not know that "comic strips cannot produce Tolstoy or Fropel", they think that they can produce great painters like Michelangelo and Leonardo da Vinci. And I believe that Tolstoy and Fropel can be produced from the songbook. Now, when it comes to the paintings of Michelangelo, no one criticizes them, but in fact, isn't that a religious propaganda poster, a comic strip of the Old Testament? And for the "now" of that time.总括起来说，苏汶先生是主张“第三种人”与其欺骗，与其做冒牌货，倒还不如努力去创作，这是极不错的。
To sum up, Mr. Su Wen advocates that the "third kind of people" should work hard to create instead of deceiving and being impostors, which is very good.“定要有自信的勇气，才会有工作的勇气！”这尤其是对的。
"You must have the courage to be confident in order to have the courage to work!" This is especially true.然而苏汶先生又说，许多大大小小的“第三种人”们，却又因为豫感了不祥之兆——左翼理论家的批评而“搁笔”了！
However, Mr. Su Wen also said that many "third people", large and small, have "put down their pens" because they have foreshadowed the ominous sign, the criticism of left-wing theorists!“怎么办呢”？
"What should I do"?十月十日。
October 10th.

“连环图画”辩护

“连环图画”辩护

“连环图画”辩护

"Comic strip" defense我自己曾经有过这样一个小小的经验。有一天，在一处筵席上，我随便的说：用活动电影来教学生，一定比教员的讲义好，将来恐怕要变成这样的。话还没有说完，就埋葬在一阵哄笑里了。
I myself had such a small experience. One day, at a banquet, I casually said: Teaching students with activity films must be better than the teacher's handouts, and I am afraid it will become like this in the future. Before he finished speaking, he was buried in a burst of laughter.自然，这话里，是埋伏着许多问题的，例如，首先第一，是用的是怎样的电影，倘用美国式的发财结婚故事的影片，那当然不行。但在我自己，却的确另外听过采用影片的细菌学讲义，见过全部照相，只有几句说明的植物学书。所以我深信不但生物学，就是历史地理，也可以这样办。
Naturally, there are many questions lurking in this statement, for example, first of all, what kind of movie is used, if you use an American-style film about a rich marriage story, of course not. But myself, I have indeed heard of bacteriology handouts using films, and I have seen botany books with all the photos and only a few sentences of explanation. Therefore, I firmly believe that not only biology, but also history and geography can also do the same.然而许多人的随便的哄笑，是一枝白粉笔，它能够将粉涂在对手的鼻子上，使他的话好像小丑的打诨。
However, the casual laughter of many people is a white chalk that can apply powder to the opponent's nose, making his words look like a clown's joke.前几天，我在《现代》上看见苏汶先生的文章，他以中立的文艺论者的立场，将“连环图画”一笔抹杀了。自然，那不过是随便提起的，并非讨论绘画的专门文字，然而在青年艺术学徒的心中，也许是一个重要的问题，所以我再来说几句。
A few days ago, I saw Mr. Su Wen's article in "Modern", and he erased the "comic strip" from the standpoint of a neutral literary and art theorist. Naturally, it is just a casual mention, not a special text to discuss painting, but in the minds of young art apprentices, it may be an important issue, so I will say a few more words.我们看惯了绘画史的插图上，没有“连环图画”，名人的作品的展览会上，不是“罗马夕照”，就是“西湖晚凉”，便以为那是一种下等物事，不足以登“大雅之堂”的。但若走进意大利的教皇宫——我没有游历意大利的幸福，所走进的自然只是纸上的教皇宫——去，就能看见凡有伟大的壁画，几乎都是《旧约》，《耶稣传》，《圣者传》的连环图画，艺术史家截取其中的一段，印在书上，题之曰《亚当的创造》，《最后之晚餐》，读者就不觉得这是下等，这在宣传了，然而那原画，却明明是宣传的连环图画。
We are used to seeing illustrations in the history of painting, there is no "comic strip", and the exhibition of famous people's works is either "Roman sunset" or "West Lake evening coolness", so we think that it is a kind of inferior thing, not enough to enter the "Hall of Elegance". But if you walk into the Papal Palace in Italy - I did not travel to Italy with happiness, and what I walked into was naturally only the Papal Palace on paper - you can see that almost all the great frescoes are comic strips of the Old Testament, the Biography of Jesus, and the Biography of the Saints.在东方也一样。印度的阿强陀石窟，经英国人摹印了壁画以后，在艺术史上发光了；中国的《孔子圣迹图》，只要是明版的，也早为收藏家所宝重。这两样，一是佛陀的本生，一是孔子的事迹，明明是连环图画，而且是宣传。
The same is true in the East. The Achanta Grottoes in India shone in the history of art after the British copied the murals; China's "Confucius Sacred Relics", as long as it is a Ming edition, has long been treasured by collectors. These two, one is the Buddha's Jataka, and the other is the deeds of Confucius, which are obviously comic strips and propaganda.书籍的插画，原意是在装饰书籍，增加读者的兴趣的，但那力量，能补助文字之所不及，所以也是一种宣传画。这种画的幅数极多的时候，即能只靠图像，悟到文字的内容，和文字一分开，也就成了独立的连环图画。最显著的例子是法国的陀莱（Gustave Doré），他是插图版画的名家，最有名的是《神曲》，《失乐园》，《吉诃德先生》，还有《十字军记》的插画，德国都有单印本（前二种在日本也有印本），只靠略解，即可以知道本书的梗概。然而有谁说陀莱不是艺术家呢？
The original intention of book illustrations is to decorate books and increase readers' interest, but that power can make up for what words cannot reach, so it is also a kind of propaganda poster. When the number of such paintings is extremely large, it can only rely on images to realize the content of the text, and once it is separated from the text, it becomes an independent comic strip. The most notable example is Gustave Doré of France, who is a famous illustrator of printmaking, the most famous is "The Divine Comedy", "Paradise Lost", "Mr. Quixote", and the illustrations of "Crusade", both of which are in single print in Germany (the first two are also printed in Japan), and you can know the outline of the book only by a little explanation. But who says that Torai is not an artist?宋人的《唐风图》和《耕织图》，现在还可找到印本和石刻；至于仇英的《飞燕外传图》和《会真记图》，则翻印本就在文明书局发卖的。凡这些，也都是当时和现在的艺术品。
The Song people's "Tang Feng Tu" and "Cultivation and Weaving Map" can still be found in prints and stone carvings; As for Qiu Ying's "Feiyan Gaiden Tu" and "Huizhen Ji Tu", the reprints were sold at the Civilization Bookstore. All of these are works of art at that time and now.自十九世纪后半以来，版画复兴了，许多作家，往往喜欢刻印一些以几幅画汇成一帖的“连作”（Blattfolge）。这些连作，也有并非一个事件的。现在为青年的艺术学徒计，我想写出几个版画史上已经有了地位的作家和有连续事实的作品在下面：
Since the second half of the nineteenth century, printmaking has been revived, and many writers often like to engrave some "Blattfolge" (Blattfolge), which is a combination of several paintings. These series of works are also not an event. Now for the art apprenticeship of young people, I would like to write a few works that have established themselves in the history of printmaking and have continuous facts below:首先应该举出来的是德国的珂勒惠支（Käthe Kollwitz）夫人。她除了为霍普德曼的《织匠》（Die Weber）而刻的六幅版画外，还有三种，有题目，无说明——
The first thing that should be mentioned is Mrs. Käthe Kollwitz of Germany. In addition to the six prints she engraved for Hopdemann's "Die Weber", there are three more types, with titles and no descriptions -一，《农民斗争》（Bauernkrieg），金属版七幅；
1. "Peasant Struggle" (Bauernkrieg), seven metal plates;二，《战争》（Der Krieg），木刻七幅；
2. "War" (Der Krieg), seven woodcuts;三，《无产者》（Proletariat），木刻三幅。
3. "Proletariat", three woodcuts.以《士敏土》的版画，为中国所知道的梅斐尔德（Carl Meffert），是一个新进的青年作家，他曾为德译本斐格纳尔的《猎俄皇记》（Die Jagd nach Zaren von Wera Figner）刻过五幅木版图，又有两种连作——
Carl Meffert, known in China for his prints of "Shimin Tu", is a new young writer who has engraved five woodblock prints for the German translation of Fignaar's "Die Jagd nach Zaren von Wera Figner" (Die Jagd nach Zaren von Wera Figner), and there are two consecutive works -一，《你的姊妹》（Deine Schwester），木刻七幅，题诗一幅；
1. "Your Sister" (Deine Schwester), seven woodcuts, one poem;二，《养护的门徒》（原名未详），木刻十三幅。
2. "Disciple of Conservation" (original name unknown), thirteen woodcuts.比国有一个麦绥莱勒（Frans Masereel），是欧洲大战时候，像罗曼罗兰一样，因为非战而逃出过外国的。他的作品最多，都是一本书，只有书名，连小题目也没有。现在德国印出了普及版（Bei Kurt Wolff，München），每本三马克半，容易到手了。我所见过的是这几种——
Belgium has a Frans Masereel, who, like Romain Rolland, fled abroad because of non-war during the European War. His most works are all books, only book titles, not even subtitles. Now Germany has printed a popular version (Bei Kurt Wolff, München), each three and a half marks, which is easy to get. What I have seen is these-一，《理想》（Die Idee），木刻八十三幅；
1. "Die Idee", 83 woodcuts;二，《我的祷告》（Mein Stundenbuch），木刻一百六十五幅；
2. "Mein Stundenbuch", 165 woodcuts;三，《没字的故事》（Geschichte ohne Worte），木刻六十幅；
3. "The Story Without Words" (Geschichte ohne Worte), 60 woodcuts;四，《太阳》（Die Sonne），木刻六十三幅；
4. "Sun" (Die Sonne), 63 woodcuts;五，《工作》（Das Werk），木刻，幅数失记；
5. "Work" (Das Werk), woodcut, number of errors;六，《一个人的受难》（Die Passion eines Menschen），木刻二十五幅。
6. "Die Passion eines Menschen" (Die Passion eines Menschen), 25 woodcuts.美国作家的作品，我曾见过希该尔木刻的《巴黎公社》（The Paris Commune，A Story in Pictures by William Siegel），是纽约的约翰李特社（John Reed Club）出版的。还有一本石版的格罗沛尔（W. Gropper）所画的书，据赵景深教授说，是“马戏的故事”，另译起来，恐怕要“信而不顺”，只好将原名照抄在下面——
The work of an American writer, I have seen in the woodcut "The Paris Commune, A Story in Pictures by William Siegel", was published by the John Reed Club in New York. There is also a lithograph of W. Gropel (W. Gropper), according to Professor Zhao Jingshen, is a "circus story", and when translated separately, I am afraid that it will be "believed but not smooth", so I have to copy the original name below——《Alay-Oop》（Life and Love Among the Acrobats.）
《Alay-Oop》（Life and Love Among the Acrobats.）英国的作家我不大知道，因为那作品定价贵。但曾经有一本小书，只有十五幅木刻和不到二百字的说明，作者是有名的吉宾斯（Robert Gibbings），限印五百部，英国绅士是死也不肯重印的，现在恐怕已将绝版，每本要数十元了罢。那书是——
I don't know much about British writers because they are expensive. But there was once a small book, only fifteen woodcuts and less than 200 words of instructions, the author was the famous Robert Gibbings, limited to 500 copies, British gentlemen refused to reprint even if they died, and now I am afraid it will be out of print, each cost tens of yuan. That book is—《第七人》（The 7th Man）。
"The 7th Man".以上，我的意思是总算举出事实，证明了连环图画不但可以成为艺术，并且已经坐在“艺术之宫”的里面了。至于这也和其他的文艺一样，要有好的内容和技术，那是不消说得的。
What I mean above is that the facts have finally been cited to prove that comic strips can not only become art, but also sit in the "palace of art". As for this, like other literature and art, it goes without saying that it must have good content and technology.我并不劝青年的艺术学徒蔑弃大幅的油画或水彩画，但是希望一样看重并且努力于连环图画和书报的插图；自然应该研究欧洲名家的作品，但也更注意于中国旧书上的绣像和画本，以及新的单张的花纸。这些研究和由此而来的创作，自然没有现在的所谓大作家的受着有些人们的照例的叹赏，然而我敢相信：对于这，大众是要看的，大众是感激的！
I do not advise young art apprentices to abandon large-scale oil paintings or watercolors, but I hope to value and strive for comic strips and illustrations in books and newspapers; Naturally, we should study the works of famous European artists, but we should also pay more attention to the embroidery and painting books in old Chinese books, as well as the new single flower paper. These studies and the resulting creations are naturally not as admired by some people as the current so-called great writers, but I dare to believe that the public wants to see this, and the public is grateful!十月二十五日。
October 25th.

辱骂和恐吓决不是战斗

辱骂和恐吓决不是战斗

辱骂和恐吓决不是战斗

Abuse and intimidation are never fights——致《文学月报》编辑的一封信
——A letter to the editor of "Literary Monthly"起应兄：
Brother Qiying:前天收到《文学月报》第四期，看了一下。我所觉得不足的，并非因为它不及别种杂志的五花八门，乃是总还不能比先前充实。但这回提出了几位新的作家来，是极好的，作品的好坏我且不论，最近几年的刊物上，倘不是姓名曾经排印过了的作家，就很有不能登载的趋势，这么下去，新的作者要没有发表作品的机会了。现在打破了这局面，虽然不过是一种月刊的一期，但究竟也扫去一些沉闷，所以我以为是一种好事情。但是，我对于芸生先生的一篇诗，却非常失望。
The day before yesterday, I received the fourth issue of "Literary Monthly" and read it. What I find lacking is not that it is not as diverse as other magazines, but that it is not as substantial as before. But this time several new writers are proposed, which is excellent, regardless of the quality of the work, in recent years, if it is not a writer whose name has been printed, there is a tendency not to publish it, so if it continues, the new author will not have the opportunity to publish his work. Now that this situation has been broken, although it is just an issue of a monthly magazine, it has also swept away some of the dullness, so I think it is a good thing. However, I was very disappointed with a poem by Mr. Yunsheng.这诗，一目了然，是看了前一期的别德纳衣的讽刺诗而作的。然而我们来比一比罢，别德纳衣的诗虽然自认为“恶毒”，但其中最甚的也不过是笑骂。这诗怎么样？有辱骂，有恐吓，还有无聊的攻击：其实是大可以不必作的。
This poem, which is clear at a glance, was written after reading the satirical poem of Bednar Yi in the previous issue. However, let's compare, although Bedner's poems consider themselves "vicious", the worst of them is just laughter and scolding. How about this poem? There are abuses, intimidation, and boring attacks: in fact, it is not necessary.例如罢，开首就是对于姓的开玩笑。一个作者自取的别名，自然可以窥见他的思想，譬如“铁血”，“病鹃”之类，固不妨由此开一点小玩笑。但姓氏籍贯，却不能决定本人的功罪，因为这是从上代传下来的，不能由他自主。我说这话还在四年之前，当时曾有人评我为“封建余孽”，其实是捧住了这样的题材，欣欣然自以为得计者，倒是十分“封建的”的。不过这种风气，近几年颇少见了，不料现在竟又复活起来，这确不能不说是一个退步。
For example, the beginning is a joke about the surname. An author's own alias can naturally give a glimpse of his thoughts, such as "iron-blooded", "sick cuckoo", etc., so you might as well make a little joke about it. However, the surname and place of origin cannot determine one's merits and faults, because this is passed down from the previous generation and cannot be independently by him. I said this four years ago, when someone commented that I was a "feudal remnant", but in fact, it was very "feudal" to hold such a theme and happily think that it was a good idea. However, this kind of atmosphere has been quite rare in recent years, but now it has been revived, which cannot but be said to be a step backwards.尤其不堪的是结末的辱骂。现在有些作品，往往并非必要而偏在对话里写上许多骂语去，好像以为非此便不是无产者作品，骂詈愈多，就愈是无产者作品似的。其实好的工农之中，并不随口骂人的多得很，作者不应该将上海流氓的行为，涂在他们身上的。即使有喜欢骂人的无产者，也只是一种坏脾气，作者应该由文艺加以纠正，万不可再来展开，使将来的无阶级社会中，一言不合，便祖宗三代的闹得不可开交。况且即是笔战，就也如别的兵战或拳斗一样，不妨伺隙乘虚，以一击制敌人的死命，如果一味鼓噪，已是《三国志演义》式战法，至于骂一句爹娘，扬长而去，还自以为胜利，那简直是“阿Q”式的战法了。
Especially unbearable is the insults at the end. Nowadays, some works are often unnecessary and often write a lot of scolding in the dialogue, as if thinking that it is not a proletarian work, and the more scolding, the more it is a proletarian work. In fact, among the good workers and peasants, there are not many people who scold people casually, and the author should not apply the behavior of Shanghai hooligans to them. Even if there are proletarians who like to scold people, it is just a bad temper, and the author should correct it by literature and art, and must not unfold it again, so that in the future classless society, if there is a disagreement, the three generations of ancestors will be in trouble. Moreover, even if it is a pen battle, it is like other military battles or fist fights, you might as well wait for an opportunity to take advantage of the situation and control the enemy's death with one blow, if you blindly shout, it is already a "Romance of the Three Kingdoms" style of tactics, as for scolding a parent, walking away, and thinking that you are victorious, it is simply a "Ah Q" style of tactics.接着又是什么“剖西瓜”之类的恐吓，这也是极不对的，我想。无产者的革命，乃是为了自己的解放和消灭阶级，并非因为要杀人，即使是正面的敌人，倘不死于战场，就有大众的裁判，决不是一个诗人所能提笔判定生死的。现在虽然很有什么“杀人放火”的传闻，但这只是一种诬陷。中国的报纸上看不出实话，然而只要一看别国的例子也就可以恍然：德国的无产阶级革命（虽然没有成功），并没有乱杀人；俄国不是连皇帝的宫殿都没有烧掉么？而我们的作者，却将革命的工农用笔涂成一个吓人的鬼脸，由我看来，真是卤莽之极了。
Then there is some kind of intimidation such as "splitting watermelon", which is also extremely wrong, I think. The revolution of the proletariat is for its own liberation and the elimination of the class, not because it wants to kill, even if it is a frontal enemy, if it does not die on the battlefield, there will be the judgment of the masses, and it is by no means something that a poet can write to judge life and death. Although there are many rumors of "murder and arson" now, this is just a false accusation. The truth cannot be seen in Chinese newspapers, but as long as you look at the examples of other countries, you can suddenly understand: the German proletarian revolution (although it was not successful) did not kill people indiscriminately; Didn't Russia even burn down the emperor's palace? Our author, on the other hand, painted a frightening grimace with the pen of the revolutionary workers and peasants, which, in my opinion, is really reckless.自然，中国历来的文坛上，常见的是诬陷，造谣，恐吓，辱骂，翻一翻大部的历史，就往往可以遇见这样的文章，直到现在，还在应用，而且更加厉害。但我想，这一份遗产，还是都让给叭儿狗文艺家去承受罢，我们的作者倘不竭力的抛弃了它，是会和他们成为“一丘之貉”的。
Naturally, in China's literary circles, it is common to frame, spread rumors, intimidate, insult, and look through most of the history, and you can often encounter such articles, which are still being applied until now, and they are even more powerful. But I think that this inheritance should still be borne by the Ba'ergou writers and artists, and if our authors do not try their best to abandon it, they will become "a raccoon dog on a hill".不过我并非主张要对敌人陪笑脸，三鞠躬。我只是说，战斗的作者应该注重于“论争”；倘在诗人，则因为情不可遏而愤怒，而笑骂，自然也无不可。但必须止于嘲笑，止于热骂，而且要“喜笑怒骂，皆成文章”，使敌人因此受伤或致死，而自己并无卑劣的行为，观者也不以为污秽，这才是战斗的作者的本领。
But I am not advocating smiling and bowing three times to the enemy. I am just saying that the author of the battle should focus on the "argument"; If it is a poet, it is natural to be angry because of the uncontrollable emotion, and laugh and scold. But it must stop at ridicule, stop at scolding, and "laugh and curse, all become articles", so that the enemy is injured or killed because of this, and he has no despicable behavior, and the viewer does not think it is dirty, which is the skill of the author of the battle.刚才想到了以上的一些，便写出寄上，也许于编辑上可供参考。总之，我是极希望此后的《文学月报》上不再有那样的作品的。
I just thought of some of the above, so I wrote it down and sent it, maybe it can be used as an editorial reference. In short, I really hope that there will be no more such works in the "Literary Monthly" in the future.专此布达，并问
Specifically for this announcement, ask questions好。
Good.鲁迅。十二月十日。
Lu Xun. December 10th.

《自选集》自序

《自选集》自序

《自选集》自序

"Selected Collection" self-introduction我做小说，是开手于一九一八年，《新青年》上提倡“文学革命”的时候的。这一种运动，现在固然已经成为文学史上的陈迹了，但在那时，却无疑地是一个革命的运动。
I started writing novels in 1918, when "New Youth" advocated a "literary revolution". Although this movement has now become a relic in the history of literature, it was undoubtedly a revolutionary movement at that time.我的作品在《新青年》上，步调是和大家大概一致的，所以我想，这些确可以算作那时的“革命文学”。
My works on "New Youth" are roughly the same as everyone else, so I think these can indeed be counted as "revolutionary literature" at that time.然而我那时对于“文学革命”，其实并没有怎样的热情。见过辛亥革命，见过二次革命，见过袁世凯称帝，张勋复辟，看来看去，就看得怀疑起来，于是失望，颓唐得很了。民族主义的文学家在今年的一种小报上说，“鲁迅多疑”，是不错的，我正在疑心这批人们也并非真的民族主义文学者，变化正未可限量呢。不过我却又怀疑于自己的失望，因为我所见过的人们，事件，是有限得很的，这想头，就给了我提笔的力量。
However, I didn't have much enthusiasm for the "literary revolution" at that time. I have seen the Xinhai Revolution, I have seen the Second Revolution, I have seen Yuan Shikai proclaimed himself emperor, and Zhang Xun has been restored. Nationalist writers said in a tabloid this year, "Lu Xun is suspicious", which is good, but I am suspicious that this group of people is not really nationalist writers, and the changes are limitless. However, I doubted my own disappointment, because the people and events I had seen were very limited, and this thought gave me the strength to write a pen.“绝望之为虚妄，正与希望相同。”
“绝望之为虚妄，正与希望相同。 ”既不是直接对于“文学革命”的热情，又为什么提笔的呢？想起来，大半倒是为了对于热情者们的同感。这些战士，我想，虽在寂寞中，想头是不错的，也来喊几声助助威罢。首先，就是为此。自然，在这中间，也不免夹杂些将旧社会的病根暴露出来，催人留心，设法加以疗治的希望。但为达到这希望计，是必须与前驱者取同一的步调的，我于是删削些黑暗，装点些欢容，使作品比较的显出若干亮色，那就是后来结集起来的《呐喊》，一共有十四篇。
It is not a direct enthusiasm for the "literary revolution", so why did you write it? Come to think of it, most of it is for the sympathy of the enthusiasts. These soldiers, I think, although in loneliness, think well, and come to shout a few cheers. First of all, it is for this. Naturally, in the middle, there is inevitably some hope that the root cause of the old society will be exposed, and people will be careful and try to cure it. But in order to achieve this hope, it was necessary to keep pace with the pioneers, so I cut out some darkness and decorated some joy, so that the work showed a few bright colors, that is, "The Scream", which was later compiled, a total of fourteen pieces.这些也可以说，是“遵命文学”。不过我所遵奉的，是那时革命的前驱者的命令，也是我自己所愿意遵奉的命令，决不是皇上的圣旨，也不是金元和真的指挥刀。
These can also be said to be "obedience literature". However, what I obeyed was the order of the pioneers of the revolution at that time, and it was also the order I was willing to obey, by no means the emperor's imperial decree, nor was it Jin Yuanhe's real commanding knife.后来《新青年》的团体散掉了，有的高升，有的退隐，有的前进，我又经验了一回同一战阵中的伙伴还是会这么变化，并且落得一个“作家”的头衔，依然在沙漠中走来走去，不过已经逃不出在散漫的刊物上做文字，叫作随便谈谈。有了小感触，就写些短文，夸大点说，就是散文诗，以后印成一本，谓之《野草》。得到较整齐的材料，则还是做短篇小说，只因为成了游勇，布不成阵了，所以技术虽然比先前好一些，思路也似乎较无拘束，而战斗的意气却冷得不少。新的战友在那里呢？我想，这是很不好的。于是集印了这时期的十一篇作品，谓之《彷徨》，愿以后不再这模样。
Later, the group of "New Youth" dispersed, some were promoted, some retired, and some moved forward, and I experienced that my partners in the same battlefield would still change like this, and ended up with the title of "writer", still walking around in the desert, but I could not escape writing in scattered publications, which was called casual talk. If you have a small feeling, write some short articles, exaggerate it, that is, prose poems, and later print them into a book, called "Weeds". If you get more neat materials, you will still make short stories, just because you have become a wandering warrior and you can't form a formation, so although the technology is better than before, the thinking seems to be more unrestrained, and the fighting spirit is a lot colder. Where are the new comrades-in-arms? I think this is very bad. So he collected and printed eleven works from this period, called "Wandering", hoping that he would not look like this again in the future.“路漫漫其修远兮，吾将上下而求索。”
"The road is long and long, and I will search up and down."不料这大口竟夸得无影无踪。逃出北京，躲进厦门，只在大楼上写了几则《故事新编》和十篇《朝花夕拾》。前者是神话，传说及史实的演义，后者则只是回忆的记事罢了。
Unexpectedly, this big mouth was boasted without a trace. escaped from Beijing and hid in Xiamen, and only wrote a few "New Stories" and ten "Morning Flowers and Evening Collections" on the building. The former is a romance of myths, legends and historical facts, while the latter is just a memory of memories.此后就一无所作，“空空如也”。
After that, he did nothing, "empty".可以勉强称为创作的，在我至今只有这五种，本可以顷刻读了的，但出版者要我自选一本集。推测起来，恐怕因为这么一办，一者能够节省读者的费用，二则，以为由作者自选，该能比别人格外明白罢。对于第一层，我没有异议；至第二层，我却觉得也很难。因为我向来就没有格外用力或格外偷懒的作品，所以也没有自以为特别高妙，配得上提拔出来的作品。没有法，就将材料，写法，都有些不同，可供读者参考的东西，取出二十二篇来，凑成了一本，但将给读者一种“重压之感”的作品，却特地竭力抽掉了。这是我现在自有我的想头的：
It can be barely called creation, but I only have these five so far, and I could have read it in an instant, but the publisher asked me to choose a collection of my own. I speculate that because of this, one can save the reader's money, and the other is that the author chooses himself, which should be more understandable than others. For the first layer, I have no objection; On the second floor, I find it difficult. Because I have never had works that are particularly hard or lazy, I do not think that works are particularly exquisite and worthy of being promoted. There is no way, so the materials and writing methods are a little different, and the things that can be used for readers' reference are taken out and made into a book, but the works that will give readers a "sense of pressure" are specially removed. This is what I have my own thoughts now:“并不愿将自以为苦的寂寞，再来传染给也如我那年青时候似的正做着好梦的青年。”
"I don't want to infect the loneliness I think is suffering to young people who are dreaming like I did when I was young."然而这又不似做那《呐喊》时候的故意的隐瞒，因为现在我相信，现在和将来的青年是不会有这样的心境的了。
However, this is not like the deliberate concealment when doing "The Scream", because now I believe that young people now and in the future will not have such a state of mind.一九三二年十二月十四日，鲁迅于上海寓居记。
On December 14, 1932, Lu Xun lived in Shanghai.

《两地书》序言

《两地书》序言

《两地书》序言

Preface to the Book of Two Places这一本书，是这样地编起来的 ——
This book is compiled like this -一九三二年八月五日，我得到霁野，静农，丛芜三个人署名的信，说漱园于八月一日晨五时半，病殁于北平同仁医院了，大家想搜集他的遗文，为他出一本纪念册，问我这里可还藏有他的信札没有。这真使我的心突然紧缩起来。因为，首先，我是希望着他能够痊愈的，虽然明知道他大约未必会好；其次，是我虽然明知道他未必会好，却有时竟没有想到，也许将他的来信统统毁掉了，那些伏在枕上，一字字写出来的信。
On August 5, 1932, I received a letter signed by Jiye, Jingnong, and Cong Wu, saying that Shuyuan died of illness at 5:30 a.m. on August 1 in Tongren Hospital in Peking. This really made my heart shrink suddenly. Because, first of all, I hope that he will be cured, although I know that he may not be well; Secondly, although I knew that he might not be good, sometimes I didn't expect that I might destroy all his letters, those letters that were written word by word on the pillow.我的习惯，对于平常的信，是随复随毁的，但其中如果有些议论，有些故事，也往往留起来。直到近三年，我才大烧毁了两次。
My habit is to destroy ordinary letters at will, but if there are some discussions and stories, they are often kept. It wasn't until the past three years that I burned it twice.五年前，国民党清党的时候，我在广州，常听到因为捕甲，从甲这里看见乙的信，于是捕乙，又从乙家搜得丙的信，于是连丙也捕去了，都不知道下落。古时候有牵牵连连的“瓜蔓抄”，我是知道的，但总以为这是古时候的事，直到事实给了我教训，我才分明省悟了做今人也和做古人一样难。然而我还是漫不经心，随随便便，待到一九三〇年我签名于自由大同盟，浙江省党部呈请中央通缉“堕落文人鲁迅等”的时候，我在弃家出走之前，忽然心血来潮，将朋友给我的信都毁掉了。这并非为了消灭“谋为不轨”的痕迹，不过以为因通信而累及别人，是很无谓的，况且中国的衙门是谁都知道只要一碰着，就有多么的可怕。后来逃过了这一关，搬了寓，而信札又积起来，我又随随便便了，不料一九三一年一月，柔石被捕，在他的衣袋里搜出有我名字的东西来，因此听说就在找我。自然罗，我只得又弃家出走，但这回是心血来潮得更加明白，当然先将所有信札完全烧掉了。
Five years ago, when the Kuomintang was purging the party, I was in Guangzhou, and I often heard that because of the arrest of A, I saw B's letter from A, so I arrested B, and found C's letter from B's house, so even C was arrested, and I didn't know his whereabouts. In ancient times, there were implicated "melon vine copying", I knew it, but I always thought that this was an ancient thing, until the facts taught me a lesson, I clearly realized that being a modern person is as difficult as being an ancient person. However, I was still careless and casual, and when I signed the Freedom League in 1930 and the Zhejiang Provincial Party Department petitioned the central government to arrest "degenerate literati Lu Xun and others", I suddenly destroyed all the letters my friend gave me on a whim before I ran away from home. This is not to eliminate the traces of "conspiracy", but it is very meaningless to think that it will affect others because of communication, and everyone in China's yamen knows how terrible it is as long as they touch it. Unexpectedly, in January 1931, Rou Shi was arrested and found something with my name in his pocket, so I heard that he was looking for me. Naturally, I had to run away from home again, but this time it was a whim to understand better, of course, I burned all the letters completely.因为有过这样的两回事，所以一得到北平的来信，我就担心，怕大约未必有，但还是翻箱倒箧的寻了一通，果然无踪无影。朋友的信一封也没有，我们自己的信倒寻出来了。这也并非对于自己的东西特别看作宝贝，倒是因为那时时间很有限，而自己的信至多也不过蔓在自身上，因此放下了的。此后这些信又在枪炮的交叉火线下，躺了二三十天，也一点没有损失。其中虽然有些缺少，但恐怕是自己当时没有留心， 早经遗失，并不是由于什么官灾兵燹的。
Because of these two things, as soon as I got a letter from Peiping, I was worried, afraid that it might not be there, but I still rummaged through the boxes and found it, and sure enough, there was no trace. There was not a single letter from a friend, but our own letter was found. This is not because he regards his own things as treasures, but because time was very limited at that time, and his letters were only on himself at most, so he let go. After that, these letters lay under the crossfire of guns and guns for twenty or thirty days, and there was no loss at all. Although there are some shortcomings, I am afraid that I did not pay attention at that time, and it was lost early, not due to some official disaster.一个人如果一生没有遇到横祸，大家决不另眼相看，但若坐过牢监，到过战场，则即使他是一个万分平凡的人，人们也总看得特别一点。我们对于这些信，也正是这样。先前是一任他垫在箱子底下的，但现在一想起他曾经几乎要打官司，要遭炮火，就觉得他好像有些特别，有些可爱似的了。夏夜多蚊，不能静静的写字，我们便略照年月，将他编了起来，因地而分为三集，统名之曰《两地书》。
If a person has not encountered a misfortune in his life, everyone will never look at him differently, but if he has been in prison and on the battlefield, even if he is an extremely ordinary person, people will always look at him specially. That's exactly what we do with these letters. He used to be under the box, but now when he remembers that he was almost going to a lawsuit and being fired, he felt that he was a little special and cute. There are many mosquitoes on summer nights, and we can't write quietly, so we compiled him according to the years, divided into three episodes according to the place, collectively called "Book of Two Places".这是说：这一本书，在我们自己，一时是有意思的，但对于别人，却并不如此。其中既没有死呀活呀的热情，也没有花呀月呀的佳句；文辞呢，我们都未曾研究过“尺牍精华”或“书信作法”，只是信笔写来，大背文律，活该进“文章病院”的居多。所讲的又不外乎学校风潮，本身情况，饭菜好坏，天气阴晴，而最坏的是我们当日居漫天幕中，幽明莫辨，讲自己的事倒没有什么，但一遇到推测天下大事，就不免胡涂得很，所以凡有欢欣鼓舞之词，从现在看起来，大抵成了梦呓了。如果定要恭维这一本书的特色，那么，我想，恐怕是因为他的平凡罢。这样平凡的东西，别人大概是不会有，即有也未必存留的，而我们不然，这就只好谓之也是一种特色。
This means that this book is interesting for a while, but not for others. There is neither the enthusiasm of death or life, nor the good sentences of flowers and moons; As for the writing, we have never studied the "essence of the ruler" or "the method of letters", but most of them are written with a letter pen, and they deserve to be in the "literary hospital". What is said is nothing more than the school trend, its own situation, the quality of the food, the weather is cloudy, and the worst thing is that we live in the sky that day, it is indistinguishable, and there is nothing to talk about ourselves, but when we encounter speculation about the major events in the world, we will inevitably be very foolish, so whenever there are words of joy and encouragement, from now on, it seems that it has probably become a dream. If I had to compliment the characteristics of this book, then, I think, it was probably because of his ordinaryness. Such an ordinary thing is probably not something that others will have, and even if it exists, it may not exist, but we don't, so we have to call it a characteristic.然而奇怪的是竟又会有一个书店愿意来印这一本书。要印，印去就是，这倒仍然可以随随便便，不过因此也就要和读者相见了，却使我又得加上两点声明在这里，以免误解。其一，是：我现在是左翼作家联盟中之一人，看近来书籍的广告，大有凡作家一旦向左，则旧作也即飞升，连他孩子时代的啼哭也合于革命文学之概，不过我们的这书是不然的，其中并无革命气息。其二，常听得有人说，书信是最不掩饰，最显真面的文章，但我也并不，我无论给谁写信，最初，总是敷敷衍衍，口是心非的，即在这一本中，遇有较为紧要的地方，到后来也还是往往故意写得含胡些，因为我们所处，是在“当地长官”，邮局，校长……，都可以随意检查信件的国度里。但自然，明白的话，是也不少的。
However, it is strange that there will be another bookstore willing to print this book. If you want to print it, you can still do it casually, but because of this, you have to meet the reader, but I have to add two more statements here to avoid misunderstanding. First, I am now a member of the Left-wing Writers' Union, and when I read the advertisements for books recently, I found that once a writer goes to the left, his old works will soar, and even the crying of his childhood is in line with the general idea of revolutionary literature, but this is not the case with our book, there is no revolutionary atmosphere in it. Second, I often hear people say that letters are the most unabashed and sincere articles, but I am not, no matter who I write to, at first, I am always perfunctory and duplicitous, that is, in this book, when there is a more important place, I often write deliberately in a nonsense, because we are in a country where "local governors", post offices, principals, ......, can check letters at will. But naturally, if you understand, there are quite a few.还有一点，是信中的人名，我将有几个改掉了，用意有好有坏，并不相同。此无他，或则怕别人见于我们的信里，于他有些不便，或则单为自己，省得又是什么“听候开审”之类的麻烦而已。
Another point is that I will change a few of the names in the letter, the intentions are good and bad, but they are not the same. There is no other way, or we are afraid that others will see it in our letters, which will be inconvenient for him, or it is just for ourselves, so as not to save any trouble such as "waiting for trial".回想六七年来，环绕我们的风波也可谓不少了，在不断的挣扎中，相助的也有，下石的也有，笑骂诬蔑的也有，但我们紧咬了牙关，却也已经挣扎着生活了六七年。其间，含沙射影者都逐渐自己没入更黑暗的处所去了，而好意的朋友也已有两个不在人间，就是漱园和柔石。我们以这一本书为自己记念，并以感谢好意的朋友，并且留赠我们的孩子，给将来知道我们所经历的真相，其实大致是如此的。
In the continuous struggle, there are those who help each other, there are those who get off the stone, and there are those who laugh and slander us, but we grit our teeth, but we have been struggling to live for six or seven years. In the meantime, the sand projectors gradually disappeared into darker places, and two well-meaning friends were already out of the world, namely Shuyuan and Roushi. We remember this book as a reminder of ourselves, as a thank you to our well-meaning friends, and as a gift to our children, so that we can know the truth of what we have experienced in the future.一九三二年十二月十六日，鲁迅。
December 16, 1932, Lu Xun.

祝中俄文字之交

祝中俄文字之交

祝中俄文字之交

I wish you a friendship between Chinese and Russian characters十五年前，被西欧的所谓文明国人看作半开化的俄国，那文学，在世界文坛上，是胜利的；十五年以来，被帝国主义者看作恶魔的苏联，那文学，在世界文坛上，是胜利的。这里的所谓“胜利”，是说：以它的内容和技术的杰出，而得到广大的读者，并且给与了读者许多有益的东西。
Fifteen years ago, Russia, which was regarded as a semi-civilized Russia by the so-called civilized people of Western Europe, was a victory in the world literary world; For fifteen years, the Soviet Union, which was regarded as a demon by the imperialists, was victorious in the world literary world. The so-called "victory" here means that it has won a wide range of readers with its outstanding content and technology, and has given readers many useful things.它在中国，也没有出于这例子之外。
It is not in China, nor is it out of this example.我们曾在梁启超所办的《时务报》上，看见了《福尔摩斯包探案》的变幻，又在《新小说》上，看见了焦士威奴（Jules Verne）所做的号称科学小说的《海底旅行》之类的新奇。后来林琴南大译英国哈葛德（H. Rider Haggard）的小说了，我们又看见了伦敦小姐之缠绵和菲洲野蛮之古怪。至于俄国文学，却一点不知道，——但有几位也许自己心里明白，而没有告诉我们的“先觉”先生，自然是例外。不过在别一方面，是已经有了感应的。那时较为革命的青年，谁不知道俄国青年是革命的，暗杀的好手？尤其忘不掉的是苏菲亚，虽然大半也因为她是一位漂亮的姑娘。现在的国货的作品中，还常有“苏菲”一类的名字，那渊源就在此。
We have seen the changes in "Sherlock Holmes Detective" in Liang Qichao's "Current Affairs", and in "New Novel", we have seen novelties such as "Journey Under the Sea", which is known as a science fiction by Jules Verne. Later, Lin Qinnan translated the English Haggard (H. Rider Haggard), we see the lingering of Miss London and the barbarism of the Philippines. As for Russian literature, I don't know anything,—— but there are a few "pre-enlightened" gentlemen who may have understood it in their hearts but did not tell us, and naturally they are exceptions. But on the other hand, there is already a sense. At that time, the more revolutionary youth, who didn't know that the Russian youth were revolutionary and good assassins? Especially unforgettable is Sophia, although most of it is also because she is a beautiful girl. In today's domestic works, there are often names such as "Sophie", and this is the origin.那时——十九世纪末——的俄国文学，尤其是陀思妥夫斯基和托尔斯泰的作品，已经很影响了德国文学，但这和中国无关，因为那时研究德文的人少得很。最有关系的是英美帝国主义者，他们一面也翻译了陀思妥夫斯基，都介涅夫，托尔斯泰，契诃夫的选集了，一面也用那做给印度人读的读本来教我们的青年以拉玛和吉利瑟那（Rama and Krishna）的对话，然而因此也携带了阅读那些选集的可能。包探，冒险家，英国姑娘，菲洲野蛮的故事，是只能当醉饱之后，在发胀的身体上搔搔痒的，然而我们的一部分的青年却已经觉得压迫，只有痛楚，他要挣扎，用不着痒痒的抚摩，只在寻切实的指示了。
At that time, at the end of the nineteenth century, Russian literature, especially the works of Dostovsky and Tolstoy, had already influenced German literature, but this had nothing to do with China, because there were very few people studying German at that time. The most relevant were the Anglo-American imperialists, who on the one hand translated the anthologies of Dostovsky, Dugeniev, Tolstoy, and Chekhov, and on the other hand, they also used the readings for Indians to teach our youth the dialogues of Rama and Krishna, but thus also carried the possibility of reading those anthologies. The story of the detective, the adventurer, the English girl, and the savage of the Philippines can only be used as a drunken and full one, scratching the swollen body, but some of our young people already feel oppressed, only pain, and they have to struggle, without the need for tickling stroking, only looking for practical instructions.那时就看见了俄国文学。
That's when I saw Russian literature.那时就知道了俄国文学是我们的导师和朋友。因为从那里面，看见了被压迫者的善良的灵魂，的酸辛，的挣扎；还和四十年代的作品一同烧起希望，和六十年代的作品一同感到悲哀。我们岂不知道那时的大俄罗斯帝国也正在侵略中国，然而从文学里明白了一件大事，是世界上有两种人：压迫者和被压迫者！
It was then that I knew that Russian literature was our mentor and friend. Because from there, we can see the good souls, sorrows, and struggles of the oppressed; It also burns hope with the works of the forties and feels sad with the works of the sixties. Don't we know that the Great Russian Empire was also invading China at that time, but we understand from literature that there are two kinds of people in the world: the oppressor and the oppressed!从现在看来，这是谁都明白，不足道的，但在那时，却是一个大发见，正不亚于古人的发见了火的可以照暗夜，煮东西。
From now on, everyone understands that this is insignificant, but at that time, it was a great discovery, no less than the ancients who discovered that fire can shine in the dark night and cook things.俄国的作品，渐渐的绍介进中国来了，同时也得了一部分读者的共鸣，只是传布开去。零星的译品且不说罢，成为大部的就有《俄国戏曲集》十种和《小说月报》增刊的《俄国文学研究》一大本，还有《被压迫民族文学号》两本，则是由俄国文学的启发，而将范围扩大到一切弱小民族，并且明明点出“被压迫”的字样来了。
Russian works gradually entered China, and at the same time, they also resonated with some readers, but they were just spread. Not to mention the sporadic translations, most of them are "Russian Opera Collection" and a large volume of "Russian Literary Studies" supplemented by "Novel Monthly", as well as two copies of "Literature of Oppressed Nations", which were inspired by Russian literature and expanded the scope to all weak ethnic groups, and clearly pointed out the word "oppressed".于是也遭了文人学士的讨伐，有的主张文学的“崇高”，说描写下等人是鄙俗的勾当，有的比创作为处女，说翻译不过是媒婆，而重译尤令人讨厌。的确，除了《俄国戏曲集》以外，那时所有的俄国作品几乎都是重译的。
As a result, they were also attacked by literati and scholars, some advocated the "sublime" of literature, saying that describing people was a vulgar act, and some were more virgins than creation, saying that translation was just a matchmaker, and retranslation was particularly annoying. Indeed, with the exception of the "Russian Opera Collection", almost all Russian works at that time were retranslated.但俄国文学只是绍介进来，传布开去。
But Russian literature was only introduced and spread.作家的名字知道得更多了，我们虽然从安特来夫（L. Andreev）的作品里遇到了恐怖，阿尔志跋绥夫（M. Artsybashev）的作品里看见了绝望和荒唐，但也从珂罗连珂（V. Korolenko）学得了宽宏，从戈理基（Maxim Gorky）感受了反抗。读者大众的共鸣和热爱，早不是几个论客的自私的曲说所能掩蔽，这伟力，终于使先前膜拜曼殊斐儿（Katherine Mansfield）的绅士也重译了都介涅夫的《父与子》，排斥“媒婆”的作家也重译着托尔斯泰的《战争与和平》了。
The name of the writer is known better, although we know it from L. Andreev's work encounters horror, and M. Artsybashev's work shows despair and absurdity, but it also shows the difference between V. Korolenko and V. Korolenko) learned magnanimity and felt resistance from Maxim Gorky. The resonance and love of the readers and the masses could no longer be covered up by the selfish distortions of a few commentators, and this great power finally made the gentlemen who had previously worshipped Katherine Mansfield retranslate Dugehnev's "Fathers and Sons", and the writers who rejected the "matchmaker" also retranslated Tolstoy's "War and Peace".这之间，自然又遭了文人学士和流氓警犬的联军的讨伐。对于绍介者，有的说是为了卢布，有的说是意在投降，有的笑为“破锣”，有的指为共党，而实际上的对于书籍的禁止和没收，还因为是秘密的居多，无从列举。
In the meantime, it was naturally attacked by the coalition of literati scholars and rogue police dogs. For those who introduce, some say it is for rubles, some say it is intended to surrender, some laugh at it as "broken gong", some refer to it as the Communist Party, and the actual ban and confiscation of books are mostly secret, so it is impossible to enumerate.但俄国文学只是绍介进来，传布开去。
But Russian literature was only introduced and spread.有些人们，也译了《莫索里尼传》，也译了《希特拉传》，但他们绍介不出一册现代意国或德国的白色的大作品，《战后》是不属于希特拉的卐字旗下的，《死的胜利》又只好以“死”自傲。但苏联文学在我们却已有了里培进斯基的《一周间》，革拉特珂夫的《士敏土》，法捷耶夫的《毁灭》，绥拉菲摩微支的《铁流》；此外中篇短篇，还多得很。凡这些，都在御用文人的明枪暗箭之中，大踏步跨到读者大众的怀里去，给一一知道了变革，战斗，建设的辛苦和成功。
Some people also translated "The Biography of Mussolini" and "The Biography of Hitler", but they could not produce a large volume of white works in modern Italy or Germany, "After the War" did not belong to Hitler's swastika, and "The Victory of Death" had to be proud of "death". But Soviet literature already has Lipekinsky's "Between a Week", Gratkov's "Smintu", Fadeev's "Destruction", and Suirafimo Weizhi's "Iron Flow"; In addition, there are many short novellas. All of these are in the open and hidden arrows of the imperial literati, and they have strode into the arms of the readers and the public, and have known the hard work and success of change, battle, and construction one by one.但一月以前，对于苏联的“舆论”，刹时都转变了，昨夜的魔鬼，今朝的良朋，许多报章，总要提起几点苏联的好处，有时自然也涉及文艺上：“复交”之故也。然而，可祝贺的却并不在这里。自利者一淹在水里面，将要灭顶的时候，只要抓得着，是无论“破锣”破鼓，都会抓住的，他决没有所谓“洁癖”。然而无论他终于灭亡或幸而爬起，始终还是一个自利者。随手来举一个例子罢，上海称为“大报”的《申报》，不是一面甜嘴蜜舌的主张着“组织苏联考察团”（三二年十二月二十八日时评），而一面又将林克多的《苏联闻见录》称为“反动书籍”（同二十七日新闻）么？
But before a month, the "public opinion" of the Soviet Union changed in an instant, and the devil of last night, the good friends of today, and many newspapers always mentioned a few points of the benefits of the Soviet Union, and sometimes it naturally involved literary and artistic reasons: "re-enactment of diplomatic relations". However, the congratulations are not here. When a self-interested person is drowning in the water and is about to perish, as long as he can catch it, he will catch it no matter whether he "breaks the gong" or the drum, and he will never have the so-called "cleanliness fetish". However, whether he finally perished or fortunately rose up, he was still a self-interested person. To give an example, didn't the "Declaration" called "Big News" in Shanghai sweetly advocate "organizing a Soviet delegation" (Times Review on December 28, 32), and on the other hand, called Linkdor's "Soviet News and Observations" a "reactionary book" (same as the news on the 27th)?可祝贺的，是在中俄的文字之交，开始虽然比中英，中法迟，但在近十年中，两国的绝交也好，复交也好，我们的读者大众却不因此而进退；译本的放任也好，禁压也好，我们的读者也决不因此而盛衰。不但如常，而且扩大；不但虽绝交和禁压还是如常，而且虽绝交和禁压而更加扩大。这可见我们的读者大众，是一向不用自私的“势利眼”来看俄国文学的。我们的读者大众，在朦胧中，早知道这伟大肥沃的“黑土”里，要生长出什么东西来，而这“黑土”却也确实生长了东西，给我们亲见了：忍受，呻吟，挣扎，反抗，战斗，变革，战斗，建设，战斗，成功。
What can be congratulated is that although the writing friendship between China and Russia began later than China, Britain, China and France, in the past ten years, whether the two countries have broken off diplomatic relations or resumed diplomatic relations, our readers and the public have not been forced to advance or retreat because of this; Whether the translation is laissez-faire or suppressed, our readers will never prosper or decline because of this. Not only as usual, but also expanded; Not only is it still the same as usual, but it has been further expanded despite the severance of diplomatic relations and the ban. This shows that our readers have never looked at Russian literature without selfish "snobbery". Our readers, in the haze, already know what will grow in this great and fertile "black soil", but this "black soil" has indeed grown something, and we have seen it with our own eyes: enduring, groaning, struggling, resisting, fighting, changing, fighting, building, fighting, and succeeding.在现在，英国的萧，法国的罗兰，也都成为苏联的朋友了。这，也是当我们中国和苏联在历来不断的“文字之交”的途中，扩大而与世界结成真的“文字之交”的开始。
Now, Xiao of Britain and Roland of France have also become friends of the Soviet Union. This is also the beginning of the "literary friendship" between China and the Soviet Union that has been expanding and forming a real "friendship with the world" on the way of continuous "literary friendship".这是我们应该祝贺的。
This is something we should congratulate.十二月三十日。
December 30th.

一九三三年

一九三三年

一九三三年

In 1933

听说梦

听说梦

听说梦

Hear about dreams做梦，是自由的，说梦，就不自由。做梦，是做真梦的，说梦，就难免说谎。
Dreaming is free, but dreaming is not free. Dreaming is a real dream, and if you say a dream, you will inevitably lie.大年初一，就得到一本《东方杂志》新年特大号，临末有“新年的梦想”，问的是“梦想中的未来中国”和“个人生活”，答的有一百四十多人。记者的苦心，我是明白的，想必以为言论不自由，不如来说梦，而且与其说所谓真话之假，不如来谈谈梦话之真，我高兴的翻了一下，知道记者先生却大大的失败了。
On the first day of the Lunar New Year, I got a New Year's extra large copy of "Oriental Magazine", and at the end of the year, there was a "New Year's Dream", asking about "Dream Future China" and "Personal Life", and more than 140 people answered. I understand the hard work of the reporter, I must think that speech is not free, it is better to talk about dreams, and instead of telling the so-called truth and falsehood, it is better to talk about the truth of dreams.当我还未得到这本特大号之前，就遇到过一位投稿者，他比我先看见印本，自说他的答案已被资本家删改了，他所说的梦其实并不如此。这可见资本家虽然还没法禁止人们做梦，而说了出来，倘为权力所及，却要干涉的，决不给你自由。这一点，已是记者的大失败。
Before I got this extra-large book, I met a contributor who saw the print before I did, and said that his answer had been edited by the capitalist, and that the dream he was talking about was not like that. This shows that although the capitalists have not yet forbidden people from dreaming, they have said that if they are within the reach of power, they will never give you freedom if they want to interfere. This is already a big failure for journalists.但我们且不去管这改梦案子，只来看写着的梦境罢，诚如记者所说，来答复的几乎全部是智识分子。首先，是谁也觉得生活不安定，其次，是许多人梦想着将来的好社会，“各尽所能”呀，“大同世界”呀，很有些“越轨”气息了（末三句是我添的，记者并没有说）。
But let's not worry about this dream change case, just look at the dream written, as the reporter said, almost all of the answers are intellectuals. First of all, no one feels that life is unstable, and secondly, many people dream of a good society in the future, "each doing their best", "Datong world", there is a bit of a "deviant" atmosphere (the last three sentences were added by me, the reporter did not say).但他后来就有点“痴”起来，他不知从那里拾来了一种学说，将一百多个梦分为两大类，说那些梦想好社会的都是“载道”之梦，是“异端”，正宗的梦应该是“言志”的，硬把“志”弄成一个空洞无物的东西。然而，孔子曰，“盍各言尔志”，而终于赞成曾点者，就因为其“志”合于孔子之“道”的缘故也。
But he later became a little "crazy", he picked up a doctrine from somewhere, divided more than a hundred dreams into two categories, saying that those who dream of a good society are all dreams of "carrying the way", which is "heresy", and the authentic dream should be "Yanzhi", and the "zhi" is made into an empty thing. However, Confucius said, "Why don't you say your own will", and finally agreed with Zeng Dian, because his "will" was in line with Confucius's "Tao".其实是记者的所以为“载道”的梦，那里面少得很。文章是醒着的时候写的，问题又近于“心理测验”，遂致对答者不能不做出各各适宜于目下自己的职业，地位，身分的梦来（已被删改者自然不在此例），即使看去好像怎样“载道”，但为将来的好社会“宣传”的意思，是没有的。所以，虽然梦“大家有饭吃”者有人，梦“无阶级社会”者有人，梦“大同世界”者有人，而很少有人梦见建设这样社会以前的阶级斗争，白色恐怖，轰炸，虐杀，鼻子里灌辣椒水，电刑……倘不梦见这些，好社会是不会来的，无论怎么写得光明，终究是一个梦，空头的梦，说了出来，也无非教人都进这空头的梦境里面去。
In fact, it is the dream of the reporter to "carry the way", and there are very few of them. The article was written in waking hours, and the questions were close to "psychological tests", so the respondents had to make dreams that were suitable for their current occupations, statuses, and identities (those who have been deleted are naturally not in this case). Therefore, although there are people who dream of "everyone has food", there are people who dream of "classless society", and there are people who dream of "Datong world", few people dream of building such a society before the class struggle, white terror, bombing, torture, pepper water in their noses, and electrocution...... If you don't dream of these, a good society will not come, no matter how brightly it is written, after all, it is a dream, an empty dream, and if you say it, it is nothing more than teaching people to enter this empty dream.然而要实现这“梦”境的人们是有的，他们不是说，而是做，梦着将来，而致力于达到这一种将来的现在。因为有这事实，这才使许多智识分子不能不说好像“载道”的梦，但其实并非“载道”，乃是给“道”载了一下，倘要简洁，应该说是“道载”的。
However, there are people who want to realize this "dream", they do not say, but do, dream of the future, and are committed to achieving this kind of future present. Because of this fact, many intellectuals cannot help but say that it is like a dream of "carrying the Dao", but in fact it is not "carrying the Dao", but carrying the "Dao".为什么会给“道载”呢？曰：为目前和将来的吃饭问题而已。
Why is it given to "Dao Zai"? The answer is: it is just a matter of eating now and in the future.我们还受着旧思想的束缚，一说到吃，就觉得近乎鄙俗。但我是毫没有轻视对答者诸公的意思的。《东方杂志》记者在《读后感》里，也曾引佛洛伊特的意见，以为“正宗”的梦，是“表现各人的心底的秘密而不带着社会作用的”。但佛洛伊特以被压抑为梦的根柢——人为什么被压抑的呢？这就和社会制度，习惯之类连结了起来，单是做梦不打紧，一说，一问，一分析，可就不妥当了。记者没有想到这一层，于是就一头撞在资本家的朱笔上。但引“压抑说”来释梦，我想，大家必已经不以为忤了罢。
We are still bound by old ideas, and when we talk about eating, we feel almost vulgar. But I have no intention of despising the respondents. In "Impressions After Reading", a reporter from "Oriental Magazine" also quoted Freud's opinion, believing that "authentic" dreams are "expressing the secrets of each person's heart without social effect". But Freud took repression as the root of his dream - why is man repressed? This is linked to social systems, habits, etc., and it is not appropriate to just dream, a word, a question, and an analysis. The reporter didn't expect this layer, so he hit the capitalist's red pen. But to quote the "repressive theory" to interpret the dream, I think everyone must have been disobedient.不过，佛洛伊特恐怕是有几文钱，吃得饱饱的罢，所以没有感到吃饭之难，只注意于性欲。有许多人正和他在同一境遇上，就也轰然的拍起手来。诚然，他也告诉过我们，女儿多爱父亲，儿子多爱母亲，即因为异性的缘故。然而婴孩出生不多久，无论男女，就尖起嘴唇，将头转来转去。莫非它想和异性接吻么？不，谁都知道：是要吃东西！
However, Freud probably had a few pennies and was full, so he didn't feel the difficulty of eating, and only paid attention to his sexual desire. Many people were in the same situation as him, and they also clapped their hands. True, he also told us that daughters love their fathers more and sons love their mothers more, that is, because of the opposite sex. However, not long after the baby was born, both men and women pucked their lips and turned their heads around. Could it be that it wants to kiss the opposite sex? No, everyone knows: it's about eating!食欲的根柢，实在比性欲还要深，在目下开口爱人，闭口情书，并不以为肉麻的时候，我们也大可以不必讳言要吃饭。因为是醒着做的梦，所以不免有些不真，因为题目究竟是“梦想”，而且如记者先生所说，我们是“物质的需要远过于精神的追求”了，所以乘着Censors（也引用佛洛伊特语）的监护好像解除了之际，便公开了一部分。其实也是在“梦中贴标语，喊口号”，不过不是积极的罢了，而且有些也许倒和表面的“标语”正相反。
The root of appetite is really deeper than sexual desire, and when we open our mouths to love people, close our mouths, and don't think that we are numb, we don't have to shy away from saying that we want to eat. Because it is a waking dream, it is inevitable that it is a little untrue, because the title is "dream", and as Mr. Reporter said, we are "material needs far more than spiritual pursuits", so we made part of it public when the guardianship of Censors (also quoting Freud) seemed to be lifted. In fact, it is also "sticking slogans and shouting slogans in dreams", but it is not positive, and some of them may be the opposite of the superficial "slogans".时代是这么变化，饭碗是这样艰难，想想现在和将来，有些人也只能如此说梦，同是小资产阶级（虽然也有人定我为“封建余孽”或“土著资产阶级”，但我自己姑且定为属于这阶级），很能够彼此心照，然而也无须秘而不宣的。
The times are so changing, the job is so difficult, thinking about the present and the future, some people can only dream like this, the same petty bourgeoisie (although some people have designated me as a "feudal remnant" or "indigenous bourgeoisie", but I myself have decided to belong to this class), I am very able to understand each other, but there is no need to keep it a secret.至于另有些梦为隐士，梦为渔樵，和本相全不相同的名人，其实也只是豫感饭碗之脆，而却想将吃饭范围扩大起来，从朝廷而至园林，由洋场及于山泽，比上面说过的那些志向要大得远，不过这里不来多说了。
As for some other celebrities who dream of being hermits, dreaming of being fishermen and woodcutters, and who are completely different from their true nature, in fact, they only feel the crispness of the rice bowl, but they want to expand the scope of eating, from the imperial court to the garden, from the foreign farm to the mountains and marshes, which is much bigger than the aspirations mentioned above, but I won't say more here.一月一日。
January 1st.

论“赴难”和“逃难”

论“赴难”和“逃难”

论“赴难”和“逃难”

On "going to trouble" and "fleeing"——寄《涛声》编辑的一封信
——A letter sent to the editor of "The Sound of the Waves"编辑先生：
Mr. Editor:我常常看《涛声》，也常常叫“快哉！”但这回见了周木斋先生那篇《骂人与自骂》，其中说北平的大学生“即使不能赴难，最低最低的限度也应不逃难”，而致慨于五四运动时代式锋芒之销尽，却使我如骨鲠在喉，不能不说几句话。因为我是和周先生的主张正相反，以为“倘不能赴难，就应该逃难”，属于“逃难党”的。
I often watch "The Sound of the Waves", and I often call it "Fast! But this time I saw Mr. Zhou Muzhai's article "Scolding and Self-Insulting", which said that college students in Peking "even if they cannot go to the disaster, they should not flee at the minimum limit", and lamented that the era-style edge of the May Fourth Movement was gone, but it made me feel like a bone in my throat, and I couldn't help but say a few words. Because I am the exact opposite of Mr. Zhou's proposition, I think that "if you can't go to the disaster, you should flee", which belongs to the "fleeing party".周先生在文章的末尾，“疑心是北京改为北平的应验”，我想，一半是对的。那时的北京，还挂着“共和”的假面，学生嚷嚷还不妨事；那时的执政，是昨天上海市十八团体为他开了“上海各界欢迎段公芝老大会”的段祺瑞先生，他虽然是武人，却还没有看过《莫索理尼传》。然而，你瞧，来了呀。有一回，对着请愿的学生毕毕剥剥的开枪了，兵们最爱瞄准的是女学生，这用精神分析学来解释，是说得过去的，尤其是剪发的女学生，这用整顿风俗的学说来解说，也是说得过去的。总之是死了一些“莘莘学子”。然而还可以开追悼会；还可以游行过执政府之门，大叫“打倒段祺瑞”。为什么呢？因为这时又还挂着“共和”的假面。然而，你瞧，又来了呀。现为党国大教授的陈源先生，在《现代评论》上哀悼死掉的学生，说可惜他们为几个卢布送了性命；《语丝》反对了几句，现为党国要人的唐有壬先生在《晶报》上发表一封信，说这些言动是受墨斯科的命令的。这实在已经有了北平气味了。
At the end of the article, Mr. Zhou said, "Doubt is the fulfillment of Beijing's change to Peiping", I think, half of it is right. At that time, Beijing still had the mask of "republic", and students shouted that it was okay; At that time, it was Mr. Duan Qirui, who held the "Shanghai Welcome Duan Gongzhi Old Conference" for him yesterday, although he was a martial artist, he had not yet read "The Biography of Mussolini". However, lo and behold, here it comes. Once, he shot at the petitioning students, and the soldiers' favorite target was female students, which was explained by psychoanalysis, which made sense, especially the female students who cut their hair, which was explained by the doctrine of rectifying customs, and it was also reasonable. In short, some "diligent students" died. However, a memorial service can also be held; You can also march past the gate of the ruling government, shouting "Down with Duan Qirui". Why? Because at this time, there was still a mask of "republic". However, lo and behold, here it is again. Mr. Chen Yuan, who is now a professor at the Party and State University, mourned the dead students in the "Modern Review", saying that it was a pity that they gave their lives for a few rubles; Mr. Tang Youren, who is now an important figure in the party and state, published a letter in the "Crystal Newspaper", saying that these words and actions were ordered by Musco. This really smells like Peking.后来，北伐成功了，北京属于党国，学生们就都到了进研究室的时代，五四式是不对了。为什么呢？因为这是很容易为“反动派”所利用的。为了矫正这种坏脾气，我们的政府，军人，学者，文豪，警察，侦探，实在费了不少的苦心。用诰谕，用刀枪，用书报，用煅炼，用逮捕，用拷问，直到去年请愿之徒，死的都是“自行失足落水”，连追悼会也不开的时候为止，这才显出了新教育的效果。
Later, the Northern Expedition was successful, Beijing belonged to the party-state, and the students all entered the era of entering the research room, and the May Fourth style was wrong. Why? Because this is easy for the "reactionaries" to exploit. In order to correct this bad temper, our government, soldiers, scholars, writers, police, and detectives have really spent a lot of painstaking efforts. With edicts, knives and guns, books and newspapers, with calcination, with arrest, with torture, until last year's petitioners, those who died "fell into the water on their own" and did not even hold a memorial service showed the effect of new education.倘使日本人不再攻榆关，我想，天下是太平了的，“必先安内而后可以攘外”。但可恨的是外患来得太快一点，太繁一点，日本人太不为中国诸公设想之故也，而且也因此引起了周先生的责难。
If the Japanese no longer attack Yuguan, I think the world is peaceful, "we must first settle the internal and then expel the outside." But the hateful thing is that the external troubles came too quickly and too complicated, and the Japanese did not think about the Chinese princes, and this also caused Mr. Zhou's criticism.看周先生的主张，似乎最好是“赴难”。不过，这是难的。倘使早先有了组织，经过训练，前线的军人力战之后，人员缺少了，副司令下令召集，那自然应该去的。无奈据去年的事实，则连火车也不能白坐，而况平日所学的又是债权论，土耳其文学史，最小公倍数之类。去打日本，一定打不过的。大学生们曾经和中国的兵警打过架，但是“自行失足落水”了，现在中国的兵警尚且不抵抗，大学生能抵抗么？我们虽然也看见过许多慷慨激昂的诗，什么用死尸堵住敌人的炮口呀，用热血胶住倭奴的刀枪呀，但是，先生，这是“诗”呵！事实并不这样的，死得比蚂蚁还不如，炮口也堵不住，刀枪也胶不住。孔子曰：“以不教民战，是谓弃之。”我并不全拜服孔老夫子，不过觉得这话是对的，我也正是反对大学生“赴难”的一个。
Looking at Mr. Zhou's proposition, it seems that it is best to "go to the disaster". However, it is difficult. If there had been an organization earlier, after training, and after the frontline soldiers fought, there was a shortage of personnel, and the deputy commander ordered it to be called, then it should naturally go. Unfortunately, according to last year's facts, even the train cannot be sitting in vain, and what I usually study is creditor's theory, Turkish literary history, and the least public multiple. If you go to Japan, you will definitely not be able to beat it. College students have fought with Chinese soldiers and police, but they have "fallen into the water on their own", and now China's soldiers and police are still not resisting, can college students resist? Although we have also seen many impassioned poems, what uses dead corpses to block the enemy's cannon muzzle, and uses blood to glue the swords and guns of Japanese slaves, but, sir, this is "poetry"! In fact, it is not like this, it dies worse than ants, the muzzle cannot be blocked, and the swords and guns cannot be glued. Confucius said, "To fight without teaching the people is to abandon them." "I don't fully admire Master Kong, but I think this is right, and I am also one of those who oppose college students' "going to trouble".那么，“不逃难”怎样呢？我也是完全反对。自然，现在是“敌人未到”的，但假使一到，大学生们将赤手空拳，骂贼而死呢，还是躲在屋里，以图幸免呢？我想，还是前一着堂皇些，将来也可以有一本烈士传。不过于大局依然无补，无论是一个或十万个，至多，也只能又向“国联”报告一声罢了。去年十九路军的某某英雄怎样杀敌，大家说得眉飞色舞，因此忘却了全线退出一百里的大事情，可是中国其实还是输了的。而况大学生们连武器也没有。现在中国的新闻上大登“满洲国”的虐政，说是不准私藏军器，但我们大中华民国人民来藏一件护身的东西试试看，也会家破人亡，——先生，这是很容易“为反动派所利用”的呵。
So, what about "not fleeing"? I am also completely opposed. Naturally, now it is "the enemy has not arrived", but if it arrives, the college students will die with their bare hands, scolding the thief, or hiding in the house in order to escape? I think that the previous one is more dignified, and there can be a biography of martyrs in the future.
