《凯绥·珂勒惠支版画选集》序目

Preface to the "Selected Prints of Kaisui Kellerhuithi"凯绥·勖密特（Kaethe Schmidt）以一八六七年七月八日生于东普鲁士的区匿培克（Koenigsberg）。她的外祖父是卢柏（Julius Rupp），即那地方的自由宗教协会的创立者。父亲原是候补的法官，但因为宗教上和政治上的意见，没有补缺的希望了，这穷困的法学家便如俄国人之所说：“到民间去”，做了木匠，一直到卢柏死后，才来当这教区的首领和教师。他有四个孩子，都很用心的加以教育，然而先不知道凯绥的艺术的才能。凯绥先学的是刻铜的手艺，到一八八五年冬，这才赴她的兄弟在研究文学的柏林，向斯滔发·培伦（Stauffer Bern）去学绘画。后回故乡，学于奈台（Neide），为了“厌倦”，终于向闵兴的哈台列克（Herterich）那里去学习了。
Kaethe Schmidt was born on July 8, 1867 in Koenigsberg, East Prussia. Her maternal grandfather was Julius Rupp, the founder of the local Free Religious Association. My father was originally an alternate judge, but because of religious and political opinions, there was no hope of filling the vacancy, so the poor jurist became a carpenter, as the Russians said, "to the people", and became a carpenter until after Luper's death. He had four children, all of whom were educated with great care, but they did not know Kaisui's artistic talent. Kaisui first learned the craft of copper carving, and in the winter of 1885, she went to Berlin, where her brother was studying literature, to learn painting from Stauffer Bern. Later, he returned to his hometown and studied at Neide, and in order to "get tired of it", he finally went to study with Herterich in Minxing.一八九一年，和她兄弟的幼年之友卡尔·珂勒惠支（Karl Kollwitz）结婚，他是一个开业的医生，于是凯绥也就在柏林的“小百姓”之间住下，这才放下绘画，刻起版画来。待到孩子们长大了，又用力于雕刻。一八九八年，制成有名的《织工一揆》计六幅，取材于一八四四年的史实，是与先出的霍普德曼（Gerhart Hauptmann）的剧本同名的；一八九九年刻《格莱亲》，零一年刻《断头台边的舞蹈》；零四年旅行巴黎；零四至八年成连续版画《农民战争》七幅，获盛名，受Villa-Romana奖金，得游学于意大利。这时她和一个女友由佛罗棱萨步行而入罗马，然而这旅行，据她自己说，对于她的艺术似乎并无大影响。一九〇九年作《失业》，一〇年作《妇人被死亡所捕》和以“死”为题材的小图。
In 1891, she married her brother's childhood friend Karl Kollwitz, a practicing doctor, so Kaiser also lived among the "common people" in Berlin, and then put down painting and carved prints. When the children grow up, they work carving. In 1898, six famous "Weaver's Ikki" were produced, based on historical facts from 1844, which is the same name as the play by Gerhart Hauptmann; In 1899, he engraved "Grammy", and in 01, he engraved "Dance by the Guillotine"; Traveled to Paris in '04; From 04 to 8, he completed seven continuous prints "Peasant War", which became famous, and he received a prize from Villa-Romana to study in Italy. At this time she and a girlfriend walked from Florenza to Rome, but this trip, according to herself, did not seem to have much influence on her art. In 1909, he wrote "Unemployed", and in 10 years, he wrote "A Woman Caught by Death" and a small picture with the theme of "death".世界大战起，她几乎并无制作。一九一四年十月末，她的很年青的大儿子以义勇兵死于弗兰兑伦（Flandern）战线上。一八年十一月，被选为普鲁士艺术学院会员，这是以妇女而入选的第一个。从一九年以来，她才仿佛从大梦初醒似的，又从事于版画了，有名的是这一年的纪念里勃克内希（Liebknecht）的木刻和石刻，零二至零三年的木刻连续画《战争》，后来又有三幅《无产者》，也是木刻连续画。一九二七年为她的六十岁纪念，霍普德曼那时还是一个战斗的作家，给她书简道：“你的无声的描线，侵人心髓，如一种惨苦的呼声：希腊和罗马时候都没有听到过的呼声。”法国罗曼·罗兰（Romain Rolland）则说：“凯绥·珂勒惠支的作品是现代德国的最伟大的诗歌，它照出穷人与平民的困苦和悲痛。这有丈夫气概的妇人，用了阴郁和纤秾的同情，把这些收在她的眼中，她的慈母的腕里了。这是做了牺牲的人民的沉默的声音。”然而她在现在，却不能教授，不能作画，只能真的沉默的和她的儿子住在柏林了；她的儿子像那父亲一样，也是一个医生。
Since the World War, she has almost no production. At the end of October 1914, her very young eldest son died as a volunteer on the Flandern front. In November 18, she was elected a member of the Prussian Academy of Arts, the first woman to be elected. Since 19 years, she has been engaged in printmaking again, as if she had just woken up from a big dream, and is famous for the woodcuts and stone carvings of Liebknecht in this year, the continuous woodcut painting "War" from 02 to 03, and later three "Proletarians", which are also continuous woodcut paintings. In 1927, to commemorate her sixtieth birthday, Hopdemann, who was still a combat writer at the time, wrote to her: "Your silent lines are intrusive, like a miserable cry: a cry that neither Greece nor Rome had ever heard. Romain Rolland of France said: "The work of Kaiser Kölhuitz is the greatest poetry of modern Germany, which reflects the hardship and sorrow of the poor and the common people." This husbandly woman, with gloom and delicate sympathy, took these in her eyes, in the wrist of her loving mother. This is the silent voice of the people who have made sacrifices. "However, she cannot teach or paint now, but can only live in Berlin with her son in silence; Her son, like that father, was also a doctor.在女性艺术家之中，震动了艺术界的，现代几乎无出于凯绥·珂勒惠支之上——或者赞美，或者攻击，或者又对攻击给她以辩护。诚如亚斐那留斯（Ferdinand Avenarius）之所说：“新世纪的前几年，她第一次展览作品的时候，就为报章所喧传的了。从此以来，一个说，‘她是伟大的版画家’；人就过作无聊的不成话道：‘凯绥·珂勒惠支是属于只有一个男子的新派版画家里的’。别一个说：‘她是社会民主主义的宣传家’，第三个却道：‘她是悲观的困苦的画手’。而第四个又以为‘是一个宗教的艺术家’。要之：无论人们怎样地各以自己的感觉和思想来解释这艺术，怎样地从中只看见一种的意义——然而有一件事情是普遍的：人没有忘记她。谁一听到凯绥·珂勒惠支的名姓，就仿佛看见这艺术。这艺术是阴郁的，虽然都在坚决的动弹，集中于强韧的力量，这艺术是统一而单纯的——非常之逼人。”
Among female artists, there is hardly anything that has shaken the art world in modern times above Kaiser Kölhuitsch—either praising her, or attacking, or defending her. As Ferdinand Avenarius said: "In the first few years of the new century, when she first exhibited her work, it was noisy in the newspapers. From then on, one said, 'She is a great printmaker'; people lived a boring nonsense: 'Kaiser Kölhuitz belonged to a new school of printmakers with only one man'. Don't say: 'She is a propagandist of social democracy', and the third says: 'She is a pessimistic and miserable painter'. And the fourth thinks that 'an artist of a religion'. In short: no matter how people interpret art with their own feelings and thoughts, no matter how much they see only one meaning in it—yet one thing is universal: people have not forgotten her. Whoever hears the name of Kaisui Kelehuizhi seems to see this art. This art is gloomy, although it is all resolutely moving, concentrating on the strength of strength, this art is unified and simple—very compelling. ”但在我们中国，绍介的还不多，我只记得在已经停刊的《现代》和《译文》上，各曾刊印过她的一幅木刻，原画自然更少看见；前四五年，上海曾经展览过她的几幅作品，但恐怕也不大有十分注意的人。她的本国所复制的作品，据我所见，以《凯绥·珂勒惠支画帖》（Kaethe Kollwitz Mappe，Herausgegeben Von Kunstwart，Kunstwart-Verlag，Muenchen，1927）为最佳，但后一版便变了内容，忧郁的多于战斗的了。印刷未精，而幅数较多的，则有《凯绥·珂勒惠支作品集》（Das Kaethe Kollwitz Werk，Carl Reisner Verlag，Dresden，1930），只要一翻这集子，就知道她以深广的慈母之爱，为一切被侮辱和损害者悲哀，抗议，愤怒，斗争；所取的题材大抵是困苦，饥饿，流离，疾病，死亡，然而也有呼号，挣扎，联合和奋起。此后又出了一本新集（Das Neue K. Kollwitz Werk，1933），却更多明朗之作了。霍善斯坦因（Wilhelm Hausenstein）批评她中期的作品，以为虽然间有鼓动的男性的版画，暴力的恐吓，但在根本上，是和颇深的生活相联系，形式也出于颇激的纠葛的，所以那形式，是紧握着世事的形相。永田一修并取她的后来之作，以这批评为不足，他说凯绥·珂勒惠支的作品，和里培尔曼（Max Liebermann）不同，并非只觉得题材有趣，来画下层世界的；她因为被周围的悲惨生活所动，所以非画不可，这是对于榨取人类者的无穷的“愤怒”。“她照目前的感觉，——永田一修说——描写着黑土的大众。她不将样式来范围现象。时而见得悲剧，时而见得英雄化，是不免的。然而无论她怎样阴郁，怎样悲哀，却决不是非革命。她没有忘却变革现社会的可能。而且愈入老境，就愈脱离了悲剧的，或者英雄的，阴暗的形式。”
But in China, there are not many Shaojie, I only remember that in the discontinued "Modern" and "Translation", one of her woodcuts was printed, and the original painting was naturally less seen; In the first four or five years, several of her works were exhibited in Shanghai, but I am afraid that not many people paid much attention. As far as I can see, the best of her reproductions in her home country is Kaethe Kollwitz Mappe, Herausgegeben von Kunstwart, Kunstwart-Verlag, Muenchen, 1927, but the content is changed in the latter edition, and it is more melancholy than combat. The printed works are not fine and have a large number of pages, such as "Das Kaethe Kollwitz Werk, Carl Reisner Verlag, Dresden, 1930", as long as you turn to this collection, you will know that she mourned, protested, angered, and struggled for all those who were insulted and harmed with her deep and broad motherly love; The themes taken are mostly hardship, hunger, displacement, disease, death, but there are also cry outs, struggles, unity and rise. After that, a new collection (Das Neue K. Kollwitz Werk, 1933) was published, but it was more clear. Wilhelm Hausenstein criticized her mid-term works, believing that although there were occasional engraving male prints and violent intimidation, they were fundamentally deeply connected to life, and the form was also out of a lot of intense entanglement, so the form was a form that grasped the appearance of the world. Nagata took her later works as insufficient, saying that Kaisui Kölhuitsch's works, unlike Max Liebermann, did not only find the subject matter interesting to depict the lower world; She is moved by the miserable life around her, so she must paint, which is an infinite "anger" for those who exploit humans. She said according to her current feelings,—— Nagata Kazushu - describing the masses of the black soil. She does not range the style of the phenomenon. Sometimes we see tragedy, sometimes we see heroism, which is inevitable. However, no matter how gloomy and sad she is, it is by no means non-revolutionary. She has not forgotten the possibility of changing the current society. And the older you get, the more you detach yourself from tragic, heroic, and dark forms. ”而且她不但为周围的悲惨生活抗争，对于中国也没有像中国对于她那样的冷淡：一九三一年一月间，六个青年作家遇害之后，全世界的进步的文艺家联名提出抗议的时候，她也是署名的一个人。现在，用中国法计算作者的年龄，她已届七十岁了，这一本书的出版，虽然篇幅有限，但也可以算是为她作一个小小的记念的罢。
And she not only fought for the miserable life around her, but also did not have the same indifference to China as China did to her: in January 1931, after the murder of six young writers, she was also one of the signatories when progressive writers and artists from all over the world jointly protested. Now, using Chinese law to calculate the author's age, she is seventy years old, and the publication of this book, although limited in space, can also be regarded as a small memory for her.
选集所取，计二十一幅，以原版拓本为主，并复制一九二七年的印本《画帖》以足之。以下据亚斐那留斯及第勒（Louise Diel）的解说，并略参己见，为目录——
The anthology consists of 21 pieces, mainly original rubbings, and a copy of the 1927 print "Picture Post" to fill it up. The following is based on the explanation of Aphinarius and Louise Diel, and with a brief reference to my own opinion, as a table of contents -（1）《自画像》（Selbstbild）。石刻，制作年代未详，按《作品集》所列次序，当成于一九一〇年顷；据原拓本，原大34×30cm.这是作者从许多版画的肖像中，自己选给中国的一幅，隐然可见她的悲悯，愤怒和慈和。
(1) "Self-Portrait" (Selbstbild). The stone carving, the date of production is unknown, according to the order listed in the "Collection", it is believed to have been completed around 1910; According to the original rubbing, the original size is 34×30cm. This is one that the author chose for China from many prints, and her compassion, anger and kindness are faintly visible.（2）《穷苦》（Not）。石刻，原大15×15cm.据原版拓本，后五幅同。这是有名的《织工一揆》（Ein Weberaufstand）的第一幅，一八九八年作。前四年，霍普德曼的剧本《织匠》始开演于柏林的德国剧场，取材是一八四四年的勖列济安（Schle-sien）麻布工人的蜂起，作者也许是受着一点这作品的影响的，但这可以不必深论，因为那是剧本，而这却是图画。我们借此进了一间穷苦的人家，冰冷，破烂，父亲抱一个孩子，毫无方法的坐在屋角里，母亲是愁苦的，两手支头，在看垂危的儿子，纺车静静的停在她的旁边。
(2) "Not". Stone carving, originally 15×15cm. According to the original rubbing, the last five pieces are the same. This is the first painting of the famous "Weaver's Journey" (Ein Weberaufstand), made in 1898. Four years ago, Hopdemann's play "The Weaver" was first performed in the German theater in Berlin, based on the uprising of the linen workers in Schle-sien in 1844, and the author may have been influenced by this work a little, but this does not need to be discussed in detail, because it is a play, and this is a picture. We took this opportunity to enter a poor house, cold, tattered, the father held a child, sitting in the corner of the house without any way, the mother was sad, holding her head with both hands, looking at her dying son, and the spinning wheel stopped quietly next to her.（3）《死亡》（Tod）。石刻，原大22×18cm.同上的第二幅。还是冰冷的房屋，母亲疲劳得睡去了，父亲还是毫无方法的，然而站立着在沉思他的无法。桌上的烛火尚有余光，“死”却已经近来，伸开他骨出的手，抱住了弱小的孩子。孩子的眼睛张得极大，在凝视我们，他要生存，他至死还在希望人有改革运命的力量。
(3) "Death" (Tod). Stone carving, original size 22×18cm. Ibid. It was still a cold house, and my mother fell asleep from fatigue, and my father was still helpless, but he stood there contemplating his impossibility. The candlelight on the table was still lingering, but "death" was already near, stretched out his bone-out hand, and hugged the weak child. The child's eyes are extremely wide open, staring at us, he wants to survive, and he still hopes that people will have the power to reform their destiny until death.（4）《商议》（Beratung）。石刻，原大27×17cm.同上的第三幅。接着前两幅的沉默的忍受和苦恼之后，到这里却现出生存竞争的景象来了。我们只在黑暗中看见一片桌面，一只杯子和两个人，但为的是在商议摔掉被践踏的运命。
(4) "Consultation" (Beratung). Stone carving, original size 27×17cm. After the silent enduring and distressing of the first two paintings, the scene of survival competition appears here. We only saw a table, a cup and two people in the dark, but we were discussing the fate of being trampled on.（5）《织工队》（Weberzug）。铜刻，原大22×29cm.同上的第四幅。队伍进向吮取脂膏的工场，手里捏着极可怜的武器，手脸都瘦损，神情也很颓唐，因为向来总饿着肚子。队伍中有女人，也疲惫到不过走得动；这作者所写的大众里，是大抵有女人的。她还背着孩子，却伏在肩头睡去了。
(5) "Weaver's Team" (Weberzug). Bronze engraving, originally 22×29cm. The team entered the workshop where the ointment was sucked, holding a very pitiful weapon in their hands, their hands and face were thin, and their expressions were also very depressed, because they were always hungry. There are women in the team, and they are too tired to walk; Among the masses written by this author, there are probably women. She was still carrying the child on her back, but fell asleep on her shoulder.（6）《突击》（Sturm）。铜刻，原大24×29cm.同上的第五幅。工场的铁门早经锁闭，织工们却想用无力的手和可怜的武器，来破坏这铁门，或者是飞进石子去。女人们在助战，用痉挛的手，从地上挖起石块来。孩子哭了，也许是路上睡着的那一个。这是在六幅之中，人认为最好的一幅，有时用这来证明作者的《织工》，艺术达到怎样的高度的。
(6) "Sturm". Bronze engraving, originally 24×29cm. Ibid. The iron gate of the workshop had long been locked, but the weavers wanted to destroy the iron gate with weak hands and pitiful weapons, or fly into the stones. The women were helping the battle, using their cramped hands to dig stones from the ground. The child cried, maybe the one who fell asleep on the road. This is the best of the six paintings, and it is sometimes used to prove what height the author's "Weaver" art has reached.（7）《收场》（Ende）。铜刻，原大24×30cm.同上的第六和末一幅。我们到底又和织工回到他们的家里来，织机默默的停着，旁边躺着两具尸体，伏着一个女人；而门口还在抬进尸体来。这是四十年代，在德国的织工的求生的结局。
(7) "Ende". Bronze engraving, originally 24×30cm. When we returned to their home with the weaver, the loom stopped silently, and there were two corpses lying next to it, lying a woman; And the body was still being carried in at the door. This is the end of the survival of weavers in Germany in the forties.（8）《格莱亲》（Gretchen）。一八九九年作，石刻；据《画帖》，原大未详。歌德（Goethe）的《浮士德》（Faust）有浮士德爱格莱亲，诱与通情，有孕；她在井边，从女友听到邻女被情人所弃，想到自己，于是向圣母供花祷告事。这一幅所写的是这可怜的少女经过极狭的桥上，在水里幻觉的看见自己的将来。她在剧本里，后来是将她和浮士德所生的孩子投在水里淹死，下狱了。原石已破碎。
(8) "Gretchen". Made in 1899, stone carving; According to the "Picture Post", the original size is unknown. Goethe's "Faust" has Faust's love for Gladstone, seducing and having an affair, and being pregnant; She heard from her girlfriend that her neighbor had been abandoned by her lover, and thought of herself, so she offered flowers and prayed to the Virgin. This picture is about this poor girl passing through a very narrow bridge and hallucinating her future in the water. She was in the script, and later she threw the child born to her and Faust into the water and drowned, and was imprisoned. The rough stone is broken.（9）《断头台边的舞蹈》（Tanz Um Die Guillotine）。一九〇一年作，铜刻；据《画帖》，原大未详。是法国大革命时候的一种情景：断头台造起来了，大家围着它，吼着“让我们来跳加尔玛弱儿舞罢！”（Dansons La Carmagnole！）的歌，在跳舞。不是一个，是为了同样的原因而同样的可怕了的一群。周围的破屋，像积叠起来的困苦的峭壁，上面只见一块天。狂暴的人堆的臂膊，恰如净罪的火焰一般，照出来的只有一个阴暗。
(9) "Tanz um Die Guillotine" (Dance by the Guillotine). Made in 1901, bronze engraving; According to the "Picture Post", the original size is unknown. It was a scene from the French Revolution: the guillotine was built, and everyone surrounded it, shouting, "Let's dance the Garma weakling!" ”（Dansons La Carmagnole！ The song is dancing. Not one, but for the same reasons, the same horrible group. The surrounding dilapidated houses are like piled up cliffs, and only a piece of sky can be seen on them. The arms of the violent crowd were like the flame of purification, and only one darkness was illuminated.（10）《耕夫》（Die Pflueger）。原大31×45cm.这就是有名的历史的连续画《农民战争》（Bauernkrieg）的第一幅。画共七幅，作于一九〇四至〇八年，都是铜刻。现在据以影印的也都是原拓本。“农民战争”是近代德国最大的社会改革运动之一，以一五二四年顷，起于南方，其时农民都在奴隶的状态，被虐于贵族的封建的特权；玛丁·路德既提倡新教，同时也传播了自由主义的福音，农民就觉醒起来，要求废止领主的苛例，发表宣言，还烧教堂，攻地主，扰动及于全国。然而这时路德却反对了，以为这种破坏的行为，大背人道，应该加以镇压，诸侯们于是放手的讨伐，恣行残酷的复仇，到第二年，农民就都失败了，境遇更加悲惨，所以他们后来就称路德为“撒谎博士”。这里刻划出来的是没有太阳的天空之下，两个耕夫在耕地，大约是弟兄，他们套着绳索，拉着犁头，几乎爬着的前进，像牛马一般，令人仿佛看见他们的流汗，听到他们的喘息。后面还该有一个扶犁的妇女，那恐怕总是他们的母亲了。
(10) "Die Pflueger". The original size is 31×45 cm. This is the first of the famous historical series "Peasant War" (Bauernkrieg). There are seven paintings, painted from 1904 to 08, all of which are engraved in bronze. Now the photocopies are also the original rubbings. The "Peasant War" is one of the largest social reform movements in modern Germany, starting in the south in 1524, when the peasants were in a state of slavery and were abused by the feudal privileges of the aristocracy; Martin Luther both promoted Protestantism and spread the gospel of liberalism, and the peasants woke up, demanded the abolition of the harsh rules of the lords, issued manifestos, burned churches, attacked landlords, and disturbed the whole country. However, Luther objected at this time, thinking that this kind of destruction was very inhumane and should be suppressed, so the princes let go of the crusade and carried out cruel revenge, and by the second year, the peasants had failed, and the situation was even more miserable, so they later called Luther "Dr. Liar". What is depicted here is two plowmen plowing the land under the sunless sky, about brothers, they are ropes and pulling plowshares, almost crawling forward, like cattle and horses, as if they can see their sweat and hear their breathing. There should be a woman holding the plow in the back, and it will probably always be their mother.（11）《凌辱》（Vergewaltigt）。同上的第二幅，原大35×53cm.男人们的受苦还没有激起变乱，但农妇也遭到可耻的凌辱了；她反缚两手，躺着，下颏向天，不见脸。死了，还是昏着呢，我们不知道。只见一路的野草都被蹂躏，显着曾经格斗的样子，较远之处，却站着可爱的小小的葵花。
(11) "Humiliation" (Vergewaltigt). The second picture of the same as above, the original size is 35×53cm. The suffering of the men has not yet provoked chaos, but the peasant woman has also been shamefully humiliated; she tied her hands behind her back, lay down, and lowered her chin to the sky, without seeing her face. Dead or unconscious, we don't know. I saw that all the weeds along the way were ravaged, and it looked like they had fought, but in the distance, there were cute little sunflowers.（12）《磨镰刀》（Beim Dengeln）。同上的第三幅，原大30×30cm.这里就出现了饱尝苦楚的女人，她的壮大粗糙的手，在用一块磨石，磨快大镰刀的刀锋，她那小小的两眼里，是充满着极顶的憎恶和愤怒。
(12) "Sharpening the Scythe" (Beim Dengeln). The third picture of the same as above, the original size is 30×30cm. Here appears a woman who has suffered a lot, her strong and rough hands, sharpening the blade of the big sickle with a millstone, and her small eyes are full of extreme hatred and anger.（13）《圆洞门里的武装》（Bewaffnung In Einem Gewoelbe）。同上的第四幅，原大50×33cm.大家都在一个阴暗的圆洞门下武装了起来，从狭窄的戈谛克式阶级蜂涌而上：是一大群拚死的农民。光线愈高愈少；奇特的半暗，阴森的人相。
(13) "Bewaffnung In Einem Gewoelbe" (Bewaffnung In Einem Gewoelbe). The fourth picture is the same as above, originally 50×33 cm. Everyone is armed under a gloomy round door, and from the narrow Godik class swarms up: a large group of desperate peasants. The higher the light, the less it is; Strange semi-dark, gloomy physiognomy.（14）《反抗》（Losbruch）。同上的第五幅，原大51×50cm.谁都在草地上没命的向前，最先是少年，喝令的却是一个女人，从全体上洋溢着复仇的愤怒。她浑身是力，挥手顿足，不但令人看了就生勇往直前之心，还好像天上的云，也应声裂成片片。她的姿态，是所有名画中最有力量的女性的一个。也如《织工一揆》里一样，女性总是参加着非常的事变，而且极有力，这也就是“这有丈夫气概的妇人”的精神。
(14) "Resistance" (Losbruch). The fifth picture of the same as above, the original size is 51×50cm. Everyone is dying on the grass and moving forward, the first is the teenager, but the one who calls is a woman, and the whole is full of vengeful anger. She was full of strength and waved her hands, which not only made people feel brave when they saw it, but also like clouds in the sky, which also cracked into pieces. Her posture is the most powerful woman in all famous paintings. Just like in "The Weaver's Ikki", women always participate in extraordinary events, and they are extremely powerful, which is the spirit of "this husbandly woman".（15）《战场》（Schlachtfeld）。同上的第六幅，原大41×53cm.农民们打败了，他们敌不过官兵。剩在战场上的是什么呢？几乎看不清东西。只在隐约看见尸横遍野的黑夜中，有一个妇人，用风灯照出她一只劳作到满是筋节的手，在触动一个死尸的下巴。光线都集中在这一小块上。这，恐怕正是她的儿子，这处所，恐怕正是她先前扶犁的地方，但现在流着的却不是汗而是鲜血了。
(15) "Battlefield" (Schlachtfeld). The sixth picture of the same as above, the original size is 41×53cm. The peasants were defeated, and they were no match for the officers and soldiers. What is left on the battlefield? Almost impossible to see. In the dark night when corpses were vaguely seen, a woman was touching the chin of a corpse with a wind lamp shining on her hand full of tendons. The light is focused on this small area. This is probably her son, this place is probably the place where she used to plow, but now it is not sweat but blood.（16）《俘虏》（Die Gefangenen）。同上的第七幅，原大33×42cm.画里是被捕的孑遗，有赤脚的，有穿木鞋的，都是强有力的汉子，但竟也有儿童，个个反缚两手，禁在绳圈里。他们的运命，是可想而知的了，但各人的神气，有已绝望的，有还是倔强或愤怒的，也有自在沉思的，却不见有什么萎靡或屈服。
(16) "Captive" (Die Gefangenen). The seventh picture of the same as above, the original size is 33×42cm. In the painting are arrested widows, some barefoot, some wearing wooden shoes, all strong men, but there are also children, all of whom are bound with their hands behind their backs and confined in rope rings. Their fate can be imagined, but everyone's spirit is desperate, some are still stubborn or angry, and some are free to contemplate, but there is no malaise or submission.（17）《失业》（Arbeitslosigkeit）。一九〇九年作，铜刻；据《画帖》，原大44×54cm.他现在闲空了，坐在她的床边，思索着——然而什么法子也想不出。那母亲和睡着的孩子们的模样，很美妙而崇高，为作者的作品中所罕见。
(17) "Unemployment" (Arbeitslosigkeit). Made in 1909, bronze engraving; According to the "Picture Post", the original size is 44×54cm. He is now idle, sitting on the edge of her bed, thinking—but he can't think of any way. The appearance of the mother and the sleeping children is wonderful and sublime, which is rare in the author's works.（18）《妇人为死亡所捕获》（Frau Vom Tod Gepackt），亦名《死和女人》（Tod Und Weib）。一九一〇年作，铜刻；据《画帖》，原大未详。“死”从她本身的阴影中出现，由背后来袭击她，将她缠住，反剪了；剩下弱小的孩子，无法叫回他自己的慈爱的母亲。一转眼间，对面就是两界。“死”是世界上最出众的拳师，死亡是现社会最动人的悲剧，而这妇人则是全作品中最伟大的一人。
(18) "Frau Vom Tod Gepackt" (Woman Captured by Death), also known as "Death and Woman" (Tod und Weib). Made in 1910, bronze engraving; According to the "Picture Post", the original size is unknown. In the blink of an eye, the opposite side is the two realms. "Death" is the most outstanding boxer in the world, death is the most moving tragedy in modern society, and this woman is the greatest person in the whole work.（19）《母与子》（Mutter Und Kind）。制作年代未详，铜刻；据《画帖》，原大19×13cm.在《凯绥·珂勒惠支作品集》中所见的百八十二幅中，可指为快乐的不过四五幅，这就是其一。亚斐那留斯以为从特地描写着孩子的呆气的侧脸，用光亮衬托出来之处，颇令人觉得有些忍俊不禁。
(19) "Mother and Son" (Mutter und Kind). The date of production is unknown, bronze engraving; According to the "Painting Post", the original size is 19×13cm. Aphinarius thought that the place where the child's dull profile was specially described and set off with light was quite funny.（20）《面包！》（Brot！）。石刻，制作年代未详，想当在欧洲大战之后；据原拓本，原大30×28cm.饥饿的孩子的急切的索食，是最碎裂了做母亲的的心的。这里是孩子们徒然张着悲哀，而热烈地希望着的眼，母亲却只能弯了无力的腰。她的肩膀耸了起来，是在背人饮泣。她背着人，因为肯帮助的和她一样的无力，而有力的是横竖不肯帮助的。她也不愿意给孩子们看见这是剩在她这里的仅有的慈爱。
(20) "Bread! 》（Brot！ ）。 The stone carving, the date of production is unknown, presumably after the European War; According to the original rubbing, the original size is 30×28cm. The eager request for food of the hungry child is the most broken mother's heart. Here are the children's eyes that are sad and hopeful in vain, but the mother can only bend her weak waist. Her shoulders shrugged, and she was crying behind her back. She carried people behind her back, because those who were willing to help were as powerless as her, and those who were powerful were those who refused to help. She also did not want to show her children that this was the only love left for her.（21）《德国的孩子们饿着！》（Deutschlands Kinder Hungern！）。石刻，制作年代未详，想当在欧洲大战之后；据原拓本，原大43×29cm.他们都擎着空碗向人，瘦削的脸上的圆睁的眼睛里，炎炎的燃着如火的热望。谁伸出手来呢？这里无从知道。这原是横幅，一面写着现在作为标题的一句，大约是当时募捐的揭帖。后来印行的，却只存了图画。作者还有一幅石刻，题为《决不再战！》（Nie Wieder Krieg！），是略早的石刻，可惜不能搜得；而那时的孩子，存留至今的，则已都成了二十以上的青年，可又将被驱作兵火的粮食了。
(21) "The German Children Are Hungry!" 》（Deutschlands Kinder Hungern！ ）。 The stone carving, the date of production is unknown, presumably after the European War; According to the original rubbing, the original size is 43×29cm. 记苏联版画展览会

记苏联版画展览会

记苏联版画展览会

Record the exhibition of prints in the USSR我记得曾有一个时候，我们很少能够从本国的刊物上，知道一点苏联的情形。虽是文艺罢，有些可敬的作家和学者们，也如千金小姐的遇到柏油一样，不但决不沾手，离得还远呢，却已经皱起了鼻子。近一两年可不同了，自然间或还看见几幅从外国刊物上取来的讽刺画，但更多的是真心的绍介着建设的成绩，令人抬起头来，看见飞机，水闸，工人住宅，集体农场，不再专门两眼看地，惦记着破皮鞋摇头叹气了。这些绍介者，都并非有所谓可怕的政治倾向的人，但决不幸灾乐祸，因此看得邻人的平和的繁荣，也就非常高兴，并且将这高兴来分给中国人。我以为为中国和苏联两国起见，这现象是极好的，一面是真相为我们所知道，得到了解，一面是不再误解，而且证明了我们中国，确有许多“威武不能屈，贫贱不能移”的必说真话的人们。
I remember a time when we could rarely know a little about the Soviet Union from our own publications. Although it is literature and art, some respectable writers and scholars, like Miss Qianjin's encounter with tar, not only will they never touch their hands, but they are still far away, but they have already wrinkled their noses. In the past year or two, it has been different, and naturally I may see a few satirical paintings taken from foreign publications, but more of them are sincere about the achievements of construction, which makes people raise their heads and see airplanes, sluices, workers' houses, collective farms, no longer looking at the ground with two eyes, thinking about the broken leather shoes and shaking their heads and sighing. These introducers are not people with so-called terrible political tendencies, but they are unfortunate and happy to be happy to see the peace and prosperity of their neighbors, and they share this happiness with the Chinese. I think this phenomenon is excellent for the sake of China and the Soviet Union, on the one hand, the truth is known and understood, and on the other hand, it is no longer misunderstood, and it proves that there are indeed many people in China who must tell the truth who are "mighty and unyielding, and poverty cannot be moved".但那些绍介，都是文章或照相，今年的版画展览会，却将艺术直接陈列在我们眼前了。作者之中，很有几个是由于作品的复制，姓名已为我们所熟识的，但现在才看到手制的原作，使我们更加觉得亲密。
But those introductions are all articles or photos, and this year's printmaking exhibition displays art directly in front of our eyes. Many of the authors are already familiar to us due to the reproduction of their works, but now we have seen the original handmade works, which makes us feel even more intimate.版画之中，木刻是中国早已发明的，但中途衰退，五年前从新兴起的是取法于欧洲，与古代木刻并无关系。不久，就遭压迫，又缺师资，所以至今不见有特别的进步。我们在这会里才得了极好，极多的模范。首先应该注意的是内战时期，就改革木刻，从此不断的前进的巨匠法复尔斯基（V. Favorsky），和他的一派兑内加（A. Deineka），冈察洛夫（A. Goncharov），叶卡斯托夫（G. Echeistov），毕珂夫（M. Pikov）等，他们在作品里各各表现着真挚的精神，继起者怎样照着导师所指示的道路，却用不同的方法，使我们知道只要内容相同，方法不妨各异，而依傍和模仿，决不能产生真艺术。
Among printmaking, woodcut has long been invented in China, but it has declined midway, and the emerging one five years ago was taken from Europe, which has nothing to do with ancient woodcuts. Soon, it was oppressed and lacked teachers, so there has been no special progress so far. We have received excellent and many models in this meeting. First of all, it should be noted that during the Civil War, the great master V. Favursky (V. Favresky), who reformed woodcuts and continued to advance ever since. Favorsky), and his faction of A. Favorsky. Deineka), A. Goncharov (A. Goncharov), G. Echeistov), M. Bikov (M. Pikov) and others, they each express their sincere spirit in their works, how the successors follow the path instructed by their mentors, but use different methods, so that we know that as long as the content is the same, the methods may be different, and relying on and imitating must not produce true art.兑内加和叶卡斯托夫的作品，是中国未曾绍介过的，可惜这里也很少；和法复尔斯基接近的保夫理诺夫（P. Pavlinov）的木刻，我们只见过一幅，现在却弥补了这缺憾了。
The works of Duenega and Ekastov have not been introduced in China, but unfortunately there are very few here; P. Pavlinov, who was close to Favorsky, Pavlinov), we have only seen one woodcut, but now it makes up for this shortcoming.克拉甫兼珂（A. Kravchenko）的木刻能够幸而寄到中国，翻印绍介了的也只有一幅，到现在大家才看见他更多的原作。他的浪漫的色彩，会鼓动我们的青年的热情，而注意于背景和细致的表现，也将使观者得到裨益。我们的绘画，从宋以来就盛行“写意”，两点是眼，不知是长是圆，一画是鸟，不知是鹰是燕，竞尚高简，变成空虚，这弊病还常见于现在的青年木刻家的作品里，克拉甫兼珂的新作《尼泊尔建造》（Dneprostroy），是惊起这种懒惰的空想的警钟。至于毕斯凯莱夫（N. Piskarev），则恐怕是最先绍介到中国来的木刻家。他的四幅《铁流》的插画，早为许多青年读者所欣赏，现在才又见了《安娜·加里尼娜》的插画，——他的刻法的别一端。
A. Kravchenko) was fortunately able to be sent to China, and only one was reprinted, and only one of his original works has been reprinted, and only now everyone has seen more of his original works. His romantic colors will inspire the enthusiasm of our youth, and attention to background and meticulous expression will also benefit the viewer. Our paintings, since the Song Dynasty, have been prevalent in "freehand", two points are eyes, I don't know if it is long or round, one painting is a bird, I don't know if it is an eagle or a swallow, competing for simplicity, becoming emptiness, this ill is also common in the works of today's young woodcarvers, Kraf Jianke's new work "Nepal Construction" (Dneprostroy), is a wake-up call for this lazy fantasy. As for Biskelev (N. Piskarev) is probably the first woodcarver to come to China. Here is also the Midrosyn (D. Mitrokhin), L. Shirensky (L. Khiz-hinsky), S. Mocharov (S. Mochalov), all known to Yuxian in China, and many artists I saw for the first time, from before the October Revolution to the early twentieth century, are young artists who were famous before the October Revolution and are showing us the way to work together to build peace. Other authors and works are briefly explained in the exhibition manual, and the main points of the whole are revealed at the end: "The content of socialism in general and the fundamental efforts for realism", which I do not need to repeat here.但我们还有应当注意的，是其中有乌克兰，乔其亚，白俄罗斯的艺术家的作品，我想，倘没有十月革命，这些作品是不但不能和我们见面，也未必会得出现的。
But we should also pay attention to the works of Ukrainian, Georgian, and Belarusian artists, which, I think, without the October Revolution, would not have been able to meet us, and they might not have appeared.现在，二百余幅的作品，是已经灿烂的一同出现于上海了。单就版画而论，使我们看起来，它不像法国木刻的多为纤美，也不像德国木刻的多为豪放；然而它真挚，却非固执，美丽，却非淫艳，愉快，却非狂欢，有力，却非粗暴；但又不是静止的，它令人觉得一种震动——这震动，恰如用坚实的步法，一步一步，踏着坚实的广大的黑土进向建设的路的大队友军的足音。
Now, more than 200 works have appeared brilliantly together in Shanghai. In terms of printmaking alone, it seems to us that it is not as delicate as French woodcuts, nor is it as bold as German woodcuts; However, it is sincere, but not stubborn, beautiful, but not lewd, pleasant, but not carnival, powerful, but not rude; But it is not static, it makes people feel a kind of vibration - this vibration is just like the footsteps of the big teammates who are stepping on the solid vast black soil to the road of construction step by step.附记：会中的版画，计有五种。一木刻，一胶刻（目录译作“油布刻”，颇怪），看名目自明。两种是用强水浸蚀铜版和石版而成的，译作“铜刻”和“石刻”固可，或如目录，译作“蚀刻”和“石印”亦无不可。还有一种Monotype，是在版上作画，再用纸印，所以虽是版画，却只一幅的东西，我想只好译作“独幅版画”。会中的说明书上译作“摩诺”，还不过等于不译，有时译为“单型学”，却未免比不译更难懂了。其实，那不提撰人的说明，是非常简而得要的，可惜译得很费解，如果有人改译一遍，即使在闭会之后，对于留心版画的人也还是很有用处的。
Note: There are five types of prints in the conference. A woodcut, a rubber engraving (the catalog is translated as "oilcloth carving", quite strange), the name is self-explanatory. The two are made by eroding copper plates and stone tablets with strong water, which can be translated as "copper carving" and "stone carving", or as in the catalog, it is also translated as "etching" and "stone seal". There is also a monotype, which is to paint on a plate and then print it on paper, so although it is a print, it is only one thing, so I think it has to be translated as "single print". The instructions in the meeting are translated as "Mono", which is only equivalent to not translating, and sometimes it is translated as "monotypic", but it is inevitably more difficult to understand than not translating. In fact, the explanation of the author is very concise and necessary, but unfortunately the translation is very confusing, and if someone retranslates it, even after the adjournment, it is still very useful for those who pay attention to printmaking.二月十七日。
February 17th.

我要骗人

我要骗人

我要骗人

I'm going to lie疲劳到没有法子的时候，也偶然佩服了超出现世的作家，要模仿一下来试试。然而不成功。超然的心，是得像贝类一样，外面非有壳不可的。而且还得有清水。浅间山边，倘是客店，那一定是有的罢，但我想，却未必有去造“象牙之塔”的人的。
When I was so tired that I couldn't do anything about it, I also occasionally admired the writers who were beyond the world, and I wanted to imitate it. However, it was unsuccessful. A transcendent mind must be like a shell, and there must be a shell on the outside. And there must be clean water. On the side of Asama Mountain, if it is an inn, there must be one, but I think there may not be people who build the "Ivory Tower".为了希求心的暂时的平安，作为穷余的一策，我近来发明了别样的方法了，这就是骗人。
In order to seek temporary peace in the heart, as a way to be poor, I have recently invented another method, which is deception.去年的秋天或是冬天，日本的一个水兵，在闸北被暗杀了。忽然有了许多搬家的人，汽车租钱之类，都贵了好几倍。搬家的自然是中国人，外国人是很有趣似的站在马路旁边看。我也常常去看的。一到夜里，非常之冷静，再没有卖食物的小商人了，只听得有时从远处传来着犬吠。然而过了两三天，搬家好像被禁止了。警察拚死命的在殴打那些拉着行李的大车夫和洋车夫，日本的报章，中国的报章，都异口同声的对于搬了家的人们给了一个“愚民”的徽号。这意思就是说，其实是天下太平的，只因为有这样的“愚民”，所以把颇好的天下，弄得乱七八糟了。
Last autumn or winter, a Japanese sailor was assassinated in Zhabei. Suddenly, there are many people moving, and car rental is several times more expensive. Naturally, the Chinese moved and the foreigners stood by the road as if they were very interested. I also go to see it often. At night, it was very calm, and there were no small merchants selling food anymore, only sometimes I heard the barking of dogs from afar. However, after two or three days, it seems that moving is prohibited. The police are desperately beating the big coachmen and foreign coachmen who are pulling luggage, and Japanese newspapers and Chinese newspapers have all given a "foolish people" badge to those who have moved. This means that in fact, the world is peaceful, just because there are such "foolish people", so the good world is in a mess.我自始至终没有动，并未加入“愚民”这一伙里。但这并非为了聪明，却只因为懒惰。也曾陷在五年前的正月的上海战争——日本那一面，好像是喜欢称为“事变”似的——的火线下，而且自由早被剥夺，夺了我的自由的权力者，又拿着这飞上空中了，所以无论跑到那里去，都是一个样。中国的人民是多疑的。无论那一国人，都指这为可笑的缺点。然而怀疑并不是缺点。总是疑，而并不下断语，这才是缺点。我是中国人，所以深知道这秘密。其实，是在下着断语的，而这断语，乃是：到底还是不可信。但后来的事实，却大抵证明了这断语的的确。中国人不疑自己的多疑。所以我的没有搬家，也并不是因为怀着天下太平的确信，说到底，仍不过为了无论那里都一样的危险的缘故。五年以前翻阅报章，看见过所记的孩子的死尸的数目之多，和从不见有记着交换俘虏的事，至今想起来，也还是非常悲痛的。
I didn't move from beginning to end, and I didn't join the group of "fools". But this is not for being smart, but only for laziness. I was also trapped in the line of fire of the Shanghai War in the first month of five years ago - the Japanese side seems to like to call it a "incident" - and my freedom had long been deprived of it, and the power that took away my freedom flew into the air with it, so no matter where I went, it was the same. The Chinese people are suspicious. No matter which country they are, they all point to this as a ridiculous shortcoming. However, skepticism is not a disadvantage. Always doubting without making assertions is a disadvantage. I am Chinese, so I know this secret very well. In fact, it is made with an assertiveness, and this assertion is: it is still not credible. But later facts largely proved the truth of this assertion. The Chinese do not doubt their suspiciousness. So I didn't move, not because I was convinced that the world would be peaceful, but because of the same danger everywhere. Five years ago, I flipped through the newspapers and saw the number of dead bodies of children I had recorded, and I never saw any record of the exchange of prisoners, and I am still very sad when I think about it.虐待搬家人，殴打车夫，还是极小的事情。中国的人民，是常用自己的血，去洗权力者的手，使他又变成洁净的人物的，现在单是这模样就完事，总算好得很。
Abusing the moving family and beating the coachman is still a very small thing. The Chinese people often use their own blood to wash the hands of those in power, so that they can become clean figures again.但当大家正在搬家的时候，我也没有整天站在路旁看热闹，或者坐在家里读世界文学史之类的心思。走远一点，到电影院里散闷去。一到那里，可真是天下太平了。这就是大家搬家去住的处所。我刚要跨进大门，被一个十二三岁的女孩子捉住了。是小学生，在募集水灾的捐款，因为冷，连鼻子尖也冻得通红。我说没有零钱，她就用眼睛表示了非常的失望。我觉得对不起人，就带她进了电影院，买过门票之后，付给她一块钱。她这回是非常高兴了，称赞我道，“你是好人”，还写给我一张收条。只要拿着这收条，就无论到那里，都没有再出捐款的必要。于是我，就是所谓“好人”，也轻松的走进里面了。
But when everyone was moving, I didn't stand on the side of the road all day watching the excitement, or sit at home reading the history of world literature. Go a little further and go to the cinema to relieve boredom. Once there, the world is really peaceful. This is where everyone moves to live. I was about to step through the door when I was caught by a twelve or thirteen-year-old girl. He was an elementary school student, and he was collecting donations for the flood, and because of the cold, even the tip of his nose was red from the cold. I said there was no change, and she expressed her disappointment with her eyes. I felt sorry for someone, so I took her into the cinema, bought a ticket, and paid her a dollar. She was very happy this time, praised me, "You are a good person", and wrote me a receipt. As long as you hold this receipt, no matter where you go, there is no need to make a donation. So I, the so-called "good person", also walked into it easily.看了什么电影呢？现在已经丝毫也记不起。总之，大约不外乎一个英国人，为着祖国，征服了印度的残酷的酋长，或者一个美国人，到亚非利加去，发了大财，和绝世的美人结婚之类罢。这样的消遣了一些时光，傍晚回家，又走进了静悄悄的环境。听到远地里的犬吠声。女孩子的满足的表情的相貌，又在眼前出现，自己觉得做了好事情了，但心情又立刻不舒服起来，好像嚼了肥皂或者什么一样。
What movie did you watch? I can't remember it at all now. In short, it is probably nothing more than a cruel chieftain who conquered India for the sake of his homeland, or an American who went to Asia and Africa, made a fortune, and married a peerless beauty. After spending some time like this, I went home in the evening and walked into a quiet environment again. Hear the barking of dogs in the distance. The appearance of the girl's satisfied expression appeared in front of her eyes again, and she felt that she had done a good thing, but her mood immediately became uncomfortable again, as if she had chewed soap or something.诚然，两三年前，是有过非常的水灾的，这大水和日本的不同，几个月或半年都不退。但我又知道，中国有着叫作“水利局”的机关，每年从人民收着税钱，在办事。但反而出了这样的大水了。我又知道，有一个团体演了戏来筹钱，因为后来只有二十几元，衙门就发怒不肯要。连被水灾所害的难民成群的跑到安全之处来，说是有害治安，就用机关枪去扫射的话也都听到过。恐怕早已统统死掉了罢。然而孩子们不知道，还在拚命的替死人募集生活费，募不到，就失望，募到手，就喜欢。而其实，一块来钱，是连给水利局的老爷买一天的烟卷也不够的。我明明知道着，却好像也相信款子真会到灾民的手里似的，付了一块钱。实则不过买了这天真烂漫的孩子的欢喜罢了。我不爱看人们的失望的样子。
It is true that two or three years ago, there was a very flood, which was different from Japan, and did not recede for several months or half a year. But I also know that China has an agency called the "Water Conservancy Bureau", which collects tax money from the people every year and is doing things. But there was such a flood instead. I also knew that there was a group that acted to raise money, because it was only more than 20 yuan, and the yamen was angry and refused to ask for it. Even refugees affected by floods have run to safety in droves, saying that it is harmful to public order, and they have been shot with machine guns. I'm afraid they are all dead long ago. However, the children don't know that they are still desperately trying to raise living expenses for the dead, and if they can't raise money, they will be disappointed, and if they can raise money, they will like it. In fact, one piece of money is not enough to buy cigarettes for a day for the master of the Water Conservancy Bureau. I knew it, but I also seemed to believe that the money would really go to the victims, so I paid a dollar. In fact, it's just the joy of buying this innocent child. I don't like to see people disappointed.倘使我那八十岁的母亲，问我天国是否真有，我大约是会毫不踌蹰，答道真有的罢。
If my eighty-year-old mother asked me if the kingdom of heaven really existed, I would probably answer without hesitation.然而这一天的后来的心情却不舒服。好像是又以为孩子和老人不同，骗她是不应该似的，想写一封公开信，说明自己的本心，去消释误解，但又想到横竖没有发表之处，于是中止了，时候已是夜里十二点钟。到门外去看了一下。
However, the mood later on this day was uncomfortable. As if she thought that children were different from the old man, and that she shouldn't lie to her, she wanted to write an open letter to explain her true intentions and dispel misunderstandings, but she thought that there was no place to publish horizontally and vertically, so she stopped, and it was already twelve o'clock in the night. I went outside the door to take a look.已经连人影子也看不见。只在一家的檐下，有一个卖馄饨的，在和两个警察谈闲天。这是一个平时不大看见的特别穷苦的肩贩，存着的材料多得很，可见他并无生意。用两角钱买了两碗，和我的女人两个人分吃了。算是给他赚一点钱。
I can't even see the shadow of a person. Only under the eaves of a family, there was a wonton seller who was chatting with two policemen. This is a particularly poor shoulder vendor who is not usually seen, and he has a lot of materials in store, which shows that he has no business. I bought two bowls for two dimes and shared them with my woman. It's to make him a little money.庄子曾经说过：“干下去的（曾经积水的）车辙里的鲋鱼，彼此用唾沫相湿，用湿气相嘘，”——然而他又说，“倒不如在江湖里，大家互相忘却的好。”
Zhuangzi once said: "The crucian carp in the ruts that have been dried up (once stagnant water) wet each other with saliva and booe each other with moisture," - but he also said, "It is better to forget each other in the rivers and lakes." ”可悲的是我们不能互相忘却。而我，却愈加恣意的骗起人来了。如果这骗人的学问不毕业，或者不中止，恐怕是写不出圆满的文章来的。
Sadly, we can't forget each other. And I, on the other hand, are deceiving people more and more arbitrarily. If this deceptive knowledge does not graduate or stop, I am afraid that it will not be able to write a satisfactory article.但不幸而在既未卒业，又未中止之际，遇到山本社长了。因为要我写一点什么，就在礼仪上，答道“可以的”。因为说过“可以”，就应该写出来，不要使他失望，然而到底也还是写了骗人的文章。
But unfortunately, before I finished my business and did not stop, I met President Yamamoto. Because if I were asked to write something, I would reply "yes" in terms of etiquette. Because he said "yes", he should write it and not disappoint him, but in the end he still wrote a deceptive article.写着这样的文章，也不是怎么舒服的心地。要说的话多得很，但得等候“中日亲善”更加增进的时光。不久之后，恐怕那“亲善”的程度，竟会到在我们中国，认为排日即国贼——因为说是共产党利用了排日的口号，使中国灭亡的缘故——而到处的断头台上，都闪烁着太阳的圆圈的罢，但即使到了这样子，也还不是披沥真实的心的时光。
Writing such an article is not very comfortable. There is a lot to say, but we have to wait for the time when the "Sino-Japanese friendship" will be further enhanced. Soon, I am afraid that the degree of "goodwill" will reach the point where in our China, we think that anti-Japanese is a national traitor - because it is said that the Communist Party used the slogan of anti-Japanese to bring about the destruction of China - and the guillotine everywhere is full of circles of the sun, but even if it reaches this point, it is not the time to pour out the true heart.单是自己一个人的过虑也说不定：要彼此看见和了解真实的心，倘能用了笔，舌，或者如宗教家之所谓眼泪洗明了眼睛那样的便当的方法，那固然是非常之好的，然而这样便宜事，恐怕世界上也很少有。这是可以悲哀的。一面写着漫无条理的文章，一面又觉得对不起热心的读者了。
It may be the fault of one person alone: to see and understand each other's true hearts, if they can use a pen, tongue, or a convenient method like the so-called tears that wash the eyes with tears, it is very good, but I am afraid that there are very few such cheap things in the world. This can be sad. While writing an unorganized article, I feel sorry for the enthusiastic readers.临末，用血写添几句个人的豫感，算是一个答礼罢。
At the end, write a few words of personal premonition with blood, which is a return gift.二月二十三日。

《译文》复刊词

《译文》复刊词

《译文》复刊词

The translation was reprinted先来引几句古书，——也许记的不真确，——庄子曰：“涸辙之鲋，相濡以沫，相煦以湿，——不若相忘于江湖。”
First of all, I will quote a few sentences from ancient books,—— maybe the memory is not true,—— Zhuangzi said: "The crucian carp in the dry rut, wet with each other, warm and wet,—— it is better to forget each other in the rivers and lakes." ”《译文》就在一九三四年九月中，在这样的状态之下出世的。那时候，鸿篇巨制如《世界文学》和《世界文库》之类，还没有诞生，所以在这青黄不接之际，大约可以说是仿佛戈壁中的绿洲，几个人偷点余暇，译些短文，彼此看看，倘有读者，也大家看看，自寻一点乐趣，也希望或者有一点益处，——但自然，这决不是江湖之大。
The "Translation" was born in mid-September 1934, in this state. At that time, masterpieces such as "World Literature" and "World Library" had not yet been born, so at this time of disappointment, it can be said that it was like an oasis in the Gobi, several people stole some leisure time, translated some short articles, looked at each other, if there were readers, everyone would also take a look, find a little fun for themselves, and hope or have a little benefit,—— But naturally, this is by no means a big deal.不过这与世无争的小小的期刊，终于不能不在去年九月，以“终刊号”和大家告别了。虽然不过野花小草，但曾经费过不少移栽灌溉之力，当然不免私心以为可惜的。然而竟也得了勇气和慰安：这是许多读者用了笔和舌，对于《译文》的凭吊。
However, this small journal that is indisputable finally had to say goodbye to everyone with the "final issue" in September last year. Although it is just a wildflower grass, it has spent a lot of power on transplanting and irrigation, of course, it is a pity. However, it also gained courage and comfort: this is the reason why many readers have used their pens and tongues to hang on the "Translation".我们知道感谢，我们知道自勉。
We know to be grateful, we know to encourage ourselves.我们也不断的希望复刊。但那时风传的关于终刊的原因：是折本。出版家虽然大抵是“传播文化”的，而“折本”却是“传播文化”的致命伤，所以荏苒半年，简直死得无药可救。直到今年，折本说这才起了动摇，得到再造的运会，再和大家相见了。
We also continue to hope for the resumption of publication. But at that time, the reason for the final publication was that it was a folded version. Although publishers are mostly "spreading culture", "folding money" is the fatal wound of "spreading culture", so half a year has passed, and it is simply hopeless. It wasn't until this year that Zhe Ben said that this was shaken, and he got the rebuilt Games and met everyone again.内容仍如创刊时候的《前记》里所说一样：原料没有限制；门类也没有固定；文字之外多加图画，也有和文字有关系的，意在助趣，也有和文字没有关系的，那就算是我们贡献给读者的一点小意思。
The content is still the same as what was said in the "Preface" at the time of its inception: there is no limit to raw materials; There is no fixed category; Add more pictures in addition to the text, some are related to the text, are intended to help fun, and some have nothing to do with the text, which is a little meaning we contribute to the reader.这一回，将来的运命如何呢？我们不知道。但今年文坛的情形突变，已在宣扬宽容和大度了，我们真希望在这宽容和大度的文坛里，《译文》也能够托庇比较的长生。
This time, what is the fate of the future? We don't know. But this year's sudden change in the literary world is already preaching tolerance and generosity, and we really hope that in this tolerant and generous literary world, "Translation" can also support comparative longevity.三月八日。
March 8th.

白莽作《孩儿塔》序

白莽作《孩儿塔》序

白莽作《孩儿塔》序

Bai Mang wrote the preface to "The Children's Tower."春天去了一大半了，还是冷；加上整天的下雨，淅淅沥沥，深夜独坐，听得令人有些凄凉，也因为午后得到一封远道寄来的信，要我给白莽的遗诗写一点序文之类；那信的开首说道：“我的亡友白莽，恐怕你是知道的罢。……”——这就使我更加惆怅。
Spring is more than half gone, and it is still cold; Coupled with the rain all day long, dripping, sitting alone late at night, it was a little desolate to listen to, and because I got a letter from afar in the afternoon, asking me to write a little preface to Bai Mang's posthumous poems; The letter began with the words: "My deceased friend Bai Mang, I'm afraid you know." ......" - this made me even more melancholy.说起白莽来，——不错，我知道的。四年之前，我曾经写过一篇《为忘却的记念》，要将他们忘却。他们就义了已经足有五个年头了，我的记忆上，早又蒙上许多新鲜的血迹；这一提，他的年青的相貌就又在我的眼前出现，像活着一样，热天穿着大棉袍，满脸油汗，笑笑的对我说道：“这是第三回了。自己出来的。前两回都是哥哥保出，他一保就要干涉我，这回我不去通知他了。……”——我前一回的文章上是猜错的，这哥哥才是徐培根，航空署长，终于和他成了殊途同归的兄弟；他却叫徐白，较普通的笔名是殷夫。
Speaking of Bai Mang, it's ,—— good, I know. Four years ago, I wrote an article "For the Memory of Forgetting" to forget them. They have been righteous for five years, and my memory has long been covered with a lot of fresh blood; At this mention, his youthful appearance appeared in front of my eyes again, as if he was alive, wearing a big cotton robe on a hot day, his face was full of oil and sweat, and he said to me with a smile: "This is the third time." It came out by itself. The first two times my brother guaranteed it, and he was going to interfere with me as soon as he guaranteed it, but this time I won't notify him. ......" - I guessed wrong in my previous article, this brother is Xu Bacon, the director of aviation, and finally became a brother with him; His name is Xu Bai, and his more common pseudonym is Yin Fu.一个人如果还有友情，那么，收存亡友的遗文真如捏着一团火，常要觉得寝食不安，给它企图流布的。这心情我很了然，也知道有做序文之类的义务。我所惆怅的是我简直不懂诗，也没有诗人的朋友，偶尔一有，也终至于闹开，不过和白莽没有闹，也许是他死得太快了罢。现在，对于他的诗，我一句也不说——因为我不能。
If a person still has friendship, then the posthumous writings of living and deceased friends are really like holding a fire, and they often feel restless and try to spread it. I understand this feeling, and I also know that I have an obligation to write a preface. What I am sad about is that I don't understand poetry at all, and I don't have friends with poets, and if I have it occasionally, I will eventually make trouble, but I didn't make trouble with Bai Mang, maybe he died too quickly. Now, I don't say a word about his poems - because I can't.这《孩儿塔》的出世并非要和现在一般的诗人争一日之长，是有别一种意义在。这是东方的微光，是林中的响箭，是冬末的萌芽，是进军的第一步，是对于前驱者的爱的大纛，也是对于摧残者的憎的丰碑。一切所谓圆熟简练，静穆幽远之作，都无须来作比方，因为这诗属于别一世界。
The birth of this "Children's Tower" is not to compete with ordinary poets today, but to have a different meaning. This is the glimmer of the east, the arrow in the forest, the sprout of the end of winter, the first step of the march, the banner of love for the vanguard, and the monument to the hatred of the destroyer. All the so-called perfect, concise, quiet and distant works do not need to be metaphorized, because this poem belongs to another world.那一世界里有许多许多人，白莽也是他们的亡友。单是这一点，我想，就足够保证这本集子的存在了，又何需我的序文之类。
There were many people in that world, and Bai Mang was also their dead friend. This alone, I think, is enough to ensure the existence of this collection, so why do I need a preface or the like.一九三六年三月十一夜，鲁迅记于上海之且介亭。
On the night of March 11, 1936, Lu Xun recorded in the Qiejie Pavilion in Shanghai.

Continued note这是三月十日的事。我得到一个不相识者由汉口寄来的信，自说和白莽是同济学校的同学，藏有他的遗稿《孩儿塔》，正在经营出版，但出版家有一个要求：要我做一篇序；至于原稿，因为纸张零碎，不寄来了，不过如果要看的话，却也可以补寄。其实，白莽的《孩儿塔》的稿子，却和几个同时受难者的零星遗稿，都在我这里，里面还有他亲笔的插画，但在他的朋友手里别有初稿，也是可能的；至于出版家要有一篇序，那更是平常事。
This was on March 10th. I got a letter from an unknown person from Hankou, saying that he and Bai Mang were classmates at Tongji School, and that he had his posthumous manuscript "Children's Tower" and was running a publishing operation, but the publisher had a request: he wanted me to write a preface; As for the original manuscript, it was not sent because the paper was fragmented, but if you want to see it, you can also send it back. In fact, the manuscript of Bai Mang's "Children's Tower", along with the sporadic manuscripts of several contemporaneous victims, is with me, and there are also his own illustrations, but it is also possible to have a different first draft in the hands of his friends; As for publishers to have a preface, it is even more common.近两年来，大开了印卖遗著的风气，虽是期刊，也常有死人和活人合作的，但这已不是先前的所谓“骸骨的迷恋”，倒是活人在依靠死人的余光，想用“死诸葛吓走生仲达”。我不大佩服这些活家伙。可是这一回却很受了感动，因为一个人受了难，或者遭了冤，所谓先前的朋友，一声不响的固然有，连赶紧来投几块石子，借此表明自己是属于胜利者一方面的，也并不算怎么希罕；至于抱守遗文，历多年还要给它出版，以尽对于亡友的交谊者，以我之孤陋寡闻，可实在很少知道。大病初愈，才能起坐，夜雨淅沥，怆然有怀，便力疾写了一点短文，到第二天付邮寄去，因为恐怕连累付印者，所以不题他的姓名；过了几天，才又投给《文学丛报》，因为恐怕妨碍发行，所以又隐下了诗的名目。
In the past two years, the trend of printing and selling posthumous works has been greatly opened, although it is a periodical, and there are often dead people and living people cooperating, but this is no longer the previous so-called "obsession with bones", but the living are relying on the afterglow of the dead, wanting to use "dead Zhuge to scare away Sheng Zhongda". I don't admire these living guys very much. But this time I was very moved, because a person suffered, or suffered injustice, the so-called previous friends, of course, there were silent friends, and even hurriedly came to throw a few stones, so as to show that they belonged to the victor's side, which was not very rare; As for the posthumous writings, they have to be published for many years, so as to make friends with my deceased friends, but I really rarely know about them. When he had just recovered from a serious illness, he could only sit up, and the night rain was dripping, and he was sad, so he wrote a short article and mailed it the next day, because he was afraid that it would affect the printer, so he did not write his name; A few days later, it was submitted to the "Literary Series", because it was afraid that it would hinder the distribution, so the name of the poem was hidden.此后不多几天，看见《社会日报》，说是善于翻戏的史济行，现又化名为齐涵之了。我这才悟到自己竟受了骗，因为汉口的发信者，署名正是齐涵之。他仍在玩着骗取文稿的老套，《孩儿塔》不但不会出版，大约他连初稿也未必有的，不过知道白莽和我相识，以及他的诗集的名目罢了。
Not long after that, I saw the "Social Daily", saying that it was Shi Jixing, who was good at turning dramas, and now he was pseudonymously Qi Hanzhi. Only then did I realize that I had been deceived, because the sender of Hankou signed Qi Hanzhi. He is still playing with the old trick of deceiving manuscripts, not only will "Children's Tower" not be published, probably he may not even have the first draft, but he knows that Bai Mang and I know each other, and the title of his poetry collection.至于史济行和我的通信，却早得很，还是八九年前，我在编辑《语丝》，创造社和太阳社联合起来向我围剿的时候，他就自称是一个艺术专门学校的学生，信件在我眼前出现了，投稿是几则当时所谓革命文豪的劣迹，信里还说这类文稿，可以源源的寄来。然而《语丝》里是没有“劣迹栏”的，我也不想和这种“作家”往来，于是当时即加以拒绝。后来他又或者化名“彳亍”，在刊物上捏造我的谣言，或者忽又化为“天行”（《语丝》也有同名的文字，但是别一人）或“史岩”，卑词征求我的文稿，我总给他一个置之不理。这一回，他在汉口，我是听到过的，但不能因为一个史济行在汉口，便将一切汉口的不相识者的信都看作卑劣者的圈套，我虽以多疑为忠厚长者所诟病，但这样多疑的程度是还不到的。不料人还是大意不得，偶不疑虑，偶动友情，到底成为我的弱点了。
As for Shi Jixing's correspondence with me, it was very early, or eight or nine years ago, when I was editing "Yusi", and the Creation Society and the Sun Society united to encircle and suppress me, he claimed to be a student of an art college, and the letter appeared in front of my eyes, and the submission was several bad deeds of the so-called revolutionary writers at that time, and the letter also said that such manuscripts could be sent in a steady stream. However, there is no "bad deeds column" in "Yusi", and I didn't want to associate with this kind of "writer", so I refused it at that time. Later, he either changed his name to "彳庍" and fabricated my rumors in the publication, or suddenly turned into "Tianxing" ("Yusi" also has a text of the same name, but no one else) or "Shi Yan", and asked for my manuscript in a despicable way, but I always ignored it. This time, he was in Hankou, I have heard of it, but I can't regard all the letters of strangers in Hankou as a trap of despicable people just because a Shi Jixing is in Hankou. Unexpectedly, people are still careless, occasionally unsuspicious, and occasionally friendship, which has become my weakness.今天又看见了所谓“汉出”的《人间世》的第二期，卷末写着“主编史天行”，而下期要目的豫告上，果然有我的《序〈孩儿塔〉》在。但卷端又声明着下期要更名为《西北风》了，那么，我的序文，自然就卷在第一阵“西北风”里。而第二期的第一篇，竟又是我的文章，题目是《日译本〈中国小说史略〉序》。这原是我用日本文所写的，这里却不知道何人所译，仅止一页的短文，竟充满着错误和不通，但前面却附有一行声明道：“本篇原来是我为日译本《支那小说史》写的卷头语……”乃是模拟我的语气，冒充我自己翻译的。翻译自己所写的日文，竟会满纸错误，这岂不是天下的大怪事么？
Today I saw the second issue of the so-called "Han Chu" "The World of the World", and at the end of the volume it was written "Editor-in-Chief Shi Tianxing", and the next issue was announced, and sure enough, there was my "Preface to the Children's Tower". But the end of the volume also states that the next issue will be renamed "Northwest Wind", so my preface is naturally rolled up in the first "Northwest Wind". The first article of the second issue was actually my article, titled "Preface to the Japanese Translation of the History of Chinese Novels". This was originally written by me in Japanese, but I don't know who translated it here, and the short article is only one page, which is full of errors and incomprehensions, but it is preceded by a line of statement: "This article was originally written by me for the Japanese translation of "History of Chinese Novels"...... "It was a simulated tone of my tone, pretending to be my own translation." Isn't it a big strange thing in the world to translate the Japanese you write, and the paper will be full of errors?中国原是“把人不当人”的地方，即使无端诬人为投降或转变，国贼或汉奸，社会上也并不以为奇怪。所以史济行的把戏，就更是微乎其微的事情。我所要特地声明的，只在请读了我的序文而希望《孩儿塔》出版的人，可以收回了这希望，因为这是我先受了欺骗，一转而成为我又欺骗了读者的。
China was originally a place where people were "treated as inappropriate people", and even if people were falsely accused of surrendering or converting, national traitors or traitors were not surprising in society. Therefore, Shi Jixing's trick is even more insignificant. What I want to declare is that only those who have read my preface and hope that "The Tower of Children" will be published, can withdraw this hope, because I was deceived first, and then I became the reader again.最后，我还要添几句由“多疑”而来的结论：即使真有“汉出”《孩儿塔》，这部诗也还是可疑的。我从来不想对于史济行的大事业讲一句话，但这回既经我写过一篇序，且又发表了，所以在现在或到那时，我都有指明真伪的义务和权利。
Finally, I would like to add a few conclusions from "suspiciousness": even if there is really "Han Chu" "Children's Tower", this poem is still suspicious. I never wanted to say a word about Shi Jixing's great cause, but this time I wrote a preface and published it, so I have the obligation and right to indicate the authenticity now or until then.四月十一日。
April 11th.

Written in the middle of the night一　珂勒惠支教授的版画之入中国
1. The introduction of Professor Kellerhuitt's prints into China野地上有一堆烧过的纸灰，旧墙上有几个划出的图画，经过的人是大抵未必注意的，然而这些里面，各各藏着一些意义，是爱，是悲哀，是愤怒，……而且往往比叫了出来的更猛烈。也有几个人懂得这意义。
There is a pile of burnt paper ash on the field, and there are a few drawings on the old wall, which passers-by may not pay attention to, but in these, each has some meaning, which is love, sorrow, and anger,...... And often more violently than what was screamed. There are also a few people who understand this meaning.一九三一年——我忘了月份了——创刊不久便被禁止的杂志《北斗》第一本上，有一幅木刻画，是一个母亲，悲哀的闭了眼睛，交出她的孩子去。这是珂勒惠支教授（Prof. Kaethe Kollwitz）的木刻连续画《战争》的第一幅，题目叫作《牺牲》；也是她的版画绍介进中国来的第一幅。
In 1931 - I forgot the month - there was a woodcut on the first volume of the magazine "Beidou", which was banned shortly after its launch, a mother closed her eyes sadly and handed over her child. This is Prof. Kölhuitz (Prof. Kaethe Kollwitz) is the first of a series of woodcuts "War", titled "Sacrifice"; It is also the first of her prints to be introduced into China.这幅木刻是我寄去的，算是柔石遇害的纪念。他是我的学生和朋友，一同绍介外国文艺的人，尤喜欢木刻，曾经编印过三本欧美作家的作品，虽然印得不大好。然而不知道为了什么，突然被捕了，不久就在龙华和别的五个青年作家同时枪毙。当时的报章上毫无记载，大约是不敢，也不能记载，然而许多人都明白他不在人间了，因为这是常有的事。只有他那双目失明的母亲，我知道她一定还以为她的爱子仍在上海翻译和校对。偶然看到德国书店的目录上有这幅《牺牲》，便将它投寄《北斗》了，算是我的无言的纪念。然而，后来知道，很有一些人是觉得所含的意义的，不过他们大抵以为纪念的是被害的全群。
This woodcut was sent by me, and it is a memorial to Rou Shi's murder. He is my student and friend, a person who introduces foreign literature and art, especially likes woodcuts, and has compiled and printed three works by European and American writers, although they are not very well printed. However, for some reason, he was suddenly arrested, and soon Long Hua and five other young writers were shot dead at the same time. There was no record in the newspapers at that time, probably not daring or being able to record it, but many people understood that he was no longer in the world, because this was a common occurrence. Only his blind mother, I know she must have thought that her beloved son was still translating and proofreading in Shanghai. I happened to see this "Sacrifice" in the catalog of a German bookstore, so I sent it to "Beidou", which is my silent memorial. However, I later learned that many people felt that it meant, but they probably thought it was a commemoration of the entire group of victims.这时珂勒惠支教授的版画集正在由欧洲走向中国的路上，但到得上海，勤恳的绍介者却早已睡在土里了，我们连地点也不知道。好的，我一个人来看。这里面是穷困，疾病，饥饿，死亡……自然也有挣扎和争斗，但比较的少；这正如作者的自画像，脸上虽有憎恶和愤怒，而更多的是慈爱和悲悯的相同。这是一切“被侮辱和被损害的”的母亲的心的图像。这类母亲，在中国的指甲还未染红的乡下，也常有的，然而人往往嗤笑她，说做母亲的只爱不中用的儿子。但我想，她是也爱中用的儿子的，只因为既然强壮而有能力，她便放了心，去注意“被侮辱的和被损害的”孩子去了。
At this time, Professor Kölhuitsch's printmaking collection was on the way from Europe to China, but when we arrived in Shanghai, the diligent introducers had already slept in the soil, and we didn't even know the location. Okay, I'll come and see it alone. This is poverty, disease, hunger, death...... Naturally, there are struggles and struggles, but there are few; This is like the author's self-portrait, although there is hatred and anger on his face, but more of love and compassion. This is an image of the heart of all "insulted and damaged" mothers. This kind of mother is also common in the countryside of China, where her nails are not yet dyed, but people often laugh at her, saying that mothers only love their useless sons. But I think she also loves her son, just because she is strong and capable, she lets go and pays attention to the "insulted and damaged" children.现在就有她的作品的复印二十一幅，来作证明；并且对于中国的青年艺术学徒，又有这样的益处的——
Now there are twenty-one copies of her works to prove it; And for China's young art apprentices, there is such a benefit -一，近五年来，木刻已颇流行了，虽然时时受着迫害。但别的版画，较成片段的，却只有一本关于卓伦（Anders Zorn）的书。现在所绍介的全是铜刻和石刻，使读者知道版画之中，又有这样的作品，也可以比油画之类更加普遍，而且看见和卓伦截然不同的技法和内容。
First, in the past five years, woodcuts have become quite popular, although they are often persecuted. But the other prints, which are more fragmentary, are only a book about Anders Zorn. Now all the bronze carvings and stone carvings are introduced, so that readers know that there are such works in printmaking, which can also be more common than oil paintings, and see completely different techniques and content from Zhuo Lun.二，没有到过外国的人，往往以为白种人都是对人来讲耶稣道理或开洋行的，鲜衣美食，一不高兴就用皮鞋向人乱踢。有了这画集，就明白世界上其实许多地方都还存在着“被侮辱和被损害的”人，是和我们一气的朋友，而且还有为这些人们悲哀，叫喊和战斗的艺术家。
Second, people who have never been to foreign countries often think that Caucasians are all people who preach the doctrine of Jesus to people or open foreign businesses, wear fresh clothes and eat delicious food, and kick people with leather shoes when they are unhappy. With this collection of paintings, I understand that in many parts of the world, there are still people who are "insulted and damaged", friends who are in the same breath as us, and there are artists who mourn, shout and fight for these people.三，现在中国的报纸上多喜欢登载张口大叫着的希特拉像，当时是暂时的，照相上却永久是这姿势，多看就令人觉得疲劳。现在由德国艺术家的画集，却看见了别一种人，虽然并非英雄，却可以亲近，同情，而且愈看，也愈觉得美，愈觉得有动人之力。
Third, Chinese newspapers now like to publish the portrait of Hitler with his mouth open, which was temporary at the time, but this pose is permanent in the photo, and it makes people feel tired when they look at it too much. Now the collection of paintings by German artists has seen another kind of person, although not a hero, but can be close and sympathetic, and the more I look at it, the more beautiful and moving I feel.四，今年是柔石被害后的满五年，也是作者的木刻第一次在中国出现后的第五年；而作者，用中国式计算起来，她是七十岁了，这也可以算作一个纪念。作者虽然现在也只能守着沉默，但她的作品，却更多的在远东的天下出现了。是的，为人类的艺术，别的力量是阻挡不住的。
Fourth, this year is the fifth year since Rou Shi was killed, and it is also the fifth year since the author's woodcuts first appeared in China; And the author, in Chinese calculations, is seventy years old, which can also be regarded as a commemoration. Although the author can only remain silent now, her works have appeared more in the world of the Far East. Yes, for human art, no other force can stop it.

二　略论暗暗的死

写于深夜里

2. Briefly discuss the death of darkness这几天才悟到，暗暗的死，在一个人是极其惨苦的事。
In the past few days, I realized that dying secretly is an extremely miserable thing for a person.中国在革命以前，死囚临刑，先在大街上通过，于是他或呼冤，或骂官，或自述英雄行为，或说不怕死。到壮美时，随着观看的人们，便喝一声采，后来还传述开去。在我年青的时候，常听到这种事，我总以为这情形是野蛮的，这办法是残酷的。
Before the revolution in China, death row inmates were first passed on the street when they were executed, so he either cried out for injustice, or scolded officials, or recounted his heroic deeds, or said that he was not afraid of death. When it was magnificent, the people watching cheered, and later it was recounted. When I was young, I often heard this kind of thing, and I always thought that this situation was barbaric, that this method was cruel.新近在林语堂博士编辑的《宇宙风》里，看到一篇铢堂先生的文章，却是别一种见解。他认为这种对死囚喝采，是崇拜失败的英雄，是扶弱，“理想是不能不算崇高。然而在人群的组织上实在要不得。抑强扶弱，便是永远不愿意有强。崇拜失败英雄，便是不承认成功的英雄。”所以使“凡是古来成功的帝王，欲维持几百年的威力，不定得残害几万几十万无辜的人，方才能博得一时的慑服”。
Recently, in "Cosmic Wind" edited by Dr. Lin Yutang, I saw an article by Mr. Zhutang, but it was a different opinion. He believes that this kind of applause for death row inmates is to worship failed heroes and to help the weak, "The ideal cannot be considered noble." However, it is really not necessary in the organization of the crowd. To suppress the strong and support the weak is to never be willing to be strong. To worship failed heroes is to not recognize successful heroes. Therefore, "all successful emperors in ancient times who want to maintain their power for hundreds of years may have to mutilate tens of thousands of innocent people in order to win temporary fear."残害了几万几十万人，还只“能博得一时的慑服”，为“成功的帝王”设想，实在是大可悲哀的：没有好法子。不过我并不想替他们划策，我所由此悟到的，乃是给死囚在临刑前可以当众说话，倒是“成功的帝王”的恩惠，也是他自信还有力量的证据，所以他有胆放死囚开口，给他在临死之前，得到一个自夸的陶醉，大家也明白他的收场。我先前只以为“残酷”，还不是确切的判断，其中是含有一点恩惠的。我每当朋友或学生的死，倘不知时日，不知地点，不知死法，总比知道的更悲哀和不安；由此推想那一边，在暗室中毕命于几个屠夫的手里，也一定比当众而死的更寂寞。
It is really sad to think of a "successful emperor" who has mutilated tens of thousands of people and can only "win a momentary intimidation": there is no good way. But I don't want to advise them, what I realized from this is to give death row inmates the ability to speak in public before execution, but it is the favor of the "successful emperor", and it is also evidence of his confidence and strength, so he has the courage to let the death row prisoner speak, give him a boastful intoxication before he dies, and everyone understands his ending. I only thought it was "cruel" before, not an exact judgment, and it contained a little favor. Whenever I die of a friend or student, if I don't know the time, place, or way of death, I am always sadder and more uneasy than I know; From this, it can be inferred that on the other side, dying in the hands of a few butchers in a dark room must be more lonely than dying in public.然而“成功的帝王”是不秘密杀人的，他只秘密一件事：和他那些妻妾的调笑。到得就要失败了，才又增加一件秘密：他的财产的数目和安放的处所；再下去，这才加到第三件：秘密的杀人。这时他也如铢堂先生一样，觉得民众自有好恶，不论成败的可怕了。
However, the "successful emperor" does not kill secretly, he only keeps one thing secret: teasing with his wives and concubines. When he was about to fail, he added another secret: the number of his property and the place where he was placed; Going further, this is added to the third thing: secret killing. At this time, like Mr. Zhutang, he felt that the people had their own likes and dislikes, no matter whether they succeeded or failed.所以第三种秘密法，是即使没有策士的献议，也总有一时要采用的，也许有些地方还已经采用。这时街道文明了，民众安静了，但我们试一推测死者的心，却一定比明明白白而死的更加惨苦。我先前读但丁的《神曲》，到《地狱》篇，就惊异于这作者设想的残酷，但到现在，阅历加多，才知道他还是仁厚的了：他还没有想出一个现在已极平常的惨苦到谁也看不见的地狱来。
Therefore, the third secret method is always to be adopted at some point even without the advice of the strategist, and perhaps it has been adopted in some places. At this time, the streets were civilized and the people were quiet, but if we tried to guess the heart of the deceased, it must be more miserable than the one who died clearly. I had read Dante's "Divine Comedy" before, and when I read "Hell", I was amazed at the cruelty that the author envisioned, but now, with more experience, I realize that he is still benevolent: he has not yet come up with a hell that is now so common that no one can see it.

There are many dictionaries published, and there is more than one, but they are not practical, and if you want to understand the truth, you must check the dictionary that has never been printed. There are very novel explanations here, for example: "liberation" means "shooting"; "Tolstoyism" means "fleeing"; The word "official" is annotated: "relatives, friends and servants of high officials"; The word "city" is annotated: "A tall and strong brick wall built to prevent students from entering and leaving"; The "moral" article states: "Women are not allowed to show their arms"; The "revolution" article notes: "Amplify the water into the fields and use airplanes to carry bombs on the heads of 'bandits'." ”出版有大部的法律，是派遣学者，往各国采访了现行律，摘取精华，编纂而成的，所以没有一国，能有这部法律的完全和精密。但卷头有一页白纸，只有见过没有印出的字典的人，才能够看出字来，首先计三条：一，或从宽办理；二，或从严办理；三，或有时全不适用之。
Most of the laws published were compiled by scholars who went to various countries to interview the current laws, extract the essence, and compile them, so no country could have the perfection and precision of this law. But there is a page of white paper at the beginning of the book, and only those who have seen the dictionary that has not been printed can see the words, first of all, there are three points: first, or leniency; 2. Or handle it strictly; 3. Sometimes it does not apply at all.自然有法院，但曾在白纸上看出字来的犯人，在开庭时候是决不抗辩的，因为坏人才爱抗辩，一辩即不免“从严办理”；自然也有高等法院，但曾在白纸上看出字来的人，是决不上诉的，因为坏人才爱上诉，一上诉即不免“从严办理”。

5. A true letter“敬爱的先生：
"Dear Sir:你问我出了拘留所以后的事情么，我现在大略叙述在下面——

On the last day of the last month of that year, the three of us were taken to the High Court by the ×× provincial government. As soon as they arrived, the prosecutor's office was held. The prosecutor's interrogation was very special, and he only asked three questions:‘你叫什么名字？’——第一句；
'What's your name?' '—the first sentence;‘今年你几岁？’——第二句；
'How old are you this year?' '—the second sentence;‘你是那里人？’——第三句。
'Are you from there?' '—the third sentence.开完了这样特别的庭，我们又被法院解到了军人监狱。有谁要看统治者的统治艺术的全般的么？那只要到军人监狱里去。他的虐杀异己，屠戮人民，不惨酷是不快意的。时局一紧张，就拉出一批所谓重要的政治犯来枪毙，无所谓刑期不刑期的。例如南昌陷于危急的时候，曾在三刻钟之内，打死了二十二个；福建人民政府成立时，也枪毙了不少。刑场就是狱里的五亩大的菜园，囚犯的尸体，就靠泥埋在菜园里，上面栽起菜来，当作肥料用。

The engravings are all images of Red Army officers and working starving people, in order to incite class struggle and show that the proletariat will have a dictatorship. ……’之后，没有多久，就开审判庭。庭上一字儿坐着老爷五位，威严得很。然而我倒并不怎样的手足无措，因为这时我的脑子里浮出了一幅图画，那是陀密埃（Honoré Daumier）的《法官》，真使我赞叹！

On the eighth day after the trial court opened, the final judgment was held and the verdict was pronounced.
